### 08.2 Compensation and CTC structures

The compensation model is where the two-wage-base problem originates, so it is P0 and
must be right before any statutory computation is meaningful.

**FR-PAY-101 · CTC structure builder** · **P0**
The engine shall let an admin define one or more **salary structures** as an ordered
set of **pay components**, each with a type (earning / deduction / reimbursement /
statutory / employer-cost), a calculation basis (fixed / percentage-of-basic /
percentage-of-CTC / slab / formula / balance-figure), a taxability treatment, and
per-component flags for PF-wage inclusion, ESI-wage inclusion, gratuity-wage inclusion,
bonus-wage inclusion, and payment-of-wages inclusion.
- *Detail.* A structure is a template; an employee is assigned a structure with
  component values (or the structure computes them from CTC). The "special allowance"
  as a **balance figure** (CTC minus the sum of all other annual components) is a
  required component type — it is how virtually every Indian offer letter closes CTC.
  The **five wage-base flags** (not one taxability flag) are what make I1 executable —
  the same "conveyance" component is excluded from PF but included in ESI gross and
  payment-of-wages.
- **AC-101.1** — Creating a component with `pf_wage=true, esi_wage=false` and another
  with `pf_wage=false, esi_wage=true` yields two different bases for the same employee,
  verifiable on the payslip breakdown.
- **AC-101.2** — A structure whose components do not sum to CTC is rejected with the
  exact rupee gap named, unless a balance-figure component is present to absorb it.
- **AC-101.3** — Assigning a structure to an employee with a stated annual CTC produces
  monthly component values whose 12× sum equals CTC to the rupee (rounding rule
  configurable; default: round each monthly component, reconcile the residue into the
  balance-figure component in the final month — see FR-PAY-104).
- **AC-101.4** — A component with **no wage-base flags set at all** is a blocking
  validation error (FR-PAY-1004), because a silently un-flagged component would drop out
  of every statutory base and file a wrong return.

**FR-PAY-102 · Employer-cost components inside CTC** · **P0**
The engine shall model **employer statutory contributions and other employer costs
(employer EPF, EPS, EDLI, EPF/EDLI admin charges, employer ESI, gratuity accrual,
employer LWF, statutory-bonus accrual, group-insurance premia) as CTC components** that
appear in the CTC build but **not** in gross earnings and **not** in net pay.
- *Detail.* Indian CTC is cost-to-company, so employer PF (₹1,800 typical), the ₹1,250
  EPS cap allocation, EDLI, admin charges and gratuity accrual are all part of the
  ₹X CTC the employee was quoted, but none of them are paid to the employee. The engine
  must present CTC, gross, and net as three distinct totals that reconcile.
- **AC-102.1** — For an employee on ₹15,000 PF wages contributing on the ceiling, the
  CTC view shows employer EPF ₹550, EPS ₹1,250, EDLI ₹75, EPF admin ₹75 as employer
  cost (per §06.2 worked example; Source: EPS 1995 para 3, EDLI 1976 para 8, on the
  ₹15,000 ceiling), none of which appear in gross or net.
- **AC-102.2** — `CTC = gross earnings (annual) + total employer statutory cost + other
  employer cost` holds to the rupee for every employee.

**FR-PAY-103 · Effective-dated compensation revisions** · **P0**
The engine shall store every compensation change (increment, promotion, structure
change) as an **effective-dated revision**, never an overwrite, and shall support a
revision **effective in a past period** (the trigger for arrears — FR-PAY-401).
- **AC-103.1** — A ₹60,000→₹70,000 monthly revision effective 1 April, entered in July,
  is stored with effective date 1 April and flags April–June as requiring arrears.
- **AC-103.2** — Querying an employee's compensation "as of" any historical date returns
  the value in force on that date, not the current value (supports I3, retro recompute).

**FR-PAY-104 · Proration** · **P0**
The engine shall prorate earnings for **partial-period employment** (mid-period join,
exit, unpaid leave, mid-period structure change) on a configurable basis: **calendar
days**, **fixed 30-day**, or **actual working days**.
- *Detail.* The proration basis is a tenant/state policy, not a global constant —
  calendar-day and 30-day methods give different results and both are lawful; the
  payment-of-wages register must reflect the method used. LOP (loss of pay) days from
  attendance/leave (§09) reduce the paid-day count. Note the interaction
  with the ESI coverage test: a mid-month join that prorates gross **below** ₹21,000 for
  the join month does **not** by itself pull an otherwise-out employee into ESI — the
  coverage test reads the full-month wage, not the prorated figure (§06.3).
- **AC-104.1** — An employee joining on the 16th of a 30-day month on ₹60,000/month, on
  calendar-day basis, earns ₹60,000 × 15/30 = ₹30,000 gross for the month (worked in
  full at §08.12, Example B), and PF/ESI/PT are computed on the **prorated** base per
  §06, not the full base.
- **AC-104.2** — Changing the proration basis for a tenant does not retroactively alter
  already-finalised pay runs; it applies from the next open period (effective-dated).

**FR-PAY-105 · Multi-currency / multi-establishment awareness** · **P2**
The engine shall support employees assigned to different **establishments** (PF/ESI
codes, PT/LWF states) within one tenant, computing each employee's statutory
obligations against **their establishment's** registrations and **their work state's**
PT/LWF rules.
- *Detail.* Deferred to P2 (§05.5 item 22) because the single-site beachhead does not
  need it — but the data model must carry `establishment_id` and `work_state` on every
  employee-period from v1 so the P2 build is additive, not a migration.
- **AC-105.1** — [P2] Two employees in the same tenant, one in Karnataka and one in
  Maharashtra, receive PT computed on Karnataka and Maharashtra slabs respectively in
  the same pay run.

**FR-PAY-106 · Perquisite valuation** · **P1**
The engine shall value **taxable perquisites** per the Income-tax Rule 3 method for each
applicable head and feed the taxable value into the TDS base (FR-PAY-205), storing the
valuation basis so it is auditable and effective-dated.
- *Detail.* The common heads and their statutory valuation (Source: Income-tax Act
  s.17(2), Rule 3): **rent-free / concessional accommodation** — the CBDT
  Notification 65/2023 revised city-population slabs (10%/7.5%/5% of salary, eff FY2023-24,
  replacing the old 15%/10%/7.5%); **motor car** — ₹1,800/₹2,400 per month (≤1.6L /
  >1.6L cc) + ₹900 driver where the employer provides it; **interest-free/concessional
  loan** — SBI benchmark rate on the maximum monthly outstanding, exempt if the aggregate
  is ≤ ₹20,000 or for a medical loan; **ESOP** — perquisite = FMV on exercise date minus
  exercise price, with the eligible-startup **s.192(1C) deferral** of TDS (up to 5 years /
  sale / cessation, whichever earliest; Source: Finance Act 2020, s.192(1C)); **meal and
  gift vouchers** at the 01.04.2026 thresholds (₹200/meal, ₹15,000/yr gift; §06.5/§11).
  Perquisite valuation is **rules-first** (I4) — no perquisite value is model-generated.
- **AC-106.1** — A ₹5,00,000 interest-free loan outstanding for a full year is valued at
  the SBI benchmark rate on the maximum monthly outstanding and added to the TDS base; a
  ₹15,000 aggregate loan is exempt (below the ₹20,000 floor) and adds nothing.
- **AC-106.2** — An eligible-startup ESOP perquisite defers TDS under s.192(1C); the
  engine tracks the deferral clock and triggers the deduction on the earliest of the three
  events, not on exercise.
- **AC-106.3** — Rent-free accommodation is valued on the **effective-dated** Rule 3 slab
  in force for the period (post-Notification 65/2023 slabs for FY2023-24 onward), so a
  retro recompute (I3) uses the period's slab, not today's.

**FR-PAY-107 · Worker classification and the contractor scope boundary** · **P0**
The engine shall carry a **worker class** on every payee — *employee* (s.192 salary,
PF/ESI/PT/gratuity apply), *contractor/professional* (s.194C/194J, **no** salary
statutory heads), or *gig/platform worker* — and route each to the correct TDS section
and statutory obligation set, refusing to silently treat a contractor as an employee or
vice versa.
- *Detail.* Misclassification is the most common source of a wrong return: a consultant
  paid via payroll and put through s.192 + PF is a filed error, and an employee paid as a
  "contractor" to dodge PF is a liability the engine should flag, not enable. Contractor
  payments are **out of the salary engine's statutory scope** but in scope for TDS routing
  (194C 1%/2%, 194J 10%; Source: Income-tax Act ss.194C, 194J). The **Code on Social
  Security 2020 (ss.114–115)** creates gig/platform-worker social-security obligations
  funded by an aggregator cess (1–2% of turnover, capped at 5% of amounts paid to workers)
  — **[Hypothesis]** the operative scheme, rate and collection mechanism are not yet
  notified. **Kill/validation criterion: build the `gig` worker class and a placeholder
  cess hook, but leave the cess rate/scheme `blocked-pending-notification` and escalated
  until the aggregator-cess scheme is gazetted; do not compute a guessed cess (§06.13,
  §20 Q8 pattern).**
- **AC-107.1** — A payee flagged *contractor* is deducted TDS under s.194C/194J (not 192),
  carries **no** PF/ESI/PT/gratuity, and appears on the 26Q pipeline (out of scope here),
  never on ECR/ESI.
- **AC-107.2** — An *employee* flagged with a contractor-style component set (no wage-base
  flags, no PF) trips the FR-PAY-1004 validation gate rather than filing a zero-PF ECR.

---

### 08.3 Statutory computation engine

This group **orchestrates** the deterministic rules specified in §06. It does not
re-specify rates; it specifies how the engine applies them, in what order, with what
edge-case handling. All rate/slab references point to §06, and the golden cases are
§06.14 TV1–TV12.



**Figure 47. Wage Base Fanout**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    SRC["One employee-period<br/>pay components<br/>(FR-PAY-101)"]
    FLAGS{{"Each component carries FIVE<br/>wage-base flags, not one:<br/>pf · esi · gratuity · bonus · pow<br/>(I1 — a single 'wage' field is a design error)"}}
    GATE["No flag set at all =<br/>blocking error (FR-PAY-1004):<br/>a silent component files a wrong return"]

    SRC --> FLAGS
    FLAGS -. "AC-101.4" .-> GATE

    FLAGS --> B1
    FLAGS --> B2
    FLAGS --> B3
    FLAGS --> B4
    FLAGS --> B5

    subgraph RES["FR-PAY-201 · five separately-stored bases per employee-period"]
        direction TB
        B1["PF / gratuity base<br/>excl. HRA / conveyance / OT<br/>50% add-back if excluded &gt;50% (§06.10)<br/>then ₹15,000 ceiling"]
        B2["ESI gross base<br/>INCLUDES HRA / conveyance / OT<br/>OT out of ₹21,000 coverage test,<br/>in the base once covered (TV5)"]
        B3["Gratuity wage base<br/>last-drawn Basic + DA<br/>(15/26 × wages × years)<br/>running accrual ledger"]
        B4["Bonus wage base<br/>capped at ₹7,000 OR min wage,<br/>whichever higher (§06.7)<br/>eligibility ≤ ₹21,000/mo"]
        B5["Payment-of-wages base<br/>all earnings, gross view<br/>deductions ≤ Code on Wages cap"]
    end

    B1 --> F1["EPF ECR + challan<br/>EPS ≤ ₹1,250, EDLI (FR-PAY-701)"]
    B2 --> F2["ESI contribution<br/>0.75% / 3.25%, held to<br/>Apr-Sep / Oct-Mar boundary (FR-PAY-702)"]
    B3 --> F3["Gratuity payout on exit<br/>+ AS 15 / Ind AS 19 ledger (FR-PAY-206)"]
    B4 --> F4["Bonus Form C / D by 30 Nov<br/>(FR-PAY-705)"]
    B5 --> F5["Wage register + payslip<br/>(FR-PAY-601 / 709)"]

    NOTE["Same rupee routes differently per return:<br/>statutory bonus is INVISIBLE to ECR/ESI<br/>but VISIBLE to Form 138 (§06.12 R12)"]
    B4 -. "routing, not amount" .-> NOTE

    STAMP["Every base independently auditable,<br/>stamped with the wage-definition<br/>rule version used (AC-201.3, I2/I5)"]
    RES -. logs .-> STAMP
```



**FR-PAY-201 · Dual/triple wage-base resolver** · **P0**
For every employee-period the engine shall compute, as separate stored figures: the
**PF wage base** (with the 50% add-back applied per §06.10), the **ESI gross base**, the
**gratuity wage base**, the **bonus wage base**, and the **payment-of-wages base**.
- *Detail.* This is I1 made executable. The add-back logic (Source: Code on Wages
  s.2(y) / CoSS s.2(88)): sum excluded components; if they exceed 50% of total
  remuneration, add the excess back into the PF/gratuity base (worked at §06.10 and
  §08.12 Example D; golden cases §06.14 TV6/TV7).
- **AC-201.1** — For the §06.10 illustration (remuneration ₹1,00,000, excluded
  components 65%), the engine adds back ₹15,000 and reports a PF wage base of ₹50,000
  **before** the ₹15,000 statutory ceiling is applied — both figures visible (TV6).
- **AC-201.2** — For excluded components at 45% (below the half), **no** add-back is
  applied and the PF base is Basic alone (TV7) — the engine does not add back
  unnecessarily.
- **AC-201.3** — All bases are independently auditable and each is stamped with the
  wage-definition rule version used.

**FR-PAY-202 · EPF computation** · **P0**
The engine shall compute employee EPF, the **three-way employer split (EPS capped at
₹1,250, balance to EPF), EDLI, EPF admin and EDLI admin** exactly per §06.2, honouring
per-employee **ceiling-vs-actual** election, the **excluded-employee** flag, and the
**EPS-closure rule** for high-earner first-joiners.
- *Detail.* The classic bug §06.2 warns of — applying 8.33% to actual wages above the
  ceiling instead of capping EPS at ₹1,250 — is an explicit negative test (TV1).
  (Source: EPS 1995 para 3, 8.33% on ceiling ₹15,000 = ₹1,250.)
- **AC-202.1** — For an employee on actual PF wages ₹30,000 with employer opting for
  ceiling contribution: employee EPF and employer split both computed on ₹15,000; EPS =
  ₹1,250 (not 8.33% of ₹30,000 = ₹2,499), employer EPF = ₹550. This exact case is a
  regression test (TV1).
- **AC-202.2** — For an employee opting actual-wage contribution on ₹30,000: employee
  EPF = ₹3,600, EPS still capped at ₹1,250, employer EPF = ₹3,600 − ₹1,250 = ₹2,350.
- **AC-202.3** — An "excluded employee" (joined above ₹15,000, never a prior member) is
  computed with zero EPF unless voluntarily enrolled; the exclusion basis is recorded.
- **AC-202.4** — An employee who **first joined EPF on or after 01.09.2014 with PF wages
  above ₹15,000** is closed to EPS: the full 12% employer share goes to EPF and EPS = 0
  (TV2; Source: EPS 1995 amendment, GSR 609(E) dated 22.08.2014). Splitting EPS for such
  a member is a filed error.
- **AC-202.5** — Admin charges are computed on the correct minimum-per-establishment
  floor where applicable, not a bare percentage, and the EPF/EDLI admin rate is an
  effective-dated rule version (I2), so a re-notified admin rate is a config change.

**FR-PAY-203 · ESI computation with contribution-period state machine** · **P0**
The engine shall compute ESI at the §06.3 rates (employee 0.75%, employer 3.25%; Source:
ESI (Central) Rules, Rule 51) on the gross base, apply per-employee **rupee rounding**,
handle the **low-wage employer-only** case, and **hold an employee in ESI to the
contribution-period boundary** (Apr–Sep / Oct–Mar) after their gross crosses ₹21,000
mid-period.
- *Detail.* This is the ESI trap from §06.3: an employee crossing ₹21,000 in, say, July
  continues to contribute through September, then exits from October. Dropping them in
  July files a wrong return (TV3). Overtime is **excluded from the ₹21,000 coverage
  test** but **included in the contribution base** once covered (TV5) — a subtle routing
  the wage-base resolver (FR-PAY-201) must encode.
- **AC-203.1** — An employee at ₹20,000 in June who is revised to ₹22,000 effective July
  continues ESI (on ₹22,000 gross) for July, August, September; ESI stops from October
  (TV3).
- **AC-203.2** — Contributions are rounded up to the next rupee per employee, per side,
  and the rounding is reproducible.
- **AC-203.3** — An employee whose **average daily wage is ≤ ₹176** has the **employee
  0.75% share waived** while the **employer 3.25% share is still charged** (TV4; Source:
  ESI (Central) Rules, Rule 52). Charging both or waiving both is a filed error.
- **[Hypothesis / blocked]** — **AC-203.4** — ESI computation for periods **after the
  ~21 Nov 2026 one-year saving expires** depends on the unresolved successor instrument
  (§06.9, §06.13, §20 Q8). **Kill/gate criterion: if no successor is notified before the
  cliff, ESI for post-cliff periods is escalated and blocked, never guessed** — the
  filing calendar renders it `blocked-pending-regime` (FR-PAY-709).

**FR-PAY-204 · Professional Tax computation (per-state, effective-dated)** · **P0**
The engine shall deduct PT per the employee's **work-state** slab from the maintained
per-state PT table (§06.4), respecting gender variants, the **Article 276 ₹2,500/year
cap** (Source: Constitution of India, Art. 276(2)), and state-specific quirks (e.g.,
Maharashtra's ₹300 February deduction; Source: Maharashtra State Tax on Professions Act
1975).
- *Detail.* PT follows place of employment, not residence — critical for remote/
  multi-state. Only Telangana is fully verified (§06.4; §06.13 open item). The all-states
  PT table is a maintained-dataset build dependency, so v1 ships the states where the
  first tenants operate (§05.5 item 5); all-states is P2.
- **AC-204.1** — A Maharashtra employee above the male exemption threshold is deducted
  ₹200/month Apr–Jan and ₹300 in February, totalling exactly ₹2,500 for the year (TV10).
- **AC-204.2** — An employee in a no-PT state (e.g., Delhi, Haryana, UP) has zero PT and
  no PT return is generated for that establishment.
- **AC-204.3** — Cumulative PT for any employee never exceeds ₹2,500 in a financial year
  even across multiple structures or mid-year revisions (Art. 276 cap enforced as a
  running annual ceiling, not a per-month rule).
- **[Hypothesis]** — **AC-204.4** — For a **fully-remote employee with no fixed work
  situs**, the engine applies the tenant's configured fallback (deduct at the
  registered-establishment state). **Kill criterion: replace the fallback with the
  verified state position once obtained (§06.13 open item); until then the conservative
  deduct-at-registered-state policy is flagged, not silently trusted.**

**FR-PAY-205 · TDS u/s 192, dual-regime** · **P0**
The engine shall compute monthly TDS by projecting annual tax under **both the new
default regime (s.115BAC) and the old regime**, honour the employee's **election** (and
new-regime default if silent), spread the liability across remaining months, and
**true-up** on every declaration, revision or perquisite change.
- *Detail.* Per §06.5: new-regime slabs and ₹75,000 standard deduction (Source: Finance
  Act 2024, s.115BAC(1A)) vs old-regime Chapter VI-A; s.87A rebate (FY2025-26: nil tax up
  to ₹12,00,000 taxable under the new regime; Source: Finance Act 2025 amendment to
  s.87A); s.206AA inoperative-PAN higher-rate deduction; previous-employer income via
  Form 12B for mid-year joiners; NPS employer contribution under s.80CCD(2) — **10% of
  Basic+DA in the old regime, 14% in the new regime** (raised by Finance Act 2024 eff
  FY2024-25; Source: Income-tax Act s.80CCD(2), proviso). Surcharge and health-&-education
  cess (4%) sit on the projected liability; **surcharge marginal relief** applies at the
  ₹50L / ₹1Cr / ₹2Cr / ₹5Cr thresholds (the new regime caps surcharge at 25%, the old at
  37%; Source: Finance Act 2024, First Schedule Part III). Three edge mechanics the engine
  must own, not the employee: **s.192(2B)** other-income and other-TDS declaration (may
  *increase* salary TDS but a declared loss under "income from house property" is the only
  head that may *reduce* it — no other loss can); **s.192(1A)** where the employer *bears*
  the tax on a non-monetary perquisite instead of deducting it from the employee; and
  **s.89(1) relief via Form 10E** when arrears or advance salary bunch income into one
  year (Source: Income-tax Act s.89, Rule 21A).
- **AC-205.1** — For a given gross and declaration set, the engine reports the tax under
  **both** regimes and the monthly TDS under the elected one; switching the election
  re-projects the remaining months without altering already-deducted amounts (worked at
  §08.12 Example F).
- **AC-205.2** — A mid-year salary revision (FR-PAY-103) re-projects annual tax and
  redistributes the delta across remaining months (no lump-sum in the revision month
  unless remaining months = 1).
- **AC-205.3** — An employee with an **inoperative PAN** is deducted at the higher of the
  applicable rate or 20% under **s.206AA**; **s.206AB (non-filer higher rate) does not
  apply to salary** (TV11; Source: Income-tax Act ss.206AA, 206AB(2)). Applying 206AB to
  salary is a filed error; the reason is flagged pre-run (FR-PAY-1004).
- **AC-205.4** — Perquisite values (meal ₹200/meal, gift/voucher ₹15,000/yr thresholds
  effective 01.04.2026, §06.5/§11; Source: CBDT notification eff. 01.04.2026) feed the
  TDS base at their taxable portion.
- **AC-205.5** — A mid-year joiner's **previous-employer income and TDS** (Form 12B) are
  added to the projection so the annual liability is not under-deducted; if the employee
  declines to declare, the engine projects on current-employer income only and records
  the election.
- **[Hypothesis]** — **AC-205.6** — The **FY2026-27 slabs, rebate and surcharge
  parameters** are loaded as an effective-dated rule version. **Kill criterion: re-verify
  the FY2026-27 s.115BAC slabs and s.87A rebate against the Finance Act 2026 notification
  (and any corrigendum) before the first FY2026-27 run — FY2025-26 is verified, the
  current year is pending (§06.13).**
- **AC-205.7** — When a run pays **arrears/advance salary** that bunches income into the
  year, the engine computes the **s.89(1) relief** figure and generates a
  **Form 10E**-ready worksheet (per-year re-spread of the arrears to the years they relate
  to), so the employee's TDS reflects the relief where they elect it. The relief is
  computed deterministically, never estimated by the assistant (Source: Rule 21A). Example
  C's ₹30,000 arrears is the trigger case.
- **AC-205.8** — An employee's **s.192(2B) declaration** of other income raises the TDS
  base; a declared **house-property loss** (e.g., self-occupied home-loan interest up to
  ₹2,00,000, old regime only) reduces it; **any other head's loss is ignored** for salary
  TDS. Declaring a business loss to cut salary TDS is rejected with the reason shown
  (Source: Income-tax Act s.192(2B), proviso).
- **AC-205.9** — For a **non-monetary perquisite on which the employer elects to bear the
  tax (s.192(1A))**, the borne tax is **not grossed into the employee's income** and is
  **not deductible** as the employee's TDS; it is recorded as an employer cost
  (FR-PAY-102) and reported correctly on Form 138/Form 130 (Source: Income-tax Act
  s.192(1A), s.40(a)(v) treatment).

**FR-PAY-206 · Gratuity accrual and payout** · **P0**
The engine shall maintain a **running gratuity accrual ledger** per eligible employee
(from the 10-employee latch, §06.1/§06.6) and compute the **payout** on exit using
`(15/26) × last-drawn wages × completed years`, the 6-month rounding, the 5-year
qualifying rule (waived on death/disablement), and the ₹20,00,000 exemption ceiling.
(Source: Payment of Gratuity Act 1972, ss.4, 4(2), 4(3); exemption s.10(10) Income-tax
Act / CBDT notification raising the ceiling to ₹20 lakh.)
- **AC-206.1** — For last-drawn Basic+DA ₹52,000 and 7 years 8 months service, payout =
  (15/26) × 52,000 × 8 = **₹2,40,000**, tax-free (§06.6 worked example reproduced as a
  test).
- **AC-206.2** — 6-month rounding runs **both directions** (TV8): 7y 8m → 8 completed
  years; 7y 4m → 7 completed years. Rounding the two the same direction is a defect.
- **AC-206.3** — An employee dying at 3 years' service receives gratuity (5-year rule
  waived); an employee resigning at 4 years 5 months does not qualify.
- **AC-206.4** — The accrual ledger value is queryable as-of any date for the books
  (AS 15 / Ind AS 19), independent of whether payout has occurred.

**FR-PAY-207 · LWF deduction** · **P0**
The engine shall deduct employee LWF and accrue employer LWF per the maintained
per-state LWF table (§06.8), on that state's **periodicity** (monthly / half-yearly /
annual).
- *Detail.* LWF rupee values and periodicity vary by state and are **not** yet verified
  per state (§06.13 open item; Frappe corroborates ~14 LWF states as a count only).
- **AC-207.1** — A Maharashtra employee is deducted the notified employee share and the
  employer share is accrued in the **June and December** pay runs only, not monthly
  (Source: Maharashtra Labour Welfare Fund Act 1953, half-yearly cadence).
- **AC-207.2** — Employees in no-LWF states have zero LWF and no LWF remittance.
- **[Hypothesis]** — **AC-207.3** — The per-state LWF rupee values (e.g., Maharashtra
  ₹25 employee / ₹75 employer) are loaded from the maintained table. **Kill criterion:
  verify each state's rupee value and periodicity against that state's LWF Act before it
  drives a deduction (§06.13); an unverified value is flagged, not deducted silently.**

**FR-PAY-208 · Statutory bonus (Payment of Bonus Act)** · **P0**
The engine shall compute **statutory bonus** for eligible employees, accrue it monthly,
and pay it on the annual cadence, using the correct eligibility ceiling, calculation
ceiling, and minimum/maximum percentages.
- *Detail.* (Source: Payment of Bonus Act 1965 — eligibility s.2(13) wage ≤ ₹21,000/mo;
  calculation ceiling s.12 at ₹7,000 **or the minimum wage for the scheduled
  employment, whichever is higher**; s.10 minimum 8.33%; s.11 maximum 20%; payout within
  8 months of FY close, i.e., by **30 November**, with **Form C/D** filing.) The bonus
  wage base (I1) is the ₹7,000-or-min-wage-capped figure, **not** actual wages — TV9 is
  the golden case. A statutory bonus is **invisible to ECR/ESI** but **visible to Form
  138** (§06.12 R12) — the same rupee routes differently per return.
- **AC-208.1** — For an employee on ₹18,000/mo wages in a scheduled employment with
  minimum wage ₹10,000, the bonus base is **₹10,000** (not ₹18,000, not a flat ₹7,000)
  and bonus at the declared percentage is computed on ₹10,000 × 12 (TV9).
- **AC-208.2** — An employee on wages **above ₹21,000/mo** is **not eligible** for
  statutory bonus (s.2(13)); any ex-gratia paid instead is flagged as ex-gratia, taxed,
  and excluded from Form C/D.
- **AC-208.3** — Bonus accrues monthly to an employer-cost ledger (FR-PAY-102), the
  payout run computes TDS on the bonus at the marginal projected rate (FR-PAY-205), and
  the bonus is included in Form 138 but **not** in that month's ECR/ESI wage base.
- **[Hypothesis]** — **AC-208.4** — The ₹21,000/₹7,000 ceilings are the 1965-Act values.
  **Kill criterion: verify whether Code on Wages ss.26–41 notify different bonus ceilings
  before computing any post-cliff bonus (§06.13 open item); until confirmed, the engine
  uses the 1965-Act values flagged as pending re-verification.**

**FR-PAY-209 · Computation ordering and rounding policy** · **P0**
The engine shall apply statutory computations in a **defined, documented order**
(earnings → wage-base resolution → PF/ESI/PT/LWF/bonus-accrual → taxable income → TDS →
net), with a single tenant-level **rounding policy** applied consistently and
reproducibly.
- *Detail.* Order matters: PT and PF (old regime) are deductions that affect taxable
  income; TDS is computed after them. Rounding must be defined per statute and must not
  drift between runs. The rounding policy is a versioned rule (I2), not code.

| Head | Rounding rule | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ESI (each side, per employee) | Round **up** to the next rupee | ESI (Central) Rules |
| EPF (each head) | Round to the nearest rupee | EPFO ECR file spec |
| PT | Whole-rupee slab value, no rounding | State PT Acts |
| TDS | Round to the nearest rupee; annual liability rounded per Income-tax Act | Income-tax Act |
| Net pay | Round to the rupee; residue absorbed per FR-PAY-101 AC-101.3 | tenant policy |

- **AC-209.1** — Re-running an unchanged period reproduces byte-identical figures (I4).
- **AC-209.2** — The sum of employee-level rounded figures reconciles to the challan
  total the return expects (no penny-rounding gap that fails ECR/ESI validation).

---

### 08.4 Pay-run lifecycle

The pay run is the transactional heart of the engine. Its state machine is what makes
payroll auditable and reversible.



**Figure 48. Payrun State Machine**

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    direction TB
    [*] --> Draft
    state "Draft" as Draft
    state "Inputs Locked" as InputsLocked
    state "Computed" as Computed
    state "Review" as Review
    state "Approved" as Approved
    state "Paid" as Paid
    state "Filed" as Filed
    state "Closed" as Closed

    Draft --> InputsLocked: Lock and snapshot inputs (FR-PAY-302)
    InputsLocked --> Computed: Compute gross-to-net plus variance view (FR-PAY-303)
    Computed --> Review: Present breakdown, employer cost, outliers
    Review --> Approved: Maker-checker sign-off (FR-PAY-304)
    Approved --> Paid: Disburse salaries to bank
    Paid --> Filed: File and accept ECR / ESI / PT / TDS
    Filed --> Closed: Period locked

    note right of Approved
      Blocking validations (FR-PAY-1004)
      must be clear before Approved (AC-301.1).
      Approver must differ from computer (SoD).
    end note

    note right of Filed
      Filing, not payslip, is the unit of delivery.
      Paid is not Filed; Filed is not Closed.
    end note

    Review --> InputsLocked: Reopen to fix inputs
    Approved --> InputsLocked: Reopen (pre-payment)
    Paid --> Computed: Reopen with compensating reversal (FR-PAY-306)
    Filed --> Correction: No silent reopen after filing (AC-306.2)
    state "Correction / Revised Return" as Correction
    Correction --> Filed: File revised return (FR-PAY-707/708)

    Closed --> [*]
```


**FR-PAY-301 · Pay-run state machine** · **P0**
A pay run shall progress through explicit, logged states: **Draft → Inputs Locked →
Computed → Review → Approved → Paid → Filed → Closed**, with defined forward
transitions and a controlled **reopen** path.
- *Detail.* Each transition is an audit event (I5). "Filed" is distinct from "Paid" and
  from "Closed" because the filing is the unit of delivery — a run is not done when
  salaries hit bank accounts; it is done when ECR/ESI/PT/TDS are filed and accepted.
- **AC-301.1** — No pay run reaches "Approved" while any blocking validation
  (FR-PAY-1004) is unresolved.
- **AC-301.2** — Every state transition records actor, timestamp, and (for Approved/
  Paid/Filed) the authorising role.

**FR-PAY-302 · Input locking** · **P0**
On entering "Inputs Locked," the engine shall **snapshot** all inputs that feed the run
(attendance/LOP, variable pay, reimbursement claims, declaration changes, joins/exits,
compensation revisions) so later edits to source data do not silently alter a computed
run.
- **AC-302.1** — An attendance correction made after inputs are locked does not change
  the current run; it surfaces as an arrears/adjustment item for the next run
  (FR-PAY-401) or requires an explicit reopen.

**FR-PAY-303 · Compute and preview** · **P0**
On "Compute," the engine shall produce, for every employee, the full gross-to-net
breakdown, all statutory figures, employer costs, and a **variance view** against the
prior period (new joiners, exits, absolute and % change per employee, flagged outliers).
- **AC-303.1** — The variance view flags any employee whose net changed by more than a
  configurable threshold (default ±25%) with the driver (revision / LOP / arrears /
  declaration / one-time).
- **AC-303.2** — Run totals (gross, deductions, net, employer cost, each statutory head)
  are shown and reconcile to the sum of employee figures to the rupee.

**FR-PAY-304 · Maker-checker approval** · **P0**
The engine shall enforce **segregation of duties**: the actor who computes/edits a run
cannot be the sole approver; approval requires a distinct authorised role.
- **AC-304.1** — A single user cannot both edit figures and approve the same run unless
  explicitly granted a combined role with that combination logged as a policy exception.

**FR-PAY-305 · Off-cycle and supplementary runs** · **P0**
The engine shall support **off-cycle runs** (bonus, incentive, one-time payout,
correction) that are computed, taxed and filed correctly alongside the regular monthly
run, feeding the same statutory returns for the period.
- **AC-305.1** — A mid-month bonus off-cycle run computes TDS on the bonus at the
  marginal projected rate and its PF/ESI treatment per the component's wage-base flags.
- **AC-305.2** — Off-cycle PF/ESI contributions consolidate into the **same monthly
  ECR/ESI challan** as the regular run, not a duplicate filing.

**FR-PAY-306 · Reopen and reversal** · **P0**
The engine shall support **reopening** an Approved/Paid run and **reversing** a run,
producing a compensating entry with full audit lineage rather than deleting history.
- **AC-306.1** — Reversing a paid run creates an offsetting record; the original remains
  in history; net effect on the employee and on statutory totals is traceable.
- **AC-306.2** — A run that has been "Filed" cannot be silently reopened; reopening
  after filing forces the correction path (revised return, FR-PAY-707).

---

### 08.5 Arrears, retrospective recompute, and adjustments

This group is where I3 (retro against the period's rule version) becomes a feature. It
is one of the strongest differentiators against spreadsheet/Tally workflows.

**FR-PAY-401 · Arrears from effective-dated revisions** · **P0**
When a compensation revision is effective in a closed period (FR-PAY-103), the engine
shall compute **arrears** by recomputing each affected past period **against that
period's rule versions and inputs**, and pay the delta in the current run.
- *Detail.* This is not "difference × months." It is a full recompute per past period:
  the revised gross changes PF, ESI, PT and TDS for each of those months, computed with
  the slabs and ceilings that were in force then (I3; §06.14 TV12). Worked at §08.12
  Example C.
- **AC-401.1** — A ₹60,000→₹70,000 revision effective 1 April, processed in July,
  recomputes April, May, June each against April/May/June rules; the arrears line shows
  the per-head delta (gross, PF, ESI, PT, TDS) per month, summed.
- **AC-401.2** — Arrears PF is remitted correctly (PF on arrears is due; the ECR reflects
  the corrected wage months) and arrears TDS is trued-up in the current projection.
- **AC-401.3** — If a rule changed between the corrected period and today (e.g., a PT
  slab revision), the recompute uses the **old** slab for the old months (TV12).

**FR-PAY-402 · Retrospective statutory recompute** · **P1**
The engine shall support recomputing a closed period when a **rule** changes
retroactively (e.g., the 12% PF re-notified retrospective to 21.11.2025 by S.O.
3582(E), §06.9), producing the corrected figures and the delta to file. (Source: S.O.
3582(E), re-notification of EPF Scheme 2026 rate.)
- **AC-402.1** — Applying a retroactive rate change to a range of past periods produces,
  per period, the recomputed figures, the delta, and a filing-correction task
  (FR-PAY-707).

**FR-PAY-403 · Ad-hoc adjustments and recoveries** · **P0**
The engine shall support one-time **additions** (reimbursement top-ups, incentives) and
**deductions/recoveries** (salary advance recovery, notice-pay recovery, excess-payment
recovery, canteen/asset recovery) with their correct tax and wage-base treatment.
- *Detail.* Recoveries must respect the payment-of-wages deduction ceiling (total
  deductions capped at 50% of wages, higher in specified cases; Source: Code on Wages
  s.18) — a recovery that would breach the cap is flagged and spread.
- **AC-403.1** — A salary-advance recovery of ₹5,000/month reduces net by ₹5,000, does
  not reduce the PF/ESI/tax base (it is a post-tax recovery), and tracks the outstanding
  advance balance to zero.
- **AC-403.2** — A recovery that would push total deductions above the Code on Wages cap
  is blocked/spread with the ceiling shown, not silently applied.

---

### 08.6 Reimbursements and Flexible Benefits (FBP)

Per §11, the FBP data model is P1 (build the model, defer monetisation) but its tax
treatment touches TDS, so the computation hooks are P0.

**FR-PAY-501 · FBP declaration and wallet** · **P1**
The engine shall let employees allocate a **flexible benefit budget** across declared
heads (fuel/conveyance, LTA, telephone, books/periodicals, meal cards, NPS employer
contribution, etc.), within statutory tax-exemption limits, and shall reflect the
declaration in the TDS projection.
- *Detail.* The 01.04.2026 expansion — meal perquisite ₹50→₹200/meal, gift/voucher
  ₹5,000→₹15,000/yr, ~3.8× wallet expansion (§11, [Verified]; Source: CBDT notification
  eff. 01.04.2026) — is a config value in the exemption table, effective-dated, not a
  code change.
- **AC-501.1** — An employee declaring ₹2,400/month meal-card allocation has it treated
  as tax-exempt up to the ₹200/meal × working-days limit; the excess is taxable and
  flows to TDS.

**FR-PAY-502 · Reimbursement claim and proof-of-spend** · **P1**
The engine shall accept reimbursement **claims with proof (bill upload)**, run them
through an approval workflow, and pay approved claims through payroll or off-cycle, with
the **tax-exempt vs taxable split** determined by proof and limit.
- **AC-502.1** — A ₹30,000 LTA claim with valid travel proof, within the block-year
  exemption, is paid tax-exempt; without proof it is paid as a **taxable** allowance and
  TDS is adjusted.
- **AC-502.2** — Unclaimed FBP balances at year-end are paid out as **fully taxable**
  special allowance and the TDS is trued-up in the final run of the FY.

**FR-PAY-503 · Investment declaration and proof workflow** · **P0 (tax hook)**
The engine shall support the **declaration** (provisional, drives TDS from the start of
the year) and later **proof submission** (actuals, trues up TDS in the last quarter) for
old-regime Chapter VI-A and HRA claims.
- *Detail.* §04 notes this was mis-named as a P0 differentiator — against Zoho it is
  **table stakes**, present even in the free tier ([Killed] as a differentiator; Source:
  Zoho Payroll free-tier page, §04). It is built because it is required for correct TDS,
  not because it wins deals. Phase-tagged **P0 (tax hook)**: the FBP UI is P1 but the
  declaration→TDS computation path is P0.
- **AC-503.1** — A declared ₹1,50,000 80C reduces monthly TDS from April (old regime);
  if proof of only ₹1,00,000 is submitted by the proof deadline, the last-quarter TDS is
  increased to recover the shortfall.
- **AC-503.2** — HRA exemption is computed as the least of (actual HRA, rent − 10% of
  salary, 50%/40% of salary by metro/non-metro) and drives the old-regime TDS base.
  (Source: Income-tax Act s.10(13A), Rule 2A.)

### 08.7 Payslips

**FR-PAY-601 · Payslip generation** · **P0**
The engine shall generate a per-employee **payslip** for each finalised run, itemising
earnings, deductions, employer contributions (informational), net pay in figures and
words, paid/LOP days, and YTD figures, in a **prescribed-compliant wage-slip format**
(Labour Codes wage slip, §04/§06; Source: notified Central Rules under the Code on
Wages, wage-slip form).
- **AC-601.1** — The payslip reconciles: gross earnings − total deductions = net pay,
  to the rupee, matching the pay run.
- **AC-601.2** — The payslip shows the statutory identifiers required (UAN, PF number,
  ESI IP number where applicable, PAN) and the employer's establishment details.
- **AC-601.3** — Payslips are **immutable once published**; a correction produces a
  revised payslip with a visible revision marker, never a silent overwrite (I5).

**FR-PAY-602 · Payslip distribution and self-service** · **P0**
Employees shall access current and historical payslips through the employee surface
(web/mobile app, §04 — the employee surface is a named differentiator vs Tally), with
password/OTP protection on downloads.
- **AC-602.1** — An employee can retrieve any historical payslip for the retention
  period without an admin request.

**FR-PAY-603 · Tax-projection statement** · **P1**
The engine shall provide employees a **tax computation sheet** (both regimes, current
projection, declarations applied, TDS to date and remaining) so the payslip is
explainable.
- **AC-603.1** — The projection statement's remaining-months TDS sums with TDS-to-date
  to the projected annual liability under the elected regime.

### 08.8 Statutory returns and certificates

This is the delivery layer — the artefacts §04 says the customer actually pays for. The
computation is §06; this group specifies **generation, validation, filing and
correction** of each return. All file layouts are **versioned schemas** (I2, §06.12 R6):
field numbers are never hard-coded.



**Figure 49. Journey Month End Filing**

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    classDef data fill:#0b3d2e,stroke:#0f5c46,color:#eafff5,stroke-width:1px;
    classDef gate fill:#1d1a3a,stroke:#3b357a,color:#ecebff,stroke-width:1px;
    classDef gen fill:#123a52,stroke:#1f5f85,color:#e6f5ff,stroke-width:1px;
    classDef portal fill:#4a3410,stroke:#8a6413,color:#fff4dd,stroke-width:1px;
    classDef audit fill:#5a1e1e,stroke:#8f2f2f,color:#ffecec,stroke-width:1px;

    A["1. Data assembly<br/>attendance, LOP, arrears,<br/>joiners/exits, revised CTC"]:::data
    B["2. Payroll run locked<br/>gross, deductions,<br/>employer contributions"]:::data

    V{{"3. Validation<br/>UAN/ESIC/PAN checks,<br/>wage-ceiling & rate rules,<br/>PT slab by state"}}:::gate
    VX["Exceptions queue<br/>fix & re-run"]:::gate

    G["4. Generate<br/>EPF ECR txt, ESI return,<br/>PT challan, 24Q TDS,<br/>LWF statement"]:::gen

    P1["5. Submit: EPFO Unified Portal<br/>ECR upload -> challan"]:::portal
    P2["5. Submit: ESIC portal<br/>contribution file"]:::portal
    P3["5. Submit: state PT / LWF<br/>+ TRACES 24Q"]:::portal
    PAY["Challan payment<br/>NEFT / net-banking"]:::portal

    ACK["6. Acknowledgment<br/>TRRN, CIN/CRN,<br/>24Q token, receipts"]:::audit
    AUD["7. Audit trail<br/>immutable log: who, what,<br/>when, filed vs paid,<br/>evidence pack per period"]:::audit

    A --> B --> V
    V -->|fail| VX --> B
    V -->|pass| G
    G --> P1 & P2 & P3
    P1 --> PAY
    P2 --> PAY
    P3 --> PAY
    PAY --> ACK --> AUD
```


**FR-PAY-701 · EPF ECR generation and filing** · **P0**
The engine shall generate the **Electronic Challan-cum-Return (ECR)** text file in the
current EPFO layout for the period, pre-validate it, and file it (via portal upload or
API where available), reconciling the generated challan against the computed
contributions.
- *Detail.* ECR is the master EPF filing (§06.2), monthly by the 15th, carrying
  member-level wages and the three-way split. Built against **Scheme 2026** (§06.9;
  Source: EPF Scheme 2026 / S.O. 3582(E)).
- **AC-701.1** — The ECR file's member lines sum to the challan totals; employer EPS
  never exceeds ₹1,250 per member (the §06.2 TV1 negative test surfaced at file level).
- **AC-701.2** — Members with **un-seeded/KYC-incomplete UANs** are flagged **before**
  file generation (§06.12 R9), not after portal rejection.
- **AC-701.3** — The engine can reproduce a **3A/6A-equivalent register** for audit and
  for Tally migration (§06.12 R10).

**FR-PAY-702 · ESI challan/return** · **P0**
The engine shall generate the monthly **ESI contribution** file/challan and the
half-yearly return reconciliation across the two contribution periods (§06.3), due by
the 15th.
- **AC-702.1** — Contribution-period boundary re-evaluation (FR-PAY-203) is reflected:
  an employee held to the boundary appears in the correct months' filings (TV3).
- **[Hypothesis / blocked]** — **AC-702.2** — Post-22-Nov-2026 ESI computation and
  filing depend on the unresolved successor to the one-year saving (§06.9, §06.13,
  §20 Q8). **Kill/gate criterion: ESI filing for periods after the cliff must be
  escalated and blocked, not guessed, if no successor instrument is notified.** This is a
  payroll-correctness blocker on the validation gate, not a build detail.

**FR-PAY-703 · Professional Tax returns** · **P0**
The engine shall generate the **PT return and challan per state**, on that state's
frequency and due date (monthly/annual, §06.4), with one-click export for the CA console
(§16).
- **AC-703.1** — A multi-state tenant gets one PT return per state per that state's
  cadence, each reconciling to the PT deducted from employees in that state.

**FR-PAY-704 · LWF remittance** · **P0**
The engine shall generate the **LWF remittance** per state on that state's periodicity
(§06.8).
- **AC-704.1** — LWF remittances appear only for LWF states and only in the correct
  periods (e.g., Maharashtra June/December).

**FR-PAY-705 · Statutory bonus return — Form C/D** · **P0**
The engine shall generate the **statutory bonus register and annual return (Form C and
Form D)** for the Payment of Bonus Act, with the payout scheduled by **30 November**
(8 months after FY close). (Source: Payment of Bonus Act 1965, Rule 4/5 forms; §06.11
calendar.)
- **AC-705.1** — Form D reconciles to the bonus computed under FR-PAY-208 and to the
  bonus payout run; ineligible (>₹21,000) employees paid ex-gratia are excluded.

**FR-PAY-706 · TDS — Form 138 (ex-24Q) quarterly statement** · **P0**
The engine shall generate the quarterly TDS statement (**Form 138**, replacing 24Q) in
the current versioned layout, with challan (CIN) reconciliation, and support the
**correction-statement** structure.
- *Detail.* §06.5 [Verified]: Form 138 is a **breaking layout change** (301–312 → A–K
  with 303 deleted; Annexure I 313–327 → C–N with 313/321/322/325 removed; Surcharge/
  Cess/Penalty deleted; Interest & Others Allocation added). Q1–Q3 v1.2 shipped
  22 Jul 2026; correction structures 4 Aug 2026; **the Q4 regular layout did not exist at
  draft date.** (Source: CBDT Form 138 v1.2 notification, 22 Jul 2026.)
- **AC-706.1** — Field mapping is **schema-driven**; no field number (301–312 etc.) is
  hard-coded — swapping the schema version reshapes the file without a code change
  (§06.12 R6).
- **AC-706.2** — CIN/challan totals reconcile to deducted-and-deposited amounts before
  the file is emitted; a mismatch blocks generation.
- **[Verified as absent]** — **AC-706.3** — The **Q4 layout is a pluggable schema slot**
  the engine loads when CBDT releases it; until then, Q4 generation is
  **blocked-pending-layout**, and this state is visible on the filing calendar (§06.11)
  and to the statutory watcher (§13).

**FR-PAY-707 · Annual certificate — Form 130 (ex-Form 16)** · **P0**
The engine shall generate **Form 130** (replacing Form 16), Part A (TRACES-sourced
deduction summary) and Part B (the annual salary/tax computation), for issue by 15 June.
- **[Verified as blocked]** — **AC-707.1** — Form 130 **Part B is gated on the Q4
  Form 138 layout** (§06.5) — it cannot be fully built until the Q4 annexure lands. The
  engine generates Part B against the Q4 schema once available; before that it is
  blocked-pending-layout, not silently emitted with guessed fields.
- **AC-707.2** — Part A digest reconciles to the four quarterly statements; Part B
  reconciles to the sum of the year's payslips and the elected regime's computation.

**FR-PAY-708 · Correction / revised returns** · **P0**
The engine shall generate **correction statements** for any filed return when a
reopen/reversal (FR-PAY-306) or retro recompute (FR-PAY-402) changes a filed period,
using the correction-statement structures (e.g., the 4 Aug 2026 Form 138 correction
structures, §06.5).
- **AC-708.1** — Correcting a filed April ECR after a May arrears recompute produces a
  valid ECR correction, not a duplicate original.

**FR-PAY-709 · The four consolidated statutory registers** · **P0**
The engine shall maintain the **four consolidated statutory registers** in electronic
form with **five-year retention** (§06.11, §04), derived from pay-run and attendance
data, not hand-maintained.
- **AC-709.1** — Each register is reproducible for any month in the retention window and
  reconciles to the corresponding pay runs and filings.

**FR-PAY-710 · Filing calendar and status tracking** · **P0**
The engine shall present the **per-(tenant × state × obligation) filing calendar**
(§06.11) with each filing's status (Not due / Due / Generated / Filed / Accepted /
Rejected / Blocked-pending-layout / Blocked-pending-regime), and shall surface the
headline metric **"filings completed on time"** (§04).
- **AC-710.1** — A rejected filing (e.g., ECR bounced on an un-seeded UAN) shows the
  rejection reason and the remediation task, and does not count as "completed."
- **AC-710.2** — The calendar correctly renders **state-varying** PT/LWF/bonus due dates
  and the **Q4/Form 130 blocked-pending-layout** and **post-cliff ESI
  blocked-pending-regime** states.

The central (non-state-varying) due dates the calendar seeds from — each an
effective-dated rule (I2), each a filing whose on-time completion is the headline metric
(§04):

| Filing | Statutory due date | Cadence | Source cue |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EPF ECR + challan | 15th of following month | Monthly | EPF Scheme 2026 para 38 (Source: S.O. 3582(E)) |
| ESI contribution | 15th of following month | Monthly | ESI (Central) Rules, Rule 31 |
| TDS deposit (challan 281) | 7th of following month (30 Apr for March) | Monthly | Income-tax Rule 30 |
| Form 138 (ex-24Q) | 31 Jul / 31 Oct / 31 Jan / 31 May | Quarterly | CBDT Form 138 notification (blocked-pending-layout for Q4) |
| Form 130 (ex-Form 16) | 15 June | Annual | Income-tax Rule 31 |
| Statutory bonus Form C/D | 30 November (8 months post FY-close) | Annual | Payment of Bonus Act, Rule 5 |
| PT return | State-specific (monthly/annual) | Per state | State PT Acts (§06.4) |
| LWF remittance | State-specific | Per state | State LWF Acts (§06.8) |

- **AC-710.3** — For each filing the calendar computes the due date from the
  effective-dated rule (never a hard-coded constant), rolls a due date falling on a
  Sunday/gazetted holiday to the next working day where the statute so provides, and
  surfaces the **late-filing exposure** (e.g., PF s.14B damages 5–25% p.a. + s.7Q interest
  12% p.a.; TDS s.234E ₹200/day and s.271H penalty; Source: EPF & MP Act ss.7Q/14B,
  Income-tax Act ss.234E/271H) so a slip is quantified, not merely flagged.

---

### 08.9 Full-and-final settlement (F&F)

Exit settlement concentrates the hardest edge cases — proration, arrears, recoveries,
gratuity, leave encashment, and final TDS true-up — into one computation. §05.6 names
mid-year cutover and continuity as the most-cited churn trigger, and F&F is where a
departing employee's certificate continuity is won or lost.



**Figure 50. Fnf Waterfall**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    START([Employee exit triggers F&F computation]):::trig

    subgraph EARN["Earnings and payouts (+)"]
        direction TB
        E1["+ Prorated final-month salary<br/>(FR-PAY-104 basis)"]
        E2["+ Unpaid arrears<br/>(retro recompute per period rules, FR-PAY-401)"]
        E3["+ Leave encashment<br/>exempt up to Rs 25,00,000 lifetime<br/>(s.10(10AA), Notn 31/2023)"]
        E4["+ Gratuity payout if qualified<br/>(15/26 x last wages x years)<br/>exempt up to Rs 20,00,000 (FR-PAY-206)"]
        E5["+ Statutory bonus accrued to date<br/>(FR-PAY-208)"]
        E6["+ Pending reimbursements<br/>(FR-PAY-502)"]
        E1 --> E2 --> E3 --> E4 --> E5 --> E6
    end

    GROSS{{"Gross settlement subtotal"}}:::sub

    subgraph REC["Recoveries and deductions (-)"]
        direction TB
        R1["+/- Notice-pay: recovery or payment<br/>(per policy)"]
        R2["- Advance / loan recovery<br/>(post-tax, tracks balance to zero)"]
        R3["- Asset / canteen recovery<br/>(Code on Wages s.18 50% cap)"]
        R4["- Final TDS true-up<br/>on ACTUAL YTD income, proof-verified<br/>(can be a refund adjustment, FR-PAY-801 AC-3)"]
        R1 --> R2 --> R3 --> R4
    end

    NET([F&F Net Payable<br/>reconciles to the rupee, FR-PAY-801 AC-1]):::net

    START --> EARN
    EARN --> GROSS
    GROSS --> REC
    REC --> NET

    classDef trig fill:#e8eef7,stroke:#41618c,color:#1b2a44;
    classDef sub fill:#fff4d6,stroke:#b8891f,color:#5a4208;
    classDef net fill:#dff2e1,stroke:#3d8c4b,color:#173d1f;
```



**FR-PAY-801 · F&F computation** · **P0**
On an employee exit the engine shall compute a **full-and-final settlement** comprising:
prorated final-month salary; unpaid arrears; **leave encashment** (per policy, on the
correct wage base); **gratuity payout** (FR-PAY-206) if qualified; **statutory bonus**
accrued to date (FR-PAY-208); pending reimbursements; **notice-pay recovery or
payment**; advance/loan/asset recoveries; and the **final TDS true-up** for the
year-to-date.
- **AC-801.1** — F&F net = (all final earnings + encashment + gratuity + accrued bonus +
  pending reimbursements) − (all recoveries + final TDS), shown line-by-line and
  reconciling to the rupee (worked at §08.12 Example E).
- **AC-801.2** — Gratuity is included only if the 5-year rule is met (or waived on
  death/disablement) and is exempt up to ₹20,00,000 (§06.6).
- **AC-801.3** — Final TDS is computed on **actual** year-to-date income (not the annual
  projection), applying actual proof-verified declarations, and can result in a **refund
  adjustment** where excess was deducted.
- **AC-801.4** — **Leave encashment on retirement/resignation** is exempt for a non-
  government employee up to the **₹25,00,000 lifetime ceiling** (raised from ₹3,00,000 eff
  FY2023-24; Source: CBDT Notification 31/2023 under s.10(10AA)(ii)); the ceiling is a
  **lifetime aggregate across employers**, so the engine caps on the balance the employee
  declares as already used, and the excess is taxed and flows to the final TDS true-up.
  Encashment *during* service (not on exit) is fully taxable — the engine distinguishes
  the two.

**FR-PAY-802 · Statutory exit processing and continuity** · **P0**
On exit the engine shall generate the **EPF exit** update (date of exit in ECR, enabling
the employee's UAN-based withdrawal/transfer), the **ESI exit**, and preserve **UAN/ESI
IP continuity** data for the employee's next employer (§05.6 continuity requirement).
- **AC-802.1** — An exited employee's date-of-exit is filed in the appropriate month's
  ECR so their UAN is free for transfer; the engine does not require the *next* employer
  to be in the system.
- **AC-802.2** — The exit produces the data an incoming HRMS needs (YTD earnings, TDS
  deducted, UAN, ESI IP, leave balance, gratuity accrual) as an **exportable continuity
  packet** — the mirror of the migration import (§05.6, §16).

**FR-PAY-803 · F&F approval and settlement window** · **P0**
F&F shall pass the same maker-checker approval (FR-PAY-304) and produce a **settlement
payment** via the bank file (FR-PAY-901) and a **final payslip + Form 130** for the
partial year.
- **AC-803.1** — Gratuity, once payable, is flagged for payment **within 30 days**
  (§06.6; Source: POG Act s.7(3), (3A) interest on delay) with interest exposure
  surfaced if the window is missed.

---

### 08.10 Bank / NEFT payment files

**FR-PAY-901 · Salary bank-file generation** · **P0**
The engine shall generate **bank-upload files for net-salary disbursement** in the
formats of the major Indian banks (per-bank fixed-width/CSV/Excel templates for
NEFT/RTGS/IMPS bulk upload) and a **generic NEFT/H2H** format, from Approved pay-run
net figures.
- *Detail.* Bank formats differ per bank (HDFC, ICICI, SBI, Axis, Kotak, YES, etc.);
  the format is a **versioned, per-bank template**, not hard-coded, so a bank changing
  its layout is a config update (§06.12 R6 shape, applied to bank files).
- **AC-901.1** — The bank file's total credit amount equals the sum of employee net pay
  in the Approved run, to the rupee; a mismatch blocks file generation.
- **AC-901.2** — Each line carries the employee's beneficiary account, IFSC, name and a
  narration; an employee with missing/invalid bank details (failed IFSC checksum) is
  flagged **before** file generation, not rejected at the bank.
- **AC-901.3** — Regenerating the file for the same run is **idempotent** — it does not
  produce a second payment; a reissue requires an explicit reversal/reopen (FR-PAY-306).

**FR-PAY-902 · Statutory payment challans/files** · **P0**
The engine shall generate the **payment files/challans** for PF (ECR challan), ESI, PT
and TDS deposit (challan 281 / e-payment reference), each reconciling to the computed
liability for the period.
- **AC-902.1** — Each statutory challan total equals the computed liability for that head
  and period; the CIN captured on payment feeds Form 138 reconciliation (AC-706.2).

**FR-PAY-903 · Payment status reconciliation** · **P1**
The engine shall record **payment confirmation** (bank return file, UTR, challan CIN)
and reconcile it against the pay run, flagging **failed/returned** credits for reissue.
- **AC-903.1** — A returned NEFT (wrong account) is flagged against the specific
  employee and re-queued, without re-paying the successful lines.

**FR-PAY-904 · Payment approval and segregation** · **P0**
Bank-file release shall require an authorised **payment approver** distinct from the
payroll processor (extends FR-PAY-304 to disbursement).
- **AC-904.1** — Generating a bank file and releasing it for payment cannot be done by a
  single unauthorised actor; the release is logged with actor and timestamp.

---

### 08.11 Audit trail, controls and access

**FR-PAY-1001 · Immutable audit trail** · **P0**
Every create/update/delete of a monetary field, rule assignment, approval, filing and
payment shall be recorded immutably: actor, timestamp, before/after value, rule version
applied, and reason where required (I5).
- **AC-1001.1** — For any figure on any historical payslip or return, the engine can
  answer "who set this, when, from what, under which rule version" without reconstruction.

**FR-PAY-1002 · Replay and recompute audit** · **P0**
The engine shall **replay** any historical pay run to reproduce its outputs (I4) and
**recompute** it against the period's rules (I3), showing any difference — the audit
primitive behind arrears (FR-PAY-401) and corrections (FR-PAY-708).
- **AC-1002.1** — Replaying a closed period with unchanged rules and inputs reproduces
  identical figures; any difference indicates a rule/input change and is itemised
  (§06.14 TV12).

**FR-PAY-1003 · Role-based access and data-minimisation** · **P0**
Payroll data (salary, PAN, bank, statutory IDs) shall be governed by **role-based
access** — an ESS employee sees only their own; a manager sees none by default; a
payroll admin sees their establishment; a CA console gets **read-only audit access**
(§16). DPDP s.7(i) removes the consent-UX requirement for employment-purpose processing
(§17, [Verified]; Source: DPDP Act 2023 s.7(i)), but access control and CERT-In
logging still bind from day one.
- **AC-1003.1** — A manager cannot view a report's salary figures; an ESS user cannot
  query another employee's payslip; every access to salary/PAN/bank is logged (CERT-In
  180-day ICT-log retention within Indian jurisdiction; Source: CERT-In Directions
  28.04.2022).

**FR-PAY-1004 · Pre-run validation gate** · **P0**
Before a run can be Approved, the engine shall run a **blocking validation suite** and
surface every failure with its remediation: un-seeded UANs (ECR), inoperative/
Aadhaar-unlinked PAN (higher TDS), missing/invalid bank details, negative net,
structure-not-summing-to-CTC, missing work-state (PT/LWF), component with no wage-base
flags set (AC-101.4), employees crossing a statutory threshold (§06.1 latch — e.g.,
tenant crossing 20 triggers EPF enrolment), and any filing in a
blocked-pending-layout/regime state.
- *Detail.* Draft 1 §05.6 names the **20-crossing detected inside the product** as "the
  single highest-intent acquisition moment in the beachhead" — this validation is where
  the engine detects it and moves the tenant from "not registered for EPF" to "first
  ECR filed" without leaving the app.
- **AC-1004.1** — A run with any blocking failure cannot be Approved; each failure links
  to its fix.
- **AC-1004.2** — When tenant headcount crosses 20 for the first time, the engine raises
  EPF enrolment / UAN-generation / first-ECR tasks automatically (§06.1 product
  implication; Source: EPF & MP Act 1952 s.1(3)(b), 20-employee threshold), without the
  customer knowing the threshold exists.
- **AC-1004.3** — When headcount crosses **10** (ESI/gratuity latch, on a look-back
  window), the engine latches the obligation on and does not silently drop it if
  headcount later dips (§06.1, §06.12 R4).

**FR-PAY-1005 · Statutory-change watcher integration** · **P0**
The engine's rule tables shall be updatable through the **statutory-change watcher**
(§13) which catches **amendments and corrigenda, not just new instruments** — because a
watcher keyed only to new notifications would have missed the corrigendum that inverted
the entire November 2026 EPF analysis (§06.9). (Source: §06.9 cliff analysis; the
S.O. 5319(E) vs corrected S.O. 3582(E) discrepancy.)
- **AC-1005.1** — A notified rate/slab change becomes an **effective-dated rule version**
  (I2) with a documented source (gazette/notification URL + date) before it applies; no
  rule ships without provenance (§0 standing rule).

---

### 08.12 Worked examples

These are the end-to-end computations the acceptance tests are built from. All rates
trace to §06 and to the golden vectors §06.14. Figures are illustrative but internally
exact; TDS figures use the **FY2025-26 verified** slabs and rebate (FY2026-27 is
[Hypothesis] pending Finance Act 2026, §06.13).

#### Example A — Standard monthly payslip (single, full-month, Karnataka)

Employee: monthly gross ₹75,150 (annual ₹9,01,800; CTC ≈ ₹9.6L with employer costs
inside per FR-PAY-102). Structure: Basic ₹40,000, HRA ₹20,000, special allowance
₹15,150. Work state Karnataka. New default tax regime, no declarations. PF on ceiling.

| Head | Basis | Amount (₹) | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Basic | fixed | 40,000 | PF/gratuity wage component |
| HRA | fixed | 20,000 | ESI-base only (employee above ESI ceiling anyway) |
| Special allowance | balance | 15,150 | payment-of-wages base |
| **Gross earnings** | | **75,150** | |
| Employee EPF | 12% × min(PF base, 15,000) | −1,800 | PF base = Basic ₹40,000 (no add-back: excluded < 50%), capped at ₹15,000 (TV7) |
| Professional Tax | KA slab > ₹25,000 | −200 | §06.4 (Source: KA PT Act 1976) |
| TDS u/s 192 | new-regime projection ÷ 12 | −0 | see note below |
| **Total deductions** | | **−2,000** | |
| **Net pay** | gross − deductions | **73,150** | to bank (FR-PAY-901) |
| *Employer EPF (CTC, not paid to emp)* | | *550* | ₹550 of the ₹1,800; balance to EPS |
| *Employer EPS* | 8.33% capped | *1,250* | §06.2 cap (TV1) |
| *EDLI + EPF admin* | 0.5% + 0.5% | *75 + 75* | employer cost |
| *Gratuity accrual* | (15/26)×Basic÷12 approx | *~1,923* | accrual ledger (FR-PAY-206) |

Two teaching points. First, the **add-back does not trigger**: excluded components
(HRA + special = ₹35,150) are **below** 50% of ₹75,150, so the PF base is Basic ₹40,000,
then capped at the ₹15,000 ceiling (TV7). Employee is **outside ESI** (gross > ₹21,000),
so no ESI. Second, **TDS projects to ₹0** here: annual gross ₹9,01,800 − ₹75,000
standard deduction = ₹8,26,800 taxable, and the FY2025-26 new-regime **s.87A rebate
(nil tax to ₹12L taxable)** zeroes the liability. This is itself a golden behaviour — a
naive engine that applies slab tax without the rebate over-deducts. *(FY2026-27
[Hypothesis]: re-verify the rebate ceiling against Budget 2026 before the year's run;
AC-205.6.)* Example F shows a higher earner where TDS bites.

#### Example B — Mid-month join proration (FR-PAY-104)

Same structure as A, employee joins **16 September** (30-day month, calendar-day basis).
Paid days 15/30.

- Gross = ₹75,150 × 15/30 = **₹37,575**.
- PF: wage base = prorated Basic ₹20,000, capped at ₹15,000 ceiling → employee EPF
  ₹1,800 (ceiling still binds). *If* the employer elected actual-wage below ceiling,
  PF would prorate; here the ceiling absorbs it.
- PT (Karnataka): ₹200 for the month (PT is a monthly slab on the month's earned wage,
  not day-prorated; the ₹37,575 earned still exceeds the ₹25,000 KA threshold).
- ESI: the coverage test reads the **full-month** wage (₹75,150 > ₹21,000), so the
  employee is out of ESI regardless of the prorated ₹37,575 (§06.3) — proration does not
  create ESI coverage.
- TDS: annual projection now spans 6.5 months of earning; the September run projects
  full-year tax on the prorated year and spreads it (FR-PAY-205 AC-205.2).
- **Acceptance:** the payment-of-wages register shows 15 paid days; PF/PT computed on the
  prorated base, ESI coverage on the full-month base (AC-104.1).

#### Example C — Arrears from a back-dated increment (FR-PAY-401)

Employee on ₹60,000/month gets a revision to ₹70,000 **effective 1 April**, entered and
processed in the **July** run. April–June are closed. Employee is on the **old regime**
with declarations lodged (chosen deliberately here: under the new regime the FY2025-26
s.87A rebate zeroes tax up to ₹12L taxable, so this earner's TDS would be nil and the
arrears would carry no tax delta — see the note below).

Per-month recompute (each against **that month's** rules, I3; TV12):

| Month | Old gross | New gross | Δ gross | Δ PF (emp) | Δ PT | Δ TDS | Δ net |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Apr | 60,000 | 70,000 | 10,000 | 0 (ceiling) | 0 (already max slab) | 2,080 | 7,920 |
| May | 60,000 | 70,000 | 10,000 | 0 | 0 | 2,080 | 7,920 |
| Jun | 60,000 | 70,000 | 10,000 | 0 | 0 | 2,080 | 7,920 |
| **Arrears** | | | **30,000** | **0** | **0** | **6,240** | **23,760** |

Paid in July as an **arrears line**; July's own run also reflects the new ₹70,000. PF is
0 in the delta because both ₹60,000 and ₹70,000 Basic exceed the ₹15,000 ceiling; PT is
0 because both figures already sit in Karnataka's top ₹200/mo slab. The ₹10,000/mo
increment falls entirely in the old-regime 20% slab (taxable moves ₹6.70L → ₹7.90L, both
under the ₹10L / 30% boundary), so marginal TDS ≈ **20.8%** (20% + 4% cess) = ₹2,080/mo.
**Teaching point on regime dependence:** had the employee been on the new default regime,
Δ TDS would be **0** — the arrears would still recompute PF/ESI/PT per month, but the tax
delta vanishes under the rebate. If a PT slab or PF rate had changed between April and
July, the recompute would use the **April-in-force** version (AC-401.3, TV12), not
July's. Arrears PF (if a base moved below ceiling) would generate an **ECR correction**
for those months (FR-PAY-708). Note too that a lump-sum arrears payment can trigger
**s.89(1) relief (Form 10E)** for the employee — see AC-205.7.

#### Example D — The 50% wage add-back (FR-PAY-201, §06.10, TV6)

Monthly remuneration ₹1,00,000: Basic ₹35,000, HRA ₹20,000, conveyance ₹10,000, special
₹35,000. Excluded components (HRA + conveyance + special) = ₹65,000 = **65%** of
₹1,00,000. Half of remuneration = ₹50,000. Excess over 50% = **₹15,000 added back**.
(Source: Code on Wages s.2(y) / CoSS s.2(88).)

- **PF wage base** = Basic ₹35,000 + add-back ₹15,000 = **₹50,000**, then capped at the
  ₹15,000 statutory ceiling for PF (or actual, if the employer opts in).
- **Gratuity wage base** = ₹50,000 (the add-back raises gratuity even though the PF
  ceiling absorbs it — which is exactly why gratuity and PF cannot share one base field,
  I1).
- **ESI base** = gross (not applicable here, above ceiling).
- **Bonus wage base** = ₹7,000 or the scheduled-employment minimum wage, whichever is
  higher (FR-PAY-208) — a fourth, unrelated base on the same payslip.
- **Payment-of-wages base** = full ₹1,00,000.

**Acceptance:** the engine reports all bases distinctly, each stamped with the
wage-definition rule version (AC-201.1, AC-201.3).

#### Example E — Full-and-final settlement (FR-PAY-801)

Employee resigns effective **20 September** after **6 years 4 months** (rounds down to 6,
TV8), last-drawn Basic+DA ₹52,000, monthly gross ₹75,150, 12 days of leave to encash, a
₹40,000 salary advance outstanding, one month notice served (no recovery), pending
₹8,000 reimbursement with proof.

| Component | Basis | Amount (₹) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sept salary (20/30 days) | proration | +50,100 |
| Leave encashment (12 days) | (Basic÷26)×12 | +24,000 |
| Gratuity | (15/26)×52,000×6 | +1,80,000 |
| Pending reimbursement | proof-verified | +8,000 |
| Salary-advance recovery | balance | −40,000 |
| Final TDS true-up | actual YTD | −X |
| **F&F net** | | **= sum, to the rupee** |

Gratuity ₹1,80,000 is **tax-free** (< ₹20L ceiling, §06.6). Note the **6-month rounding
rounds 6y 4m down to 6 years** (TV8) — 6y 8m would have rounded up to 7. Final TDS is
computed on **actual** year-to-date income with proof-verified declarations (AC-801.3),
possibly producing a refund adjustment. Gratuity is flagged for payment within **30
days** (AC-803.1). The exit files the **date-of-exit in September's ECR** (AC-802.1) and
emits a **continuity packet** (YTD, TDS, UAN, ESI IP, leave, gratuity accrual) for the
next employer (AC-802.2), plus a final payslip and partial-year Form 130.

#### Example F — Dual-regime TDS comparison (FR-PAY-205)

Employee: annual gross ₹18,00,000 (₹1,50,000/mo), declares old-regime 80C ₹1,50,000,
80D ₹25,000, HRA exemption computed at ₹1,80,000. FY2025-26 slabs.

| | New regime (s.115BAC) | Old regime |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gross | 18,00,000 | 18,00,000 |
| Standard deduction | −75,000 | −50,000 |
| HRA exemption | — | −1,80,000 |
| Chapter VI-A (80C + 80D) | — | −1,75,000 |
| **Taxable income** | **17,25,000** | **13,95,000** |
| Tax (before cess) | 1,45,000 | 2,31,000 |
| + 4% cess | 5,800 | 9,240 |
| **Annual TDS** | **1,50,800** | **2,40,240** |
| **Monthly TDS (÷12)** | **≈ 12,567** | **≈ 20,020** |

New-regime tax builds from the FY2025-26 slabs: 5% on ₹4–8L (₹20,000) + 10% on ₹8–12L
(₹40,000) + 15% on ₹12–16L (₹60,000) + 20% on ₹16–17.25L (₹25,000) = **₹1,45,000**.
Old-regime: 5% on ₹2.5–5L (₹12,500) + 20% on ₹5–10L (₹1,00,000) + 30% on ₹10–13.95L
(₹1,18,500) = **₹2,31,000**. Here the **new regime is cheaper** (₹1.51L vs ₹2.40L), so a
silent employee defaults to it and pays ≈ ₹12,567/mo. **Acceptance:** the engine reports
both figures (AC-205.1);
switching the election re-projects the remaining months without disturbing amounts
already deducted (AC-205.2). If this employee had declared 80C ₹1.5L, 80D, HRA *and*
a ₹2L home-loan interest (s.24), the old regime could flip to cheaper — which is
precisely why both projections run every period. *(Slab figures illustrative on
FY2025-26; FY2026-27 pending AC-205.6.)*

---

### 08.13 Cross-cutting acceptance criteria — the engine's definition of done

These are the run-level and product-level gates. A build that passes every per-FR AC but
fails these is not shippable.

| # | Gate | Ties to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| G1 | **Determinism** — re-running any unchanged period reproduces byte-identical figures and files | I4, FR-PAY-209, 1002 |
| G2 | **Reconciliation** — for every run: Σ employee net = bank-file total; Σ each statutory head = its challan; Σ payslips = registers = returns, all to the rupee | FR-PAY-303, 701–709, 901 |
| G3 | **Retro correctness** — arrears/retro recompute uses the period's rule version, not today's | I3, FR-PAY-401, 402; TV12 |
| G4 | **No model-generated figures** — no statutory or monetary value on any payslip, challan or return originates from the assistant | §12 [Verified], I-wide |
| G5 | **Filing is the metric** — the product reports "filings completed and accepted on time," not "payslips generated"; a rejected filing is not "done" | §04, FR-PAY-710 |
| G6 | **Schema-driven file formats** — Form 138 (incl. the Q4 slot), ECR, ESI, bonus Form C/D, bank templates are versioned schemas; no field number or column is hard-coded | §06.12 R6, FR-PAY-705–708, 901 |
| G7 | **Blocked states are honest** — Q4 Form 138, Form 130 Part B (blocked-pending-layout), and post-cliff ESI (blocked-pending-regime) render as blocked, never silently emitted with guessed values | FR-PAY-702, 706, 707, 710 |
| G8 | **Segregation of duties** — no single unauthorised actor can compute, approve, and pay the same run | FR-PAY-304, 904 |
| G9 | **Migration parity** — the engine reproduces migration-grade registers (3A/6A-equiv, ESI 5/6, PT/LWF, Bonus A–D) and ingests mid-year YTD without breaking certificate continuity | §05.6, §06.12 R10, FR-PAY-709, 802 |
| G10 | **Provenance** — every rule version carries a gazette/notification source (URL + date); "check for a corrigendum" is enforced in the watcher path | §0 standing rule, FR-PAY-1005 |
| G11 | **Golden vectors pass** — the engine passes all §06.14 TV1–TV12 before any rate-change release | §06.14, FR-PAY-201–208 |

**Bottom line for the engine.** The payroll & statutory-filing engine is the P0 core of
the product (§05.5 item 1) and the direct expression of the Draft 1 thesis: it exists to
**produce accepted statutory filings**, and the payslip, the bank file and the FBP
wallet are the byproducts and the acquisition surface around that core. Its correctness
is not a UX concern but a legal one, which is why every FR here reduces to a
deterministic, effective-dated, retrospectively-recomputable, fully-audited rule — and
why the competitive position (§04) is honest: this is **parity with Zoho on computation,
and differentiation only against Frappe, Kredily and Tally on filing execution and the
maintained-update SLA** behind it, not on statutory breadth ([Verified], §04).


---

## 09. Functional Requirements — Attendance, Leave & Deskless

Attendance was in the original brief and received **zero research in round one**
(Draft 1, §"Attendance, devices and the deskless worker"). This section closes
that gap and turns the one strong, hostile-checked finding in the corpus — build
the **ADMS/WDMS push receiver in v1** — into a full functional spec, alongside
the leave, shift, overtime and regularization surfaces that the beachhead
(manufacturing, retail, logistics, hospitality, clinics at 20–200 heads) will not
buy without.

The framing is the same one that runs through the whole document: **the statutory
filing, not the payslip, is the unit of delivery.** Attendance is not a
convenience feature here — it is a *filing input* and a *filing itself*. Worked
hours drive the muster/attendance register (a statutory record with five-year
retention, §09.10); overtime drives the wages base that feeds ECR, ESI and PT
(§06, §08); leave-without-pay and loss-of-pay drive the paid-days count that every
downstream challan reconciles against. A wrong punch is not a UX problem, it is a
wrong PF contribution and a wrong 24Q/Form 138 line. Attendance therefore inherits
the engine's cardinal rule (§12, Verified): **rules-first, LLM-last — no worked-hour,
overtime or leave-balance figure is ever model-generated.** The assistant explains,
nudges, translates and drafts regularizations; the deterministic engine computes.

A second framing, specific to this section: **the beachhead is more deskless than
it looks.** A 120-person auto-components firm in Pune, a 60-store QSR chain, a
3PL warehouse cluster — these are the 50–200 accounts that carry revenue (§05),
and their workforce is largely frontline, on shared or no devices, in low
connectivity, reading Hindi/Marathi/Tamil, not English. Draft 1's verified
constraints — **worker-initiated not employer-push, shared-device reality, and
terminal integration as non-optional for frontline** — are load-bearing design
inputs, not accessibility niceties. They appear throughout as `FR-DSK-###`.



**Figure 51. Attendance Engine**

**How to read the FRs.** Each requirement carries an ID (`FR-<area>-###`), a
priority (**P0** = required for v1 beachhead launch; **P1** = fast-follow within
v1.x; **P2** = expansion/v2), the requirement statement, a short rationale tied to
statute or evidence, and **acceptance criteria** as testable bullets. Confidence
markers apply to the *claim a requirement rests on*, not to the requirement itself.
The standing rule from §02 holds: **no statutory number ships without a
gazette/notified-rule citation and a "check for a corrigendum" pass** — several
figures below are marked **[Hypothesis]** precisely because the OSH&WC Central
Rules (notified 8 May 2026) devolve leave-accrual and spread-over specifics to
*state* rules that are rolling out unevenly (§20 risk: uneven state-rule
notification).
