### 14.3 The ER model — relationships and cardinality

The ERD above renders the entity-relationship model. The relationships that are non-obvious or that people get wrong are called out here, because getting cardinality wrong here is a filing-rejection bug later.

| Relationship | Cardinality | Why it is this and not the naive version |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tenant → Employer | 1 : N | A CA-run tenant, or a group, holds multiple legal entities; billing is at Tenant, filing is at Employer/Establishment. |
| Employer → Establishment | 1 : N | **This is the multi-state pivot.** EPF/ESI/PT/S&E registrations attach to Establishment, not Employer. A single PAN with offices in MH, KA, TS has ≥3 PT registrations and possibly ≥3 ESI sub-codes. |
| Person → Employment | 1 : N | Rehire and inter-entity transfer create new Employments under one immutable `employee_id`, preserving gratuity/continuous-service lineage (§07 FR-CHR-001). |
| Employment → Establishment | N : 1 (effective-dated) | A transfer re-points this link with an effective date; PT re-derives to the new state from that date; the prior state's return for the pre-transfer portion is untouched (§07 AC). |
| Employment → StatutoryIdentifier | 1 : N | One employment has many typed IDs; UAN persists across employments (portable), ESI IP persists, PF Member ID is establishment-scoped so it *changes* on transfer. Modelling PF Member ID as an attribute of Person is a bug. |
| Employment → CompensationAssignment | 1 : N (effective-dated) | Every CTC revision, promotion, or component re-tag is a new version; the current one is `effective_to IS NULL`. |
| CompensationStructure → PayComponent | 1 : N (ordered) | Order matters: "special allowance as balance figure = CTC − Σ(other components)" must evaluate last (§08 FR-PAY-101). |
| PayRun → PayrollResult | 1 : N | One per included employee. |
| PayrollResult → Payslip | 1 : 1 | Payslip is a derived render; regenerating it must reproduce byte-identical output from the same result + template (D4). |
| PayRun → Filing | 1 : N | One monthly regular run feeds **multiple** filings (ECR, ESI challan, PT return(s) — one per state, LWF where due). This 1:N is the whole product. |
| Filing → Challan/Payment | 1 : 0..N | ECR generates then requires a challan; a nil-return filing has zero payments. |
| Filing → Document | 1 : N | The generated file, the portal acknowledgement PDF, the challan receipt — all evidence, all retained. |
| Filing → PayrollResult | N : M (via snapshot) | A filing references the exact result rows it was built from; a **retro/arrears filing** references corrections spanning multiple prior runs. This is captured by an input-snapshot, not a live join, so re-opening a later period cannot silently mutate a filed artefact (D2). |
| EffectiveDatedRule → Jurisdiction | N : 1 | Every rule is scoped to Central or a State/UT (or a sub-state local body for certain PT/LWF cases). |
| PayrollResult → EffectiveDatedRule | N : M (recorded) | Each computed figure records which rule version(s) produced it — the audit lineage in D4. |
| AuditEvent → (any entity) | N : 1 (polymorphic) | Every statutory/monetary write emits one. |
| RetentionHold → (any entity) | N : M | A hold can pin an employee, a pay run, or a whole establishment's records. |
| DataPrincipalRequest → Person | N : 1 | DPDP requests attach to the natural person, spanning all their Employments. |

---

### 14.4 Entity deep-dives (the load-bearing ones)

Only the entities whose *field-level* shape is non-obvious or India-specific are expanded. Identity/master fields are specified in §07.1 and not repeated; here we specify the fields that exist *because of a statute or a filing format*.

#### 14.4.1 Establishment — the registration hub

The naive model attaches PF/ESI/PT to the company. In India they attach to the **establishment/registration**, and one company routinely holds many. This entity is the reason multi-state "just works" or doesn't.

| Field | Notes | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `epf_code` | Establishment code allotted by EPFO (region-office-scoped format, e.g. `MHBAN0012345000`: region + office + 7-digit code + 3-digit extension). ECR files and Form 3A/5/6A/10/12A are per-code. | EPFO establishment registration **[Verified]** |
| `esi_code` | 17-digit ESI employer code; **sub-codes** per state/branch office are common and each files separately. | ESIC registration **[Verified]** |
| `pt_reg_no`, `pt_enrol_no` | State PT **registration certificate (RC)** — to deduct from employees — and **enrolment certificate (EC)** — the employer's own PT liability. Distinct numbers; distinct returns. Present only in PT-levying states. | State PT Acts **[Verified]** |
| `lwf_reg_no` | State LWF registration where the state runs an LWF; periodicity varies (monthly/half-yearly/annual). | State LWF Acts **[Verified]** |
| `se_reg_no`, `se_state` | Shops & Establishments registration — per-state, and the register/leave/hours rules vary by state Act. | State S&E Acts **[Verified]** |
| `tan` | Employer's TAN for TDS; 24Q/Form 138 file at TAN. A company may run multiple TANs. | Income Tax Act s.203A **[Verified]** |
| `gstin` | 15-char GSTIN where the entity is registered; not a payroll key but needed for invoice/vendor reconciliation and some state PT portals. | CGST Act **[Verified]** |
| `jurisdiction_id` | Work-location state; the join key into `EffectiveDatedRule` for PT/LWF/S&E/OT. | — |
| `nic_code`, `hazardous_flag` | Drives Second-Schedule employee-compensation applicability and the docks/mines/construction health-check confinement (§03 corrections). | CoSS Second Schedule; notified Rules **[Verified]** |
| `headcount_tracked` | Running distinct-employee count on the "any day of the preceding twelve months" latch (§03) — drives the 10/20/50/100/300 obligation gates so a threshold crossing arms the right filings automatically. | Labour Codes headcount tests **[Verified]** |

**Edge case — new-state operation without registration.** An employee physically working in a state where the employer has *no* PT registration yet (new market entry, remote hire): the model stores the derived PT liability with a `registration_pending` state so the readiness report flags "PT due, no registration" rather than silently under-remitting — a common source of interest/penalty.

**Edge case — the obligation latch.** The 10-employee ESI/gratuity test reads "on any day of the preceding twelve months," so it **latches once crossed** and does not un-arm when headcount dips (§03 **[Verified]**). `headcount_tracked` therefore stores the *peak-in-trailing-12-months*, not the spot count, and `EligibilityState` transitions are driven off the latch, never off current headcount.

**AC-DM-03** — *Given* an Establishment with offices in MH, KA and TS, *When* a September regular run completes, *Then* the readiness report lists exactly three distinct PT `Filing` obligations keyed to three `pt_reg_no`s, and any work-location state lacking a `pt_reg_no` surfaces as `registration_pending`, never as a zero-liability line.

**AC-DM-04** — *Given* an establishment that touched 20 employees on a single day, *When* headcount later falls to 15, *Then* EPF applicability in `EligibilityState` remains armed (latch), and disabling it requires an explicit, audited administrative action with a statutory basis, not an automatic de-arm.

#### 14.4.2 Employee, Employment, StatutoryIdentifier

`Person` is immutable-identity; `Employment` is the instance. `StatutoryIdentifier` is modelled as a **typed, effective-dated, linkage-stateful** child rather than columns on Employee, because the *state* of each ID is what gates filings:

| ID type | Value format | Linkage state stored (the load-bearing part) | Gates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| UAN | 12 numeric | `seeding_status` (Aadhaar–UAN KYC: pending/verified/rejected), `transfer_status` | ECR acceptance, claim settlement |
| PAN | `AAAAA9999A` | `availability` (present / not-available → s.206AA higher rate), `verification_status` (NSDL/UTI), `holder_type` (4th char) | TDS rate, Form 138/130 |
| ESI IP | 10 numeric | `registration_status` (registered / pending), `iw_flag` (international worker) | ESI contribution filing |
| Aadhaar | 12 numeric, Verhoeff-checksum, **masked (last-4 only)** everywhere | `seeding_status`, `masking` enforced by classification (D7) | UAN seeding; never a filing key itself |
| PRAN | 12 numeric | corporate-NPS subscription state | NPS deduction, 80CCD |
| Bank account + IFSC | account + IFSC (`AAAA0999999`) + name | `verification_status` (penny-drop / name-match) — **disbursal-blocking** | Salary/FnF payout |
| PF Member ID | establishment-scoped | **changes on transfer** — modelled on Employment, not Person | Form 3A/6A, EPF claims |

**Statutory-identifier linkage state is a small state machine, not a flag.** The gating decisions (does ECR accept? is s.206AA higher rate applied? can we disburse?) are transitions, not truth values, so each identifier carries an explicit lifecycle.



**Figure 89. Statutory Identifier Linkage States**

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    direction LR

    state "UAN (Aadhaar-UAN seeding)" as UAN {
        [*] --> UAN_pending
        UAN_pending --> UAN_verified : KYC name-match OK
        UAN_pending --> UAN_rejected : name / Aadhaar mismatch
        UAN_rejected --> UAN_pending : identifier corrected, retry
        UAN_verified --> UAN_transfer : inter-est. transfer (Form 13)
        UAN_transfer --> UAN_verified : transfer settled (UAN portable)
        UAN_verified : GATE ECR accepted, claim settlement
        UAN_rejected : GATE ECR rejected -> rejection_reasons[]
    }

    state "PAN (TDS rate driver)" as PAN {
        [*] --> PAN_notAvailable
        PAN_notAvailable --> PAN_present : PAN captured
        PAN_present --> PAN_verified : NSDL / UTI verify OK
        PAN_present --> PAN_invalid : verify failed
        PAN_invalid --> PAN_present : re-captured
        PAN_notAvailable : GATE s.206AA higher-rate TDS
        PAN_verified : GATE normal TDS, Form 138 / 130
    }

    state "ESI IP" as ESI {
        [*] --> ESI_pending
        ESI_pending --> ESI_registered : IP number allotted
        ESI_registered : iw_flag drives IW sub-regime
        ESI_registered : GATE ESI contribution filing
    }

    state "Aadhaar (masked last-4)" as AAD {
        [*] --> AAD_captured : Verhoeff checksum OK, encrypted
        AAD_captured --> AAD_seeded : seeded to UAN
        AAD_seeded : feeds UAN seeding; never a filing key
    }

    state "Bank + IFSC (disbursal)" as BANK {
        [*] --> BANK_unverified
        BANK_unverified --> BANK_verified : penny-drop + name-match OK
        BANK_unverified --> BANK_failed : penny-drop / name mismatch
        BANK_failed --> BANK_unverified : account corrected
        BANK_unverified : GATE disbursal blocked
        BANK_verified : GATE salary / FnF payout released
    }

    state "PF Member ID (est.-scoped)" as PFM {
        [*] --> PFM_issued
        PFM_issued --> PFM_reissued : transfer -> new Employment
        PFM_reissued : changes on transfer (on Employment, not Person)
    }

    state "PRAN (corporate NPS)" as PRAN {
        [*] --> PRAN_inactive
        PRAN_inactive --> PRAN_active : NPS subscription live
        PRAN_active : GATE 80CCD deduction
    }

    AAD --> UAN : seeding gates ECR

    note right of UAN
        Each StatutoryIdentifier carries an explicit linkage
        lifecycle, not a boolean flag. The gate (ECR accept?
        s.206AA higher rate? can we disburse?) is a transition.
    end note
```


**Aadhaar rule (D7 + §07 FR-CHR-005):** the value is encrypted at rest, rendered as last-4 in every UI/export/log/support view, and a full read is an explicitly audited KYC action. This is enforced by the classification tag, not by developer discipline. The Verhoeff checksum lets the system reject a mistyped Aadhaar at entry *without* storing or transmitting the full value beyond the encrypted field.

`EligibilityState` is a separate effective-dated child so that **crossings are handled by rule, not by a checkbox.** The two crossings that generate the most support tickets:

- **ESI ceiling crossing mid-period.** An ESI-covered employee revised above ₹21,000 gross in July keeps coverage to 30 Sep (end of the Apr–Sep contribution period) and drops from 1 Oct — **two effective-dated rows, both visible in history** (Source: ESI (Central) Rules Rule 50 & contribution-period definition **[Verified]**). ESI contribution periods are Apr–Sep and Oct–Mar; corresponding benefit periods are Jan–Jun and Jul–Dec. The model stores the contribution-period boundary, not the salary-revision date, as the coverage-end.
- **Gratuity eligibility crossing.** Continuous-service clock (5 years / 240 days-per-year, waived on death/disablement — Source: Payment of Gratuity Act; CoSS Ch. V **[Verified]**) is a derived `EligibilityState` computed off the `Employment` DOJ lineage, so a rehire under the same `employee_id` correctly bridges (or breaks) continuous service per the transfer terms.

**AC-DM-05** — *Given* an employee whose gross rises above ₹21,000 on 12-Jul, *When* the July, August and September runs execute, *Then* ESI is deducted through September on the pre-revision coverage and stops from 1-Oct, producing exactly two `EligibilityState` rows (`covered` → `not_covered` effective 01-Oct), and the historical rows remain queryable.

**AC-DM-06** — *Given* an employee rehired under an existing `employee_id` after a 3-month gap, *When* gratuity eligibility is evaluated, *Then* continuous-service is computed from the `Employment` lineage per the recorded transfer/break terms, and PF Member ID is re-issued on the new `Employment` (establishment-scoped) while UAN and ESI IP are carried forward unchanged.

**International workers (IW) — a distinct PF sub-regime.** `StatutoryIdentifier` carries an `iw_flag`, and `EligibilityState` reads it because an IW has **no ₹15,000 PF wage ceiling** — contribution is on full PF wages (Source: EPF Scheme para 83, IW provisions **[Verified]**). Where the worker is from a country with a Social Security Agreement (SSA) with India, a **Certificate of Coverage / detachment certificate** may exempt or cap contribution; the model stores this as a `Document` (C1) linked to the `Employment` with a validity window, and `EligibilityState` reflects the exemption for that window. This is the one case where the `pf_wage_ceiling` rule row is deliberately *not applied*, driven by the identifier flag, not a code branch.

**Employment type and contract labour.** `Employment.type ∈ {permanent, fixed_term, contract, apprentice, trainee, consultant, gig_platform}` matters because obligations differ: fixed-term workers accrue **pro-rata gratuity** under the new Codes (no 5-year bar for the fixed-term cohort — Source: Code on Social Security **[Hypothesis]** on exact mechanics; kill/confirm: notified Rules read), contract labour under a principal employer may sit on the *contractor's* PF/ESI code rather than the principal's, and gig/platform workers fall under the Code on Social Security's separate aggregator-cess regime (not yet operational at Draft-1 date — **[Verified]** unresolved, watch MoLE). Modelling `type` on `Employment` (not `Person`) lets one person hold a consultant engagement and later a permanent one with correctly different statutory treatment.

#### 14.4.3 CompensationStructure / PayComponent / CompensationAssignment — where the two wage bases live

The 50% add-back forces the schema to compute *several* bases from one component set. Each `PayComponent` therefore carries independent boolean inclusion flags, not a single "statutory" flag:

| Flag on PayComponent | Feeds |
| --- | --- |
| `pf_wage` | PF/EPS/EDLI + gratuity add-back base (excludes HRA, conveyance, overtime, award settlements) |
| `esi_wage` | ESI gross base (**includes** HRA/conveyance/overtime) |
| `gratuity_wage` | Gratuity accrual base (add-back rules) |
| `pow_wage` | Payment-of-wages / equal-remuneration base (broadest) |
| `taxable`, `tax_section` | TDS u/s 192 computation, exemption section (HRA 10(13A), etc.) |
| `perquisite_flag`, `fbp_flag` | Form 12BA perquisite valuation; flexible-benefit wallet |
| `component_kind` | earning / deduction / reimbursement / statutory-employer-cost / employer-cost (CTC-only, non-payable) |
| `basis` | fixed / percent-of(basic|ctc|gross) / balance-figure / slab / attendance-prorated |

**Worked example (why one `wage` column is wrong).** Employee CTC ₹9,00,000/yr. Structure: Basic ₹3,00,000, HRA ₹1,50,000, Conveyance ₹19,200, Special Allowance ₹4,30,800 (balance figure). Basic alone = ₹25,000/month; total monthly remuneration = ₹75,000.

- **Excluded-component test (the add-back).** Excluded components for the PF/gratuity base = HRA + Conveyance + Special = (₹1,50,000 + ₹19,200 + ₹4,30,800)/12 = ₹50,000/month, i.e. **66.7% of the ₹75,000 total remuneration**. Since excluded (66.7%) > 50%, the excess over the one-half line is **deemed wages and added back** to the PF/gratuity base: add-back = excluded − (50% × total) = ₹50,000 − (50% × ₹75,000) = ₹50,000 − ₹37,500 = **₹12,500/month**. Wage base for PF/gratuity = Basic ₹25,000 + add-back ₹12,500 = **₹37,500/month** (Source: Code on Wages s.2(y) / CoSS s.2(88); final Central Rules notified 8 May 2026 **[Verified]**).
- **PF ceiling interaction.** PF/EPS statutory basis is capped at ₹15,000/month unless the employer opts to contribute on actual wages. If the employer restricts to the ceiling, employee EPF = 12% × ₹15,000 = ₹1,800; employer split: EPS = 8.33% × ₹15,000 = ₹1,250 (EPS wage capped at ₹15,000), EPF = remainder; EDLI = 0.5% × ₹15,000 = ₹75; admin charges (A/c 2) = 0.5% × ₹15,000, min ₹500/month per establishment (Source: EPF Scheme 2026; EDLI 1976; admin-charge notification **[Verified]**). The add-back computed above still matters: it is the number that governs whether the employer's "contribute on actuals" figure is itself correct.
- **ESI gross base** = full gross (Basic + HRA + Conveyance + Special) = ₹75,000 — but this employee is **above the ₹21,000 ESI ceiling** (₹25,000 for a disabled IP), so **not ESI-covered**.
- **POW base** = full gross ₹75,000, for minimum-wage and equal-remuneration tests.

Three (or four) different numbers, one payslip, one component set. The model stores components + flags; the engine (§08) computes bases against the `EffectiveDatedRule` add-back percentage in force for the period. `CompensationAssignment` versions the whole binding so a mid-year CTC revision recomputes correctly for open/retro periods only.

**Balance-figure ordering.** `PayComponent.basis = balance-figure` (special allowance = CTC − Σ others) must evaluate **last** in the ordered structure; a percent-of-CTC component and a balance-figure component in the same structure form a resolution order that the structure's `component_order` encodes and the engine topologically respects (§08 FR-PAY-101).

**AC-DM-07** — *Given* a structure whose excluded components exceed 50% of total remuneration, *When* the PF/gratuity base is computed, *Then* the deemed-wages add-back equals `excluded − 0.5 × total_remuneration`, the figure is stamped with the `addback_percent` rule version used, and changing the CTC mid-year re-runs this only for open and explicitly-reopened periods, never silently for closed/filed periods.

**AC-DM-08** — *Given* a structure containing both a percent-of-CTC component and a balance-figure special allowance, *When* the structure is evaluated, *Then* the balance figure resolves after all other components and the sum of all `component_kind ∈ {earning, statutory-employer-cost, employer-cost}` equals CTC to the paisa.

#### 14.4.4 PayRun / PayrollResult / Payslip

`PayRun.type ∈ {regular, off_cycle, arrears, bonus, reimbursement, fnf}`; `PayRun.status` walks a lifecycle. `PayrollResult` holds every computed figure **with its rule lineage** (D4): each amount references the `rule_version` rows used, so the run is **replayable** (same inputs + versions → byte-identical) and **recomputable** (retro against the period's versions). `Payslip` is a rendered `Document`, never a source of truth — regeneration must reproduce the original from result + template version.

**PayRun lifecycle** (each transition emits an `AuditEvent`; transitions after `approved` are irreversible except via a superseding arrears/correction run):



**Figure 90. Payrun Lifecycle State Machine**

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    direction TB

    [*] --> draft: Run created for (establishment, period, type)

    draft --> inputs_locked: Freeze attendance / LOP / variable inputs
    inputs_locked --> draft: Unlock (audited)
    inputs_locked --> computed: Engine writes PayrollResult rows (rule_version bound)
    computed --> inputs_locked: Recompute
    computed --> reviewed: Maker sign-off
    reviewed --> computed: Send back
    reviewed --> approved: Checker sign-off (maker-checker, D4) - snapshot taken

    approved --> disbursed: NEFT / bank file generated, UTRs captured
    disbursed --> filed: Downstream Filings acknowledged
    filed --> closed: Period fully reconciled
    closed --> [*]

    approved --> arrears_run: Correct locked period (additive, D2)
    disbursed --> arrears_run
    filed --> arrears_run
    closed --> arrears_run
    arrears_run --> draft: New PayRun; applies_to_period vs run_in_period

    note left of draft
        PayRun.type = regular / off_cycle / arrears / bonus / reimbursement / fnf
        Every transition emits exactly one AuditEvent
    end note

    note right of approved
        Approved is the point of no return. Post-approval states are
        irreversible: no in-place edit. Correction is only via a new
        arrears/FnF run computed against the original period's rule
        versions, so the filed artefact stays byte-identical.
    end note

    state arrears_run: New arrears / correction / FnF run
```


| Status | Entered when | What is locked | Reversible? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `draft` | Run created for (establishment, period, type) | Nothing | Yes |
| `inputs_locked` | Attendance/LOP/variable inputs frozen | Attendance, variable pay, arrears feed | Yes (unlock, audited) |
| `computed` | Engine has produced all `PayrollResult` rows | Rule versions bound per result | Yes (recompute) |
| `reviewed` | Maker sign-off | Results | Yes (send back) |
| `approved` | Checker sign-off (maker-checker, D4) | Everything; snapshot taken | No — correction only via new run |
| `disbursed` | Bank/NEFT file generated, UTRs captured | Payment leg | No |
| `filed` | Downstream Filings acknowledged | Filing snapshots | No |
| `closed` | Period fully reconciled | All | No |

**Retro/arrears modelling:** an arrears run does not overwrite a closed period. It creates new `PayrollResult` rows tagged `applies_to_period = March, run_in_period = September`, computed against **March's** rule versions (D2). The delta flows into September's filings while the March filing artefact remains immutable. This is the schema expression of §08's I3. LOP-reversal, retro-CTC-revision, and corrigendum-driven recompute all use this same shape — there is exactly one mechanism for "change a closed period," and it is additive.

**Full-and-final settlement (FnF) — a distinct run type, not a special payslip.** `PayRun.type = fnf` composes components that never co-occur in a regular run: **leave encashment** (reads the derived `LeaveBalance`, §14.4.7), **gratuity payout** where eligibility is met (15/26 × last-drawn × completed years, ₹20L cap — Source: Payment of Gratuity Act / CoSS Ch. V **[Verified]**), **notice-period recovery** (a negative earning), **pending reimbursements**, and a **TDS true-up** against the full-year projection now that the exit date is known. FnF is where retention (§14.7) and the gratuity claim-tail begin: the run's outputs seed the post-exit retention clock. An FnF run can itself be reopened as an arrears run if a gratuity dispute later revalues service — again additive, never in-place.

**AC-DM-09** — *Given* an `approved` March run, *When* a September arrears run corrects a March input, *Then* new `PayrollResult` rows are created with `applies_to_period=March, run_in_period=September` computed against March-effective rule versions, the March `PayrollResult` and `Payslip` remain byte-identical, and the delta appears in September's ECR/PT/TDS filings.

**AC-DM-10** — *Given* a closed run and its `PayrollResult`, *When* the run is replayed with the recorded inputs and rule versions, *Then* every figure and the rendered `Payslip` PDF reproduce byte-for-byte, and any divergence is a P0 lineage defect.

#### 14.4.5 Filing — the unit of delivery

Because the whole product is "did the return go out and get accepted," `Filing` is the most instrumented entity in the model.

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `filing_type` | ECR, ESI_CONTRIB, PT_RETURN, LWF, TDS_138 (ex-24Q), FORM_130 (ex-16), STAT_REGISTER, etc. |
| `establishment_id`, `jurisdiction_id`, `period` | What/where/when this covers. |
| `format_version` | The government file-format version used (critical: **Form 138 replaces 24Q with a breaking layout**; Q1–Q3 v1.2 shipped 22 Jul 2026, correction structures 4 Aug 2026, **Q4 regular format did not yet exist** at Draft-1 date — the model must store which format a filing was built against). Source: §06, Income-Tax file-format notifications **[Verified]** |
| `input_snapshot_ref` | Immutable snapshot of the exact `PayrollResult`/master rows the artefact was built from (the N:M-via-snapshot in §14.3). |
| `generated_document_id` | The file/return artefact (Document), with `sha256`. |
| `status` | prepared → validated → submitted → acknowledged → accepted / rejected / revised. |
| `ack_no`, `ack_document_id`, `submitted_at` | Portal acknowledgement — the proof of on-time filing, the headline metric's evidence. |
| `rejection_reasons[]` | Structured, replayable rejection codes (e.g. Aadhaar–UAN mismatch, negative wage, IFSC invalid) so the fix loop is guided, not manual. |
| `challan_id` | The money leg (§14.4.6). |
| `due_date`, `filed_date`, `on_time` | Computed against the statutory calendar for that filing_type + jurisdiction. |
| `supersedes_filing_id` | For revised/correction returns — the lineage of the original → revision chain. |
| `nil_return_flag` | A due-but-zero return (no covered employees in period) is still a filing obligation and still evidences on-time compliance. |

**Filing lifecycle.** The status walk is a state machine with two terminal-but-reopenable states (`accepted`, `rejected`) and a `revised` fork that mints a new Filing linked by `supersedes_filing_id`.



**Figure 91. Filing Lifecycle State Machine**

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    direction LR
    [*] --> prepared: Filing minted from PayRun, input_snapshot_ref frozen, nil_return_flag if zero-liability
    prepared --> validated: local format checks pass, format_version bound
    validated --> prepared: validation error, fix inputs
    validated --> submitted: uploaded to portal
    submitted --> acknowledged: ack_no + submitted_at captured
    acknowledged --> accepted: portal accepts
    acknowledged --> rejected: structured rejection reasons e.g. AADHAAR_UAN_MISMATCH, IFSC invalid
    rejected --> validated: fix identifier state, re-validate against SAME input_snapshot_ref
    accepted --> revised: correction / arrears delta
    rejected --> revised: re-file as correction
    revised --> [*]: mints NEW Filing linked by supersedes_filing_id
    accepted --> [*]

    note right of accepted
        Terminal-but-reopenable.
        Evidence of on-time filing
        (ack_no) is preserved.
    end note
    note left of rejected
        Terminal-but-reopenable.
        Resubmit keeps original
        on_time where portal
        treats correction as on-time.
    end note
```


**Filing-type catalogue with statutory calendar** (due dates drive `due_date`/`on_time`; all are `EffectiveDatedRule`-backed, since due dates themselves change by notification):

| `filing_type` | Covers | Typical due date | Source | Confidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ECR` (EPF) | Electronic Challan-cum-Return | **15th** of following month | EPFO ECR procedure | **[Verified]** |
| `ESI_CONTRIB` | ESI contribution | **15th** of following month | ESI (Central) Rules | **[Verified]** |
| `PT_RETURN` | State PT return | **Per state** — monthly/annual; e.g. MH monthly by 30th/31st, some states annual | State PT Acts | **[Hypothesis]** exact per-state dates — validate against gazette per state; only Telangana verified (§20) |
| `TDS_138` | Quarterly TDS return (ex-24Q) | **Q1 31-Jul, Q2 31-Oct, Q3 31-Jan, Q4 31-May** (subject to Form 138 transition) | Income-Tax Rules | **[Verified]** (24Q dates) / format **[Hypothesis]** for Q4 (§14.10 item 5) |
| `FORM_130` | Annual TDS certificate (ex-Form 16) | **15-Jun** following FY (depends on Q4 annexure landing) | Income-Tax Rules | **[Verified]** date / **[Hypothesis]** Part B buildability — kill/confirm: Q4 format notification, §14.10 item 5 |
| `LWF` | State LWF | **Per state** — monthly/half-yearly/annual | State LWF Acts | **[Hypothesis]** per-state dates/rates — kill/confirm: gazette per state, §14.10 item 8; Frappe ships 14 states as parity (§07 **[Verified]**) |
| `STAT_REGISTER` | Four consolidated registers (electronic) | Maintained current; **5-yr retention** | Notified Rules under the Codes (§09) | **[Verified]** |

`STAT_REGISTER` filings cover the **four consolidated statutory registers** the Codes require in electronic form with **five-year retention** (Source: §09, notified Rules **[Verified]**) — the register is itself a Filing/Document with a retention class.

**Why `PayrollResult` carries the fields it does — the ECR is the forcing function.** The EPFO ECR is a member-wise text file, and each of its columns must be reproducible from a `PayrollResult` row plus the member's identifiers. This mapping is why the result cannot be a single net-pay number:

| ECR field | Sourced from | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| UAN, Member Name | `StatutoryIdentifier` (UAN, seeding_status) + `Person` | Name-match against UAN drives the seeding rejection loop |
| Gross Wages | `PayrollResult` POW/gross base | The broadest base |
| EPF Wages | `PayrollResult` PF base (post add-back, ceiling-applied) | Distinct from gross — the §14.4.3 example |
| EPS Wages | min(EPF wages, ₹15,000) | Capped separately |
| EDLI Wages | min(EPF wages, ₹15,000) | Capped separately |
| EE / ER EPF, EPS contributions | `PayrollResult` computed shares | Each stamped with rate `rule_id` |
| NCP Days | `AttendanceRecord`-derived non-contributory-period days | LOP/unpaid days reduce the base |
| Refund of Advances | ledger | Where applicable |

A single `wage` column cannot regenerate this file — which is the schema-level proof of §14.4.3's argument, expressed as a filing format.

**Rejection-loop worked example.** An ECR is `submitted`; EPFO returns a member-level rejection "Aadhaar not seeded / name mismatch." The `rejection_reasons[]` row is `{code: AADHAAR_UAN_MISMATCH, uan: …, member_id: …}`. The fix loop routes to the `StatutoryIdentifier.seeding_status` of exactly that member, not a manual hunt; once `seeding_status = verified`, the Filing can be re-`validated` and re-`submitted` **against the same `input_snapshot_ref`** (the wage data did not change, only the identifier state), preserving the on-time evidence chain.

**AC-DM-11** — *Given* a monthly regular run for a multi-state establishment, *When* the run reaches `filed`, *Then* the run has generated one `ECR`, one `ESI_CONTRIB`, one `PT_RETURN` per PT-registered state, `LWF` where due, and `TDS_138` at quarter-end, each with its own `due_date`/`on_time` and its own `input_snapshot_ref`.

**AC-DM-12** — *Given* a `rejected` Filing with a structured member-level reason, *When* the underlying identifier state is corrected and the return re-submitted, *Then* a new attempt is recorded under the same Filing with the same `input_snapshot_ref` if no wage figure changed, and `on_time` is evaluated against the *original* submission where the portal treats a corrected resubmission as on-time.

**AC-DM-13** — *Given* an establishment with covered employees but zero contributions in a period (all on LOP), *When* the readiness report runs, *Then* a `nil_return_flag` Filing is still created and its non-filing is flagged as a missed obligation, not suppressed.

#### 14.4.6 Challan / Payment

Separates the *return* (what is owed and to whom) from the *payment* (money moved). Holds PF/ESI/PT/TDS challan numbers, CRN (TDS Challan Reference Number), bank UTR, NEFT/host-to-host file reference, amount, and reconciliation state (`initiated → debited → reconciled → failed`). A nil return has a Filing with zero Challans; a challan can fail after a return is accepted, so the two lifecycles are **independent**.

**Why independent lifecycles matter (edge case).** For EPF, the ECR is *generated* first, which produces the challan amount; payment happens after. For TDS, the challan (CRN via the e-Pay Tax / TIN 2.0 flow) is often paid *before* the quarterly return is filed and is then *quoted* inside the return. So the model cannot assume a fixed ordering between Filing and Challan; it links them and reconciles, rather than nesting one inside the other. A `Challan` in `failed` after its `Filing` is `accepted` raises a reconciliation exception, not a re-filing.

**AC-DM-14** — *Given* an accepted TDS return quoting a challan CRN, *When* the bank later reports that challan as failed/reversed, *Then* the system raises a reconciliation exception linking Filing and Challan, and does not silently mark the period compliant.

#### 14.4.7 AttendanceRecord / Leave

`AttendanceRecord` is source-tagged (`source ∈ {device_adms, geo, mobile, kiosk, manual, import}`) because device-pushed punches (the ADMS/WDMS receiver, §09 **[Verified]**) arrive with a device serial and raw packet that must be retained for dispute. The **device serial + timestamp is the idempotency key** (§14.9) so a device retrying a POST does not double-count a punch.

Overtime is computed against notified limits — **8-hour normal day / 48-hour week, overtime at twice the normal rate, ceiling ≤144 OT hours per quarter per worker** (Source: notified Rules under the Codes **[Verified]**) — so the OT rate and caps are `EffectiveDatedRule` rows, not constants, with state S&E overlays possible.

**OT worked example.** A worker on ₹26/hour normal rate logs 30 OT hours in a month; running quarter OT already at 130 hours. OT pay = 30 × (2 × ₹26) = ₹1,560, **but** the model checks the quarter cap: 130 + 30 = 160 > 144, so 16 hours are `over_statutory_cap` — paid per policy but flagged on the register as exceeding the notified ceiling, a compliance exposure surfaced rather than hidden.

`LeaveBalance` is a *derived* running total; `LeaveTransaction` is the immutable ledger that moves it (`accrual, availment, encashment, lapse, carry_forward, opening_balance, adjustment`), so a balance can always be reconstructed and a mid-year policy change is a new effective-dated `LeavePolicy` version.

**Leave-ledger worked example (why balance is derived).** Employee opens FY with 6 days (imported as an `opening_balance` transaction, §14.4.10). Monthly accrual 1.5 days; takes 3 days in June; policy changes cap in September. Balance at any date = Σ transactions ≤ that date, so an auditor reconstructs "how did we get 11.5 days on 30-Sep" without trusting a mutable counter. Encashment at exit reads the derived balance and posts an `encashment` transaction feeding FnF.

**AC-DM-15** — *Given* a worker whose quarterly OT would exceed 144 hours, *When* the run computes OT, *Then* the excess hours are paid per policy but flagged `over_statutory_cap` on the attendance register and the readiness report, and the OT rate used is the `EffectiveDatedRule` version in force for the period.

**AC-DM-16** — *Given* a leave balance on any date, *When* it is queried, *Then* it equals the sum of `LeaveTransaction` rows up to that date, and no direct write to `LeaveBalance` is possible outside a transaction.

#### 14.4.8 Document

Every stored file carries `classification` (§14.5) and `retention_class` (§14.7), plus `sha256` (tamper-evidence for filed artefacts), `storage_region` (residency, §14.8) and `linked_entity`. Document types include appointment letter (**prescribed format, new since 21 Nov 2025** — Source: §06 **[Verified]**), wage slip, Form 130 (ex-16), Form 12BB proofs, KYC images, and register exports. A `Document` that is a filed artefact is **write-once**: its `sha256` is recorded at generation and any later read verifies against it, so a filed return cannot be silently swapped.

#### 14.4.9 Benefits / FBP entities (build the model now, defer monetisation)

Per §11, the benefits *data model* is v1 even though monetisation is deferred — retrofitting these into a shipped payroll engine is expensive, and they are the option value on the entire attach business. The entities:

| Entity | Purpose | India-specific note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FbpDeclaration` | Employee's flexible-benefit-plan allocation across components (meal, LTA, telephone, books, fuel) per FY | Meal perquisite limit ₹200/meal and gift/voucher ₹15,000/yr from 1 Apr 2026 (was ₹50 / ₹5,000) — a ~3.8× wallet expansion under the new regime; these limits are `EffectiveDatedRule` rows, not hardcoded (Source: §11 **[Verified]**). |
| `WalletConfig` / `WalletTransaction` | Wallet setup and spend ledger | Kept as a *ledger* so proof-of-spend and endorsement reconcile. |
| `ProofOfSpend` | Bill/proof against a wallet or exemption (HRA, LTA) | A `Document` (C2) with verification state; feeds Form 12BB proof state (§07 FR-CHR-017). |
| `Dependant` | Dependant records (spouse/children/parents) for group health + ESI dependant benefit | C2; drives ESI dependant eligibility and insurance endorsement. |
| `InsurancePolicy` / `Endorsement` | Group health/GPA/GTL policy + add/delete endorsement history | Model software PEPM and attach revenue as **two lines never blended** (§11 **[Verified]**); the schema keeps them structurally separate. |
| `NpsSubscription` | Corporate NPS (PRAN), employer/employee contribution | Feeds 80CCD(2) computation in TDS. |

**Design rule (D9 applied):** attach entities reference `Employment` and carry classification/retention like any other C1/C2 data, but they are **isolated from the payroll `PayrollResult` money-of-record** — a benefit wallet or an insurance endorsement never silently alters a filed statutory figure. This keeps the "two lines never blended" discipline enforceable at the schema level, not just in reporting.

**AC-DM-17** — *Given* a `WalletTransaction` or `Endorsement`, *When* it posts, *Then* it can adjust taxable-perquisite inputs for the *next* TDS computation via an explicit, audited feed, but it can never mutate an already-filed `PayrollResult` or `Filing` (D9).

#### 14.4.10 Migration / opening-balance entities (mid-year cutover is first-class)

Migration is **a first-class product surface, not a services task** (§18 **[Verified]**), and mid-year cutover is where churn-inducing friction concentrates. The data model therefore has dedicated entities so an imported employee lands *fileable*, not merely *stored*:

| Entity | Carries | Why it must exist as data |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MigrationBatch` | Source system (Tally/Zoho Payroll/Kredily/Frappe/spreadsheet), cutover date, mapping profile, validation report | Importers from Zoho/Kredily/Frappe are *acquisition infrastructure* (§18); the Tally import is the wedge. |
| `OpeningBalance` | YTD earnings, YTD TDS already deducted, PF/ESI contributions YTD, leave balances, gratuity accrual clock start | Without YTD-TDS-deducted, the first in-house Form 138/130 is wrong; without gratuity clock start, continuous-service is wrong. |
| `PreviousEmployerIncome` | Form 12B income + TDS from a mid-year joiner's prior employer | Required for correct annual TDS aggregation (§07 FR-CHR-018). |
| `CertificateContinuity` | Link from prior-system Form 16/130 and prior UAN/ESI IP continuity | UAN/ESI IP are portable; the migration must *continue* them, not mint new ones. |

**Cutover edge cases the model handles:**

1. **Mid-cycle investment declaration.** An employee whose investment declaration was in-flight in the old system — `FbpDeclaration` + `PreviousEmployerIncome` reconcile so proofs already submitted aren't re-demanded.
2. **YTD TDS already deducted.** Flows into `OpeningBalance` so the remaining-year TDS spreads correctly across the balance months and the annual Form 130 is continuous across two systems. **Worked:** an employee migrated on 1-Oct with ₹4,20,000 income and ₹80,000 TDS already deducted Apr–Sep, projected full-year income ₹9,00,000, full-year tax liability (new regime, after standard deduction and rebate as `EffectiveDatedRule` rows) computed at say ₹95,000. The engine subtracts the ₹80,000 `OpeningBalance` already withheld → ₹15,000 remaining, spread over Oct–Mar ≈ ₹2,500/month. It does **not** restart the year at ₹95,000/6, which would over-withhold by ₹80,000. A mid-year joiner from another employer instead brings `PreviousEmployerIncome` (Form 12B), which the engine *aggregates* into projected income before computing liability — a different path from `OpeningBalance` (same-employer continuity vs prior-employer aggregation), and conflating the two is a common competitor bug.
3. **Leave balances** import as an opening `LeaveTransaction` so the derived `LeaveBalance` is auditable from day one.
4. **Gratuity clock.** `OpeningBalance.gratuity_clock_start` carries the original DOJ so continuous-service is not reset to the migration date — a silent reset here would understate a future gratuity claim.

**AC-DM-18** — *Given* a mid-year `MigrationBatch` with `OpeningBalance.ytd_tds_deducted`, *When* the first in-house run computes TDS, *Then* the annual liability is reduced by the opening YTD figure and spread over remaining months, and the year-end Form 130 aggregates old-system + new-system withholding into one continuous certificate.

**AC-DM-19** — *Given* an imported employee with a prior `UAN`/`ESI IP`, *When* migration completes, *Then* the existing identifiers are continued (linkage state carried forward) and no new UAN/ESI IP is minted; a duplicate mint is a P0 migration defect.

#### 14.4.11 EffectiveDatedRule + Jurisdiction

Covered in depth in §14.6 — it is the entity that makes multi-state + retrospective payroll tractable.

#### 14.4.12 AuditEvent, ConsentGrant / DataPrincipalRequest, RetentionHold

`AuditEvent` is append-only, NTP-synced (NIC/NPL, per CERT-In — Source: CERT-In Directions 28.04.2022 **[Verified]**), retained **≥180 days within Indian jurisdiction** as ICT logs (and longer where a statutory register or dispute requires). It records `actor, role, action, entity, before, after, authority (statutory basis or approval), rule_version, ts_ntp`. Because a wrong payroll number is a legal problem (§08 **[Verified]**), every statutory/monetary write path emits exactly one `AuditEvent` and cannot commit without it.

`ConsentGrant` is deliberately **not** the lawful basis for core HR/payroll data — DPDP s.7(i) exempts employment-purpose processing from consent (§14.5). It exists only for optional/secondary purposes (voluntary benefits, marketing, references) and carries `purpose, granted_at, withdrawn_at, notice_version`.

`DataPrincipalRequest` (the DPR) is a small workflow entity: `type ∈ {access, correction, erasure, grievance, nomination}`, `raised_at`, `sla_due_at`, `status`, `reasoned_response_document_id`, `decision_basis`. Its lifecycle is `received → verified_identity → evaluated → responded (with reasoned response) → closed`; erasure requests fork into the §14.7 deletion engine.

`RetentionHold` is the override that pins rows against deletion during litigation/investigation/tax scrutiny: `scope (employee|payrun|establishment|tenant), reason, authority, placed_at, released_at`. While active it beats every erasure and every retention ceiling.

**AC-DM-20** — *Given* any write to a statutory or monetary field, *When* the transaction commits, *Then* exactly one `AuditEvent` with a valid NTP timestamp and stated `authority` is committed atomically with it; a write without its audit row is impossible.

#### 14.4.13 What the model deliberately does not store (the anti-patterns)

A data model is defined as much by its refusals as its tables. Each refusal below traces to a specific §PRD finding, and is a schema-level prohibition, not a guideline:

| Refusal | Why | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **No model-generated statutory or monetary figure** is ever persisted as truth | "No statutory or monetary figure may ever be model-generated" — a wrong payroll number is a legal problem. AI output is stored only as C3 draft/explanation, structurally separated from `PayrollResult`. | §08 **[Verified]** |
| **No raw biometric template** in the cloud store | Store the device's *matched employee-id + timestamp*, never the fingerprint/face template centrally, pending final DPDP Rules. | §14.5 **[Hypothesis]**; kill/confirm §14.10 item 2 |
| **No Aadhaar as a filing key**, and never the full value in a UI/log/export | Filing keys are UAN/ESI IP; Aadhaar is a masked seeding input only. | §14.5 **[Verified]** (Aadhaar Act) |
| **No single `wage` column** | Two-to-four concurrent wage bases exist on one payslip (§14.4.3). | §06.9 **[Verified]** |
| **No `current PT slab` reference on a computed result** | Results cite a *versioned* `rule_id`, so re-opening a later period cannot mutate a filed artefact. | §14.6, D2 **[Verified]** |
| **No hard `DELETE` from the app** | Deletion is the §14.7 policy engine's reasoned decision. | D8 **[Verified]** |
| **No blending of software money-of-record and attach/interchange money** | "Two lines never blended." | §11, D9 **[Verified]** |
| **No PF Member ID on `Person`** | It is establishment-scoped and changes on transfer; it lives on `Employment`. | §14.9 **[Verified]** |

These refusals are the mirror image of §20: the product declines to build hardware, a premium AI SKU, or interchange-monetised free HRMS at the *business* layer; the data model declines the corresponding *schema* shortcuts that would quietly re-open those doors.

#### 14.4.14 Cardinality / volume shape (a hint for §15 storage)

Rough per-tenant magnitudes at the 50–200-employee beachhead, to inform partitioning and hot/cold placement (§15) — order-of-magnitude, not commitments:

| Entity | Growth driver | Shape |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AttendanceRecord` | employees × working-days (× punches) | **Highest-volume** row; ~200 emp × ~25 days × 2 punches ≈ 10k rows/month → cold-tier candidate after the register-retention window |
| `AuditEvent` | every statutory/monetary write | High-volume, append-only, ≥180-day hot floor (CERT-In), then cold |
| `PayrollResult` | employees × runs (regular + off-cycle + arrears) | ~200–400 rows/month; hot for open + reopenable periods |
| `Filing` | ~4–8 per establishment per month | Low-volume, high-value, never cold (evidence) |
| `EffectiveDatedRule` | notifications, not tenant activity | Small, shared, reference; C4; cached |
| `LeaveTransaction` | accruals + events | Medium; append-only ledger |
| `Document` | filings + KYC + slips | Object-store; `storage_region` + `retention_class` drive lifecycle |

The design consequence: the two append-only high-volume ledgers (`AttendanceRecord`, `AuditEvent`) dominate storage but are cheap to tier; the low-volume high-value entities (`Filing`, `PayrollResult` lineage, `EffectiveDatedRule`) are what must never be lost or mutated. Storage economics and integrity requirements therefore point in *opposite* directions across the model — which §15 must resolve, not average away.

---

### 14.5 Data classification

Every field and document carries one of four classifications. The tag is not documentation — it **drives** encryption, masking, access scope, residency and retention, and it is enforced in code and auditable (D7).

| Class | Definition | Examples in this model | Controls the tag enforces |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **C1 · Regulated-Sensitive** | Data whose handling is dictated by a specific statute/regulator, or whose leak is a reportable incident | Aadhaar, bank account, PAN, salary/comp, PF/ESI contributions, TDS, biometric/attendance templates, health/disability status, ICT logs | Encryption at rest + in transit; field-level masking (Aadhaar last-4); access confined to named functions + audited; **India-resident storage**; CERT-In-reportable on breach; statutory retention floor |
| **C2 · Sensitive-Personal** | DPDP personal data whose exposure causes material harm | DOB, address, personal email/mobile (DPDP data-principal contact), dependant records, nominee, marital/gender where used for statutory variance | Encryption; role-scoped access; masking in support views; DPDP access/correction rights serviced |
| **C3 · Internal-Personal** | Ordinary personal/employment data | Name, designation, department, DOJ, employment type, org mappings | Tenant-isolated; role-based access; audited on statutory-impacting change |
| **C4 · Operational / Reference** | Non-personal config and reference | `EffectiveDatedRule` rows, `Jurisdiction`, structure templates, holiday calendars, device registry | Standard access controls; changes to rules are audited (they move money) |

**India-specific classification notes:**

- **Aadhaar is its own sub-regime, not "just PII."** Aadhaar Act + regulations restrict storage/display; the model masks to last-4 universally and treats a full read as an audited event. Storing Aadhaar as a filing key is prohibited — UAN/ESI IP are the filing keys; Aadhaar is only a *seeding* input. **[Verified]** (Source: Aadhaar Act 2016 & UIDAI regulations).
- **Salary and statutory contributions are C1**, not C3, because DPDP treats them as personal data *and* they are the substance of regulated filings; a comp leak is both a privacy and a competitive event.
- **Biometric/attendance templates are C1.** Where a device stores a fingerprint/face template, DPDP and general sensitivity push this to the strictest class; prefer storing the device's *matched employee-id + timestamp*, not raw biometric templates, in the cloud. **[Hypothesis]** — the exact status of on-device biometric templates under DPDP Rules is not yet fully settled; **validate** against final DPDP Rules before storing any template server-side; if in doubt, never store raw templates centrally. Kill/confirm: final DPDP Rules text + a privacy-counsel review (§14.10 item 2).
- **DPDP s.7(i) removes the consent requirement for employment-purpose processing** (Source: DPDP Act 2023 s.7(i) **[Verified]**) — so `ConsentGrant` is *not* the lawful basis for core HR/payroll data; it is used for optional/secondary purposes (marketing, voluntary benefits, references). The classification/retention regime, not consent, is the primary control surface for employee data. This is a genuine structural advantage over GDPR-bound designs (§17).
- **CERT-In-reportable classes are tagged.** An attack on the AI/ML subsystem is an explicitly reportable incident class (item (xx) of twenty, §17 **[Verified]**); C1 fields touched by any AI egress path additionally carry `ai_egress_class` (§14.8) so the reportable surface is enumerable, not guessed, at incident time (6-hour reporting clock).

#### 14.5.1 Access, roles & maker-checker (the schema side of D4)

Classification decides *what* is protected; the role model decides *who* touches it and *under what control*. The maker-checker separation (D4) is a data constraint — the checker on a `PayrollResult` or `Filing` transition must be a distinct actor from the maker — enforced in the transition, not left to process discipline.

| Role | Reads | Writes | Constraint |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Payroll maker** | C1–C3 within scope | proposes run inputs, computes | Cannot approve own run |
| **Payroll checker / approver** | C1–C3 within scope | approves `computed → approved`, `submitted` | Must ≠ maker on the same run (segregation) |
| **HR admin** | C2–C3 | master data, structures | Comp writes are statutory-impacting → audited |
| **Employee (self-service)** | own C1–C3 (masked where C1) | own declarations, proofs, DPRs | No cross-employee read |
| **CA / bureau (console)** | **read-only** across assigned clients | none on money-of-record | Read-only audit access (§18 **[Verified]**); switching clients is tenant-scoped |
| **Data Protection contact** | DPR queue + processing summary | reasoned responses | Named PoC per CERT-In before first paying customer (**[Verified]**) |
| **Support** | masked views only | none on statutory fields | Full-Aadhaar read is a separate audited KYC action, never a support default |

**AC-DM-29** — *Given* a run at `computed`, *When* an actor attempts to approve it, *Then* the approval is rejected if that actor is the run's maker (maker ≠ checker), and the rejection is auditable; segregation-of-duties cannot be bypassed by role stacking on one account without an explicit, logged override.

**AC-DM-30** — *Given* a CA console user assigned to a set of client tenants, *When* they open any client, *Then* all money-of-record entities are read-only, the view is scoped to exactly the assigned tenants, and no write to a `PayrollResult`/`Filing`/`Challan` is possible from the console.

---

### 14.6 Effective-dated & multi-state rule storage (the hardest schema)

Two problems collapse into one entity here: **rules change over time** (retrospective payroll) and **rules differ by place** (multi-state). `EffectiveDatedRule` solves both by being keyed on (`rule_type`, `jurisdiction_id`, `effective_from`) with bitemporal columns.

#### 14.6.1 Why bitemporal, not just effective-dated

A single `effective_from` answers "what rule applied to March." It cannot answer "what did we *believe* in April about March" — which is exactly what you need when a **corrigendum** amends a notification retrospectively. The PRD's own cautionary tale is the November 2026 EPF cliff, where a corrigendum (S.O. 3582(E), 12% re-notified retrospectively to 21.11.2025) inverted an earlier reading; verifying against the uncorrected S.O. 5319(E) reproduces the wrong answer (Source: §02 **[Verified]**). A bitemporal store lets us record the corrected rule *and* preserve what we filed under the old belief, with a clean recompute path.

| Column | Axis | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `effective_from`, `effective_to` | **Business time** | The period the rule legally governs. `effective_to = NULL` = still in force. |
| `recorded_at`, `superseded_at` | **Knowledge time** | When *we* recorded/replaced this belief. A corrigendum inserts a new row that supersedes the old belief without deleting it. |
| `source_ref`, `source_url`, `source_captured_at` | Provenance | Gazette/notification citation with URL + capture timestamp — enforces the PRD standing rule that no compliance claim ships without a captured source, and the "check for a corrigendum" step. **[Verified]** (Source: §02) |
| `corrigendum_of` | Lineage | Links a corrected rule to the notification it amends (the amendment-watcher, not just new-instrument-watcher, §06). |

#### 14.6.2 What lives as a rule row (not code)

| `rule_type` | Jurisdiction | Example values / variance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pf_wage_ceiling` | Central | ₹15,000 (basis cap); IW = no ceiling (Source: EPF Scheme; para 83 IW **[Verified]**) |
| `pf_rate`, `eps_rate`, `edli_rate`, `admin_charges` | Central | 12% employee; employer split EPS 8.33% (capped at ₹15,000 → ₹1,250) / EPF balance; EDLI 0.5%; admin 0.5% min ₹500; EPF Scheme 2026 re-notification **[Verified]** |
| `addback_percent` | Central | 50%, "or such other per cent as may be notified" — the standing variable that alone justifies this entity (Source: Code on Wages s.2(y) **[Verified]**) |
| `esi_wage_ceiling`, `esi_rate_ee`, `esi_rate_er` | Central | ₹21,000 (₹25,000 disabled); 0.75% / 3.25% (Source: ESI (Central) Rules **[Verified]**) |
| `esi_contribution_period` | Central | Apr–Sep, Oct–Mar; drives the mid-period ceiling-crossing rule (§14.4.2) (Source: ESI (Central) Rules Rule 50 **[Verified]**) |
| `pt_slab` | **Per state** | MH, KA, WB, TN, TS… each a different slab table; **gender variants** (some states exempt/lower women below a threshold); some states have a Feb/annual differential (e.g. Maharashtra's Feb ₹300). **[Hypothesis]** full all-state PT dataset — only **Telangana verified** across two research rounds; aggregator data is disputed and a widely-cited 2026 table reproduces a superseded structure. **Validate/kill:** gazette-sourced dataset per state (levy y/n, slabs, gender, periodicity, dates) before claiming multi-state PT; ship beachhead states in v1, all-states in v2 (Source: §07, §20). |
| `lwf_schedule` | **Per state** | Levy y/n, employee/employer share, periodicity (monthly/half-yearly/annual), due months. Frappe HR ships LWF across 14 states free — parity, not differentiation (Source: §07 **[Verified]**). |
| `ot_rate`, `ot_quarter_cap`, `normal_hours` | Central + state overlays | 2× rate, 144 hrs/quarter, 8-hr day / 48-hr week (Source: notified Rules **[Verified]**); state S&E overlays possible. |
| `tds_slab`, `regime_params`, `surcharge`, `cess`, `standard_deduction`, `rebate_87a` | Central | New regime default AY 2024-25+; annual Budget changes (Source: Finance Act **[Verified]**). Values themselves are `EffectiveDatedRule` rows so a Budget is a data load, not a deploy. |
| `gratuity_params` | Central | 15/26 formula, ₹20L cap, 5-yr / 240-day eligibility, death/disablement waiver (Source: Payment of Gratuity Act / CoSS Ch. V **[Verified]**). |
| `meal_perq_limit`, `gift_voucher_limit` | Central | ₹200/meal, ₹15,000/yr from 1 Apr 2026 (was ₹50 / ₹5,000) — a ~3.8× wallet expansion (Source: §11 **[Verified]**). |
| `filing_due_date` | Central + state | Per `filing_type` + jurisdiction; drives `Filing.due_date`/`on_time` (§14.4.5). |
| `statutory_register_spec` | Central + state | The four consolidated registers' fields + 5-yr retention (Source: §09 **[Verified]**). |

#### 14.6.3 Rule resolution algorithm (deterministic)

For any computation of `rule_type R` for `establishment E` in `period P`, as-known-at time `T`:

1. Resolve `E.jurisdiction_id` (work-location state) → `J`.
2. Select rows where `rule_type = R AND jurisdiction ∈ {J, Central}` AND `effective_from ≤ P.end AND (effective_to IS NULL OR effective_to ≥ P.start)` AND `recorded_at ≤ T AND (superseded_at IS NULL OR superseded_at > T)`.
3. Prefer the **most specific jurisdiction** (state overrides Central where both exist and the state legislates the field, e.g. PT/LWF); Central applies where no state row exists.
4. Record the selected `rule_id`(s) on the `PayrollResult` lineage (D4).
5. A **retro run** sets `T = now` but `P = the corrected period`, so it picks up corrigenda (latest knowledge) applied to the historical business period — the desired behaviour.



**Figure 92. Rule Resolution Flow**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    START(["Resolve rule_type R for establishment E,<br/>period P, as-known-at time T"]) --> J["Resolve E.jurisdiction_id<br/>&#40;work-location state&#41; &rarr; J"]

    J --> RUN{"Retro / corrigendum<br/>run?"}
    RUN -->|"Yes"| RETRO["Set T = now, keep P = corrected period<br/>&rarr; picks up latest knowledge<br/>&#40;corrigenda&#41; for the historical period"]
    RUN -->|"No"| NORMAL["T = as-of time,<br/>P = the run period"]

    RETRO --> SELECT
    NORMAL --> SELECT

    SELECT["Select EffectiveDatedRule rows where:<br/>rule_type = R<br/>AND jurisdiction &isin; &#123;J, Central&#125;<br/>AND effective_from &le; P.end<br/>AND &#40;effective_to IS NULL OR effective_to &ge; P.start&#41; &nbsp;&#40;business time&#41;<br/>AND recorded_at &le; T<br/>AND &#40;superseded_at IS NULL OR superseded_at &gt; T&#41; &nbsp;&#40;knowledge time&#41;"] --> SPEC{"State row exists for J<br/>and state legislates<br/>this field?<br/>&#40;PT / LWF / S&amp;E&#41;"}

    SPEC -->|"Yes: state row"| STATEROW["Use most-specific-jurisdiction row<br/>&#40;state overrides Central&#41;"]
    SPEC -->|"No state row"| CENTRALROW["Use Central row<br/>&#40;PF / ESI / TDS / gratuity&#41;"]

    STATEROW --> REG{"Establishment has<br/>registration in J?<br/>&#40;e.g. pt_reg_no&#41;"}
    REG -->|"Yes"| RESOLVED
    REG -->|"No"| PENDING["Return liability tagged<br/>registration_pending<br/>&rarr; readiness report flags<br/>'due, no registration'<br/>&#40;never a zero-liability line&#41;"]

    CENTRALROW --> RESOLVED

    PENDING --> RESOLVED["Selected rule_id&#40;s&#41; resolved"]
    RESOLVED --> LINEAGE["Record selected rule_id&#40;s&#41;<br/>on PayrollResult lineage &#40;D4&#41;<br/>&rarr; result is replayable &amp; auditable"]
    LINEAGE --> DONE(["Rule version bound to the computed figure"])
```


**Worked multi-state example.** A tenant with staff in Maharashtra, Karnataka and a new hire in Assam. For September PT: MH row (slab with Feb-differential flagged for Feb only), KA row (its slab), Assam — if the employer has no Assam PT registration, resolution returns liability with `registration_pending`, surfacing "PT due, no registration" on the readiness report rather than filing wrong. Central rules (PF/ESI/TDS) resolve identically for all three; only PT/LWF/S&E diverge — which is precisely why those three rule_types are state-scoped and the rest are Central.

**AC-DM-21** — *Given* a computation of `pt_slab` for an establishment in a PT-levying state and of `pf_rate` for the same establishment, *When* rule resolution runs, *Then* `pt_slab` resolves to the state-specific row (most-specific-jurisdiction wins) and `pf_rate` resolves to the Central row (no state row exists), and both `rule_id`s are recorded on the result lineage.

#### 14.6.4 Worked bitemporal timeline — the corrigendum case

This is the scenario the whole bitemporal design exists for. Suppose the PF add-back percentage for FY2025-26 is believed to be 50%, then a corrigendum on 15-Sep-2026 amends it retrospectively (illustrative — the *mechanism*, not a real notification):

| Event (knowledge time) | `EffectiveDatedRule` rows for `addback_percent` | What a March pay run computes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Apr-2026: March run executed | Row A: 50%, `effective_from`=01-Apr-2025, `effective_to`=NULL, `recorded_at`=Apr-2026 | 50% — filed under Row A; `PayrollResult` lineage cites Row A |
| Sep-2026: corrigendum recorded | Row A: `superseded_at`=15-Sep-2026; **Row B**: 47%, `effective_from`=01-Apr-2025, `recorded_at`=15-Sep-2026, `corrigendum_of`=Row A | — (existing March filing untouched) |
| Sep-2026: retro run for March, `T=now` | Resolution picks **Row B** (latest knowledge, historical business period) | 47% — an arrears/correction `PayrollResult` (`applies_to_period`=March, `run_in_period`=Sep) and a **revised Filing** with `supersedes_filing_id` = the original March filing |



**Figure 93. Bitemporal Timeline**

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph BT["BUSINESS TIME (fixed): addback_percent governs FY2025-26, effective_from = 01-Apr-2025"]
      direction TB
      P["March period<br/>the business time never moves"]
    end

    subgraph K1["KNOWLEDGE TIME - as recorded Apr-2026"]
      A["Row A: addback = 50%<br/>effective_from = 01-Apr-2025<br/>effective_to = NULL<br/>recorded_at = Apr-2026"]
    end

    subgraph K2["KNOWLEDGE TIME - as recorded 15-Sep-2026 (corrigendum)"]
      A2["Row A: 50%<br/>superseded_at = 15-Sep-2026<br/>(not deleted, belief preserved)"]
      B["Row B: addback = 47%<br/>effective_from = 01-Apr-2025<br/>recorded_at = 15-Sep-2026<br/>corrigendum_of = Row A"]
    end

    P --> A
    A -->|"corrigendum recorded, supersedes prior belief"| A2
    A2 --> B

    A ==>|"query as-known-in-Apr / March run"| R1["Resolution picks Row A -> 50%<br/>PayrollResult lineage cites Row A"]
    R1 --> F1["Original March Filing<br/>preserved byte-identical"]

    B ==>|"retro run for March, T = now<br/>latest knowledge, historical period"| R2["Resolution picks Row B -> 47%<br/>arrears PayrollResult<br/>applies_to_period=March, run_in_period=Sep"]
    R2 --> F2["Revised Filing"]

    F2 -.->|"supersedes_filing_id"| F1

    AC["Both answers simultaneously reproducible from one store (AC-DM-22)"]
    F1 --- AC
    F2 --- AC
```


The original March artefact is preserved exactly as filed (what we believed then); the correction is a new, linked artefact (what we know now). A watcher keyed only to *new notifications* would miss the corrigendum — the model requires `corrigendum_of` and an **amendment**-watcher, per §06 **[Verified]**.

**AC-DM-22** — *Given* Row A (50%) recorded in April and Row B (47%, `corrigendum_of`=A) recorded in September, *When* the original March filing is read as-known-in-April and a September retro run is executed, *Then* the April read returns 50% and cites Row A, the September retro returns 47% and cites Row B, and both are simultaneously reproducible from the store.

```
Tenant 1─N Employer 1─N Establishment N─1 Jurisdiction 1─N EffectiveDatedRule
Person(Employee) 1─N Employment N─1 Establishment
Employment 1─N StatutoryIdentifier
Employment 1─N EligibilityState        (effective-dated)
Employment 1─N CompensationAssignment  (effective-dated) N─1 CompensationStructure 1─N PayComponent
Establishment 1─N PayRun 1─N PayrollResult 1─1 Payslip(Document)
PayrollResult N─M EffectiveDatedRule   (lineage / recorded)
PayRun 1─N Filing 1─0..N Challan/Payment
Filing N─M PayrollResult (via input_snapshot)  ;  Filing 1─N Document  ;  Filing ─self supersedes
Employment 1─N AttendanceRecord  ;  Employment 1─N LeaveTransaction ─derives─ LeaveBalance
Employment 1─N FbpDeclaration / Dependant / NpsSubscription / InsuranceEndorsement
MigrationBatch 1─N OpeningBalance / PreviousEmployerIncome ─→ Employment
AuditEvent N─1 (polymorphic)  ;  RetentionHold N─M (polymorphic)  ;  DataPrincipalRequest N─1 Person
```
