#### 15.5.1 Integration classes and contracts

| Integration | Direction | Contract / protocol | Failure mode | Fallback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Biometric devices (eSSL, ZKTeco)** | Inbound (device → us) | **ADMS/WDMS push**: terminal HTTP-POSTs punch packets to a tenant-scoped URL. No middleware, no static IP, no port-forwarding — the best-evidenced call in the corpus (§09 [Verified]). | Device offline / firmware quirk / clock drift | Buffer-and-replay when the device reconnects; the legacy port-4370 pull protocol as a last resort for pre-ADMS firmware. Long-tail brands via the paid connector market (~$345 one-time / $588-yr, §09 [Verified]) — do not build in-house for SDK-bound brands. |
| **Tally** | Inbound (import) + outbound (accounting) | Data-import path is **P0** — it is the incumbent and the import is the wedge (§18). | Malformed export / version drift | Guided import with validation and a mapping preview; never a silent partial import. |
| **Banks — salary disbursement** | Outbound | NEFT/host-to-host salary files per bank's format; reconciliation of success/failure per beneficiary. | Beneficiary reject / file reject / bank downtime | Per-beneficiary retry, partial-batch handling, and a reconciliation queue — a bank reject blocks a *disbursement line*, never the pay run. |
| **EPFO (ECR)** | Outbound | ECR text file to the EPFO portal; challan generation; acknowledgment capture. | Portal down at month-end / format-version change | Queue the submission, retry with backoff, surface status in the filing cockpit; the *file* is generated and validated locally even if the portal is unreachable. |
| **ESIC** | Outbound | ESI contribution file + challan. | Portal down / **Nov-2026 regime change unresolved** | Same queue-and-retry; the engine accepts the new ESI effective-date the moment ESIC notifies (§15.4.2). |
| **TRACES / CBDT (TDS)** | Outbound | Form 138 (ex-24Q) via RPU/FVU-validated file; Form 130 (ex-Form 16) issuance. | **Q4 format not yet published** (§06) | Q1–Q3 supported on the shipped v1.2 layout; Q4 gated and flagged in the calendar until the format lands. |
| **State PT portals** | Outbound | Per-state PT return + payment; cadence varies by state. | 15+ state portals, uneven APIs, many manual | Where no API exists, generate the exact portal-format file/return for manual upload; never claim automated filing where the state offers no channel. |
| **Job boards (Naukri, LinkedIn, foundit, apna, Indeed)** | Outbound (post) + inbound (application sync) | Multi-post from one requisition; application ingest + dedup. **Inbound-only** — Info Edge does not licence Resdex search to third-party ATS (§10 [Verified]). | API limits / no partner API (Naukri) | "Bring your own job-board contract"; **scraping is forbidden** in architecture and sales collateral (§10 [Verified] legal exposure). LinkedIn partner integration done properly and early. |
| **Accounting / HRIS migration** | Inbound | Importers from Zoho Payroll, Kredily, Frappe — **acquisition infrastructure, not integrations** (§18). | Mid-year cutover complexity | Migration is a first-class product surface (§18): opening balances, YTD earnings, TDS-already-deducted, previous-employer income, UAN/IP continuity, leave/gratuity continuity. |

#### 15.5.2 The device compatibility matrix as an architectural artefact

Device integration effort is currently **unsized** — the "85–98% success" figure was
retracted marketing (§09 [Killed]) and needs a hardware spike. Architecturally, the response
is to ship a **public, model-level device compatibility matrix and a self-serve verification
tool** (§09 highest-leverage cheap artefact): a tenant points a device at a test endpoint and
sees whether its punches arrive and parse, *before* a sales call. This turns an unsized risk
into a self-service check and neutralises a deal-gating question no incumbent answers.

#### 15.5.3 Idempotency and reconciliation as first-class

Every outbound integration is **idempotent and reconciled**: a resubmitted ECR or salary
file cannot double-file or double-pay; every submission has a client-side idempotency key and
a reconciliation record that pairs "what we sent" with "what the portal/bank acknowledged."
This is the same discipline the MCP write tools require (§12: idempotent, audited,
approval-gated) — one mechanism, two consumers.

#### 15.5.4 The compliance calendar is scheduler data, not a static list

Because the filing is the unit of delivery, the due-date calendar is a first-class,
effective-dated dataset the scheduler (§15.2.6) drives — it clusters the month-end
concurrency spike (§15.3.5) and it is the surface the CA console renders per client
(§15.2.2). The recurring statutory cadence, as of Draft 1 (each entry a rule datum subject
to the certification pipeline, not a hardcoded constant):

| Filing | Cadence | Statutory due date | Source cue |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **EPF ECR + challan** | Monthly | 15th of following month | EPF Scheme 2026, para 38 (Source: S.O. 3582(E)) |
| **ESI contribution + challan** | Monthly | 15th of following month | ESI (Central) Rules, Rule 31 |
| **PT return + payment** | Per-state (monthly / half-yearly / annual) | Varies — e.g. Maharashtra monthly by end of month; Karnataka monthly by 20th | Respective State PT Acts [Hypothesis on per-state dates — *kill:* replace with gazette-verified all-state dataset, §20 gap] |
| **LWF deduction + remittance** | Per-state (half-yearly / annual) | Varies — e.g. Maharashtra 15 Jul / 15 Jan; Karnataka by 15 Jan | State LWF Acts [Hypothesis on dates — same kill as PT] |
| **TDS payment (challan)** | Monthly | 7th of following month (Apr–Feb); 30 Apr for March | Income-tax Rules, Rule 30 |
| **TDS return (Form 138, ex-24Q)** | Quarterly | Q1 31 Jul · Q2 31 Oct · Q3 31 Jan · Q4 31 May | Income-tax Rules, Rule 31A (Form-138 transition, §06) |
| **Form 130 (ex-Form 16)** | Annual | 15 Jun | Income-tax Rules, Rule 31 |
| **Gratuity / LWF / statutory registers refresh** | Event-/period-driven | On separation / period close; 5-yr retention | Code on Social Security; Code on Wages register rules |

The scheduler pre-provisions capacity around the 7th and 15th clusters (the two heaviest
days) and raises a filing-at-risk alert a configurable lead time before each due date. A
per-state PT/LWF date that the certified dataset does not yet cover surfaces as a *gap in the
calendar*, consistent with AC-R5 — never a silently-missing obligation.

---

### 15.6 Event and audit backbone

The audit backbone is not observability plumbing added at the end; per principle 5 **it is
the write path** for every state-changing action. This is driven by three forces: statutory
proof (a filing must be defensible years later), CERT-In log retention, and the AI trust
boundary (every AI-assisted action must be attributable).

#### 15.6.1 What emits events

Every state change emits an immutable event carrying `tenant_id`, `actor` (human, machine, or
AI-agent, with the CA dual-identity where applicable), `reason`, `rule_versions_applied`
(where statutory), `request_id`, and a hash chain to the prior event for tamper-evidence:

- **Filing lifecycle** — assembled, validated, generated, submitted, acknowledged, revised.
  This is the primary event stream, because the filing is the unit of delivery.
- **Rule changes** — every rule-version promotion, with citation and the certification result.
- **Approvals and human-in-loop gates** — every statutory action a human confirmed, and every
  AI proposal a human accepted or rejected (§12).
- **Pay-run lifecycle** — run opened, computed, reviewed, approved, disbursed.
- **Access and identity** — grants, CA cross-tenant access, MCP tool invocations.

#### 15.6.2 Event sourcing where correctness demands replay

The **filing orchestrator and payroll engine are event-sourced**: their current state is a
fold over their event history, so any pay run or filing can be *replayed* to reconstruct
exactly how a number was reached, against which rule versions, by whom. This is what makes
"retrospectively recomputable with an audit trail" (§08 [Verified]) a structural property
rather than a reporting feature. Services that do not compute statutory truth (notifications,
attendance capture) use ordinary state with an audit log — event sourcing is applied where it
earns its complexity, not everywhere.

#### 15.6.3 CERT-In and DPDP obligations baked in

These bind **from day one, not at enterprise scale** (§17 [Verified]):

| Obligation | Architectural consequence | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **6-hour incident reporting** for every body corporate | The event backbone feeds an incident-detection path; a named CERT-In point of contact before the first paying customer. | Source: CERT-In Directions under s.70B(6) IT Act, No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In, 28 Apr 2022, Direction (ii) [Verified] |
| **180 days of ICT logs retained within Indian jurisdiction** | Log storage is residency-pinned to India regardless of the tenant's inference residency choice; retention is enforced, not best-effort. | Source: CERT-In Directions, 28 Apr 2022, Direction (iv) [Verified] |
| **Clock sync to NIC/NPL NTP** | All event timestamps synced to NIC/NPL NTP servers — non-trivial for distributed services and for reconciling device clock drift against server time. | Source: CERT-In Directions, 28 Apr 2022, Direction (iii) [Verified] |
| **Attacks on AI/ML systems are a reportable incident class** | The AI orchestrator's events are in scope for incident reporting; an AI-first product *enlarges* the reportable surface, so the AI edge is instrumented for anomaly detection from v1. | Source: CERT-In Directions Annexure I, reportable incident types (incl. attacks on applications/AI-ML systems) [Verified] |
| **DPDP retention limits** | Retention is per data class and enforced by the backbone (5-yr statutory registers vs shorter for transient data); erasure honours statutory-retention overrides. Employer processing needs no employee consent for employment purposes. | Source: DPDP Act 2023, s.7(i) (legitimate use) and s.8(7) (erasure on purpose completion, subject to legal-retention overrides) [Verified] |

#### 15.6.4 Cost attribution rides the event stream

Because every request carries `cost_context` (§15.2.3) and every AI action emits an event,
per-tenant/user/agent/model cost attribution (§13 [Verified], P0) is a *consumer of the event
stream*, not a parallel accounting system. Built from v1 while AI is free, it feeds gateway
budget enforcement (§15.3.5) and pricing (§18). The 52.7× model-cost spread (§13) means this
attribution is the input to the margin decision, so it must be trustworthy from the first
paying customer.

---

### 15.7 Deployment, residency and provider abstraction

Residency is the segment-specific procurement gate that cannot be deferred (§17 synthesis:
*a segment-specific gate, not a general-market differentiator*). The architecture treats it
as configuration, delivered by two abstractions that are one piece of work serving two
constraints (§17 [Verified]).

#### 15.7.1 Two residency guarantees, tracked separately

Buyers ask about both and they are different (§17 [Verified]):

- **Data-at-rest residency** — where tenant data physically lives. India-only for regulated
  tenants; the default plane is India regardless.
- **In-country inference residency** — where AI inference executes. A different guarantee from
  data-at-rest, and provider-dependent.

The tenant's **residency profile** captures both independently and the gateway + model router
enforce them per request.

#### 15.7.2 The provider matrix (must be maintained, not memorised)

**[Verified]** — Residency is a per-provider matrix, and the specific cells below are as of
Draft 1 and must be re-verified per procurement (§13):

| Provider | Data-at-rest India | In-country inference India |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OpenAI | Yes (India data-at-rest) | Via Bedrock for in-country inference |
| Anthropic | No | No — US-only immutable workspace geo |
| Vertex (Google) | India region available | India region available |
| Sarvam | **Unverified** — must not be relied on until verified; prices natively in INR (FX hedge, §13) | Unverified |

Requirement (§13 [Verified]): **≥3 interchangeable backends with residency selectable per
tenant.** The model router (§15.2.5) is where this is enforced — a tenant pinned to India-only
inference simply cannot be routed to an out-of-region backend, and the router re-points task
classes without a deploy when a provider changes price (Gemini 3.x Flash 2× on 2027-01-01 is
the *base case*, §13) or residency posture.

#### 15.7.3 Deployment topology

| Topology | Who | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Shared multi-tenant plane, India region** | Default — the whole beachhead | Pool-with-partition (§15.3). Serverless-first: serverless beats dedicated H100 by ~74× at real utilisation (§20 non-goal: never self-host *for cost*). |
| **Dedicated data plane, India region** | Named regulated accounts | Silo escape hatch; same code, isolated data + inference. |
| **Self-hosted / customer VPC** | Named regulated accounts only, **as a priced compliance SKU** | Never for cost (§20). RBI right-to-audit-by-RBI-itself and IRDAI records-in-Indian-DCs can force this contractually. |

#### 15.7.4 The ISO 27001 seasoning clock is an architecture input

Certification carries a **one-year seasoning clock** on top of 3–6 months acquisition — Indian
Bank requires ISO 27001:2022 held for ≥1 year before RFP publication (§04 [Verified]).
Consequence for month zero: **start ISO 27001 immediately** even with no customer asking; to
be useful at month 18 it must be in hand by ~month 6. This shapes the architecture now because
the controls it certifies (access logging, encryption-at-rest, incident response, the audit
backbone) must be *designed in from v1*, not retrofitted for the audit. "The cheapest year you
will ever buy" (§04).

---

### 15.8 End-to-end data flows (worked)

Three flows tie the components together. Each names the human-in-loop gate, the audit event,
and the failure fallback.

#### 15.8.1 A biometric punch → payroll input

1. Shop-floor terminal **HTTP-POSTs** a punch packet to its tenant-scoped ADMS/WDMS URL
   (§15.5). No middleware.
2. Gateway resolves the tenant from the URL/credential, injects context, rate-limits.
3. Attendance service **dedups and validates** the punch (clock-drift correction against
   NIC/NPL-synced server time, §15.6.3), maps it to the employee's shift/roster.
4. Notified OT/leave rules apply (8h/48h, 2× OT, 144-hr/qtr ceiling) — resolved via the rules
   engine, effective-dated (§15.4).
5. Result becomes a **payroll input** for the period; an event is emitted.
   **Fallback:** device offline → buffer-and-replay on reconnect; the pay run never blocks on
   a single device.

#### 15.8.2 A monthly pay run → filings (the core loop)



**Figure 99. Pay Run To Filing Loop**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["1. Inputs assembled<br/>attendance, mid-period changes,<br/>investment declarations, arrears"]

    subgraph CORE["Deterministic core (no AI in the number path)"]
        B["2. Payroll engine computes gross-to-net<br/>per employee, per component<br/>two concurrent wage bases<br/>stamps rule versions into trace"]
        RE{{"Statutory-rules engine<br/>effective-dated, period-pinned versions"}}
    end

    subgraph EDGE["Probabilistic edge (explain / route, no privileged compute)"]
        C["3. AI reconcile (optional)<br/>flags anomalies vs prior period<br/>explains and routes, never changes a number"]
    end

    D{"4. Human-in-loop gate<br/>payroll admin approves run"}
    E["5. Disbursement<br/>bank host-to-host salary file<br/>per-beneficiary reconciliation"]
    F["6. Filing orchestrator assembles filings<br/>ECR / ESI challan / PT return / Form 138<br/>validate locally: RPU / FVU / ECR fixtures"]
    G["7. Submit to EPFO / ESIC / TRACES / state PT<br/>capture acknowledgment<br/>archive artefacts, 5-yr retention"]

    A --> B
    B <-->|"resolve version for period"| RE
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D -->|approved| E
    D -->|"rejected, rework"| B
    E --> F
    F -->|"valid locally, then touch portal"| G
    G -.->|"next period, monthly cadence"| A

    E -.->|"beneficiary reject"| Ebf["Fallback: retry per beneficiary,<br/>run stays approved"]
    Ebf -.-> E
    G -.->|"portal down"| Gbf["Fallback: queue-and-retry with backoff,<br/>file valid locally,<br/>cockpit shows generated, awaiting portal"]
    Gbf -.-> G

    A -.-> EV
    B -.-> EV
    C -.-> EV
    D -.-> EV
    E -.-> EV
    F -.-> EV
    G -.-> EV
    EV[("8. Event / audit stream (filing-first)<br/>every step emits an immutable event<br/>run replayable end to end")]
```


1. **Inputs assembled:** attendance, mid-period changes, investment declarations, arrears.
2. **Payroll engine computes** gross-to-net per employee, invoking the rules engine per
   component; produces the two concurrent wage bases; stamps rule versions into the
   computation trace (§15.4.3). Deterministic — no AI in the number path.
3. **AI reconcile (optional, edge):** the AI orchestrator flags anomalies vs prior period
   (a component that jumped, a missing declaration) — it *explains and routes*, it does not
   change a number (§12). Human reviews.
4. **Human-in-loop approval gate:** payroll admin approves the run. Event emitted with actor
   and reason.
5. **Disbursement:** bank host-to-host salary file generated; per-beneficiary reconciliation.
   **Fallback:** partial rejects retried per beneficiary; run stays approved.
6. **Filing orchestrator** turns the approved run + period data into ECR / ESI challan / PT
   return / Form 138; validates locally (RPU/FVU/ECR-validator fixtures, §15.4.5) *before*
   the portal is touched.
7. **Submission** to EPFO/ESIC/TRACES/state PT; acknowledgment captured; artefacts archived
   with 5-year retention.
   **Fallback:** portal down → queue-and-retry with backoff; the file exists and is valid
   locally; the cockpit shows "generated, awaiting portal." A portal outage never blocks a
   pay run — it delays a *submission* (principle 7).
8. **Every step is an event** on the filing stream; the run is replayable end to end.

#### 15.8.3 A retrospective correction (the case that justifies the whole design)

1. A corrigendum lands, dated back, changing (say) the PT slab for a state effective a past
   period. The **watcher catches the corrigendum** (not just new instruments, §15.4.5).
2. Statutory analyst verifies against primary source, drafts a new rule version with a
   **retro-effective flag** and citation; certification fixtures pass; pack promoted.
3. The pipeline **enqueues affected past periods** for recompute. The payroll engine replays
   those periods against the *corrected* version for that period (§15.4.3), producing revised
   numbers and a diff.
4. Where a filing was already submitted against the old version, the filing orchestrator
   generates a **revised return** and flags it in the compliance calendar.
5. Human-in-loop approves the corrected filings; full audit trail links original → corrigendum
   → recompute → revised filing.

This flow is the concrete reason effective-dating, event sourcing, the corrigendum-aware
watcher and the certification pipeline all exist. It is also exactly the scenario that
inverted the Nov-2026 analysis when done by hand (§02) — the architecture's job is to make it
mechanical and auditable instead of a research accident.

---

### 15.9 Build sequencing (architecture, mapped to phases)

Per the phasing rule (memory: treat "all of it" as vision, not v1). This orders *architectural
capability*, not features (features are §05.5).

| Phase | Architecture delivered | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **v1 (beachhead 20–200)** | Gateway + tenant router; pool-with-partition multi-tenancy (India plane); statutory-rules engine with effective-dating + certification pipeline; payroll engine (event-sourced) + filing orchestrator; ADMS/WDMS push receiver; Tally import; bank H2H; EPFO/ESIC/TRACES/PT integrations; event/audit backbone; CERT-In log retention + NTP; cost attribution; model router with ≥3 backends; ISO 27001 controls designed in. | Everything needed to *file*, isolate tenants, and stay auditable. AI is architecture/COGS, bundled (§13). |
| **v2 (expansion 200–2,000)** | Cohort sharding of the pool if pressure warrants (§15.3.5); CA cross-tenant grant model matured; talent integrations (job boards, LinkedIn partner); richer MCP tool surface. | Same product shape, more tenants and larger tenants; CA channel scaled *if* validated (§20 Q5). |
| **Vision (enterprise, benefits, full AI)** | Silo/dedicated + self-host compliance SKU; per-provider residency matrix hardened for regulated procurement (RBI/IRDAI/SBI); benefits-attach data model activated (built in v1, monetised later, §11). | Enterprise procurement is arithmetically closed for ~3 years (§01/§04); the ISO seasoning clock started at month 0 makes month-18 bids possible. |

---

### 15.10 Open architecture questions and hypotheses

Consistent with the PRD's standing rule that surviving hypotheses carry a kill/validation
criterion:

| # | Hypothesis | Validation method | Kill criterion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | Pool-with-partition scales to the v1 tenant population on one India plane within residency + per-tenant rate SLA. | Load model against projected tenant count before GA. | If it cannot without breaching the noisy-neighbour SLA, cohort-shard earlier (§15.3.5). |
| A2 | One certified rule-pack pipeline keeps pace with recurring statutory load. | Track notification→certified-pack latency for two quarters. | Median latency > shortest observed statutory effective-notice window → statutory team under-resourced (§13). |
| A3 | The CA-as-cross-tenant-actor auth model is worth its complexity. | §20 validation Q5 (20–30 CA interviews). | CAs see us as disintermediation → degrade to per-tenant export + reporting view (§15.3.6). |
| A4 | ≥3 residency-selectable inference backends satisfy every regulated procurement we target in v2–vision. | Per-procurement provider-matrix re-verification. | A required buyer mandates in-country inference no listed provider offers → self-host inference SKU moves up the roadmap. |
| A5 | Real tokens-per-query keep AI within the bundled-free envelope at beachhead ARPU. | Instrument the prototype (§20 Q4); attribution built in from v1. | Actual ≥5× the estimate → bundling AI free stops working at the low end; router cost ceilings tighten (§13). |
| A6 | Device integration effort is affordable in-house for the common fleet (eSSL/ZKTeco ADMS). | Hardware spike (effort currently **unsized**, §09 [Killed] the old figure). | If mixed-fleet success is materially below what the spike shows viable, lean on the paid connector market for the long tail (§15.5.1). |

**[Killed]** — reminders that must not re-enter the architecture: "cache everything" as a
default (Gemini hourly cache storage ≈100× worse for sub-1,000-emp tenants, §13); self-hosting
*for cost* (serverless beats dedicated H100 ~74× at real utilisation, §20); any claim of
automated filing where a state PT portal offers no channel; and treating multi-state PT/LWF as
a differentiator (Frappe ships it free, §04).

---

### 15.11 Summary — how the pieces enforce the thesis

The architecture is arranged so that the product's two central claims are *structural
properties*, not aspirations:

- **"The filing is the unit of delivery"** is enforced by making the filing orchestrator
  event-sourced and the primary audit stream — the system's durable truth is an acknowledged
  filing, and every other component exists to feed it.
- **"Rules-first, LLM-last"** is enforced by a hard trust boundary: the deterministic core
  computes every statutory number and stamps its rule versions; the AI edge explains, drafts
  and routes through the same audited, approval-gated write path a human uses, with no
  privileged compute path.

Effective-dating, the corrigendum-aware certification pipeline, per-tenant partition with a
regulated silo escape hatch, residency-as-configuration with ≥3 interchangeable backends, and
cost attribution built while AI is still free — each is one design choice serving a named,
sourced constraint elsewhere in this PRD. None is gold-plating; each has a kill criterion or a
[Verified] source behind it.


---

## 16. Integrations & External Interfaces

This section specifies **every external system the product talks to**, and — because in
this market most of those systems are hostile, undocumented, or have no API at all — it
specifies the *fallback* for each one with the same weight as the happy path. That is the
governing design stance of the whole section:

> **In an Indian statutory HRMS, the integration is judged by its fallback, not its API.**
> The government portals that carry the unit of delivery (§04 — the filing, not the
> payslip) publish no stable machine interface; the incumbent (Tally, §04) is a
> file-import wedge, not a live connection; and the device fleet (§09) speaks a
> reverse-engineered binary protocol on the long tail. A design that assumes clean APIs
> everywhere ships a demo, not a product. Every integration below therefore carries a
> **contract, a data-exchange spec, an enumerated failure taxonomy, and a fallback that
> keeps the filing on time when the primary path is down.**

Three framing rules from Draft 1 govern this section and are not restated per-integration:

- **The filing is the unit of delivery (§04, [Verified]).** An integration is "working"
  only when the artefact it feeds — an accepted ECR, a settled bank batch, a filed Form
  138 — completes. A green API call that does not produce an accepted filing is a red
  status here.
- **Rules-first, LLM-last (§07, [Verified]).** No integration may allow a model to
  generate a statutory or monetary figure that crosses a system boundary. The assistant
  may draft an email to a bank RM or explain a portal rejection; it never computes the
  amount on a challan or a NEFT line. Every outbound file is produced by the deterministic
  engine (§08) and reconciled to the rupee before it leaves the system.
- **Own the data and the tools, not the assistant (§12 of Draft 1, [Verified]).** The
  public API and MCP posture (§16.11) are built so that when an enterprise buyer's
  assistant (Copilot, Glean, a Darwinbox Cortex successor) wants our data, we are the
  governed source of tools it calls — not a competitor for the chat surface.

### 16.1 Integration taxonomy and posture

Not all integrations are the same kind of thing, and conflating them is the most common
architectural error in this category. We classify every external interface on four axes,
because the axis determines the engineering, the SLA, and the fallback.

| Axis | Values | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Direction** | Inbound (we ingest) · Outbound (we emit) · Bidirectional | Determines who owns the schema and who breaks whom on a change |
| **Transport** | Live API (REST/SOAP) · File exchange (upload/download) · Device push (ADMS) · RPA/browser (no API) · Manual/human-in-loop | Determines reliability, monitorability, and legal exposure |
| **Cadence** | Real-time · Event/webhook · Scheduled batch · One-time (migration) | Determines idempotency and retry design |
| **Criticality to the filing** | On the filing path (blocks a return) · On the pay path (blocks disbursement) · Convenience | Determines on-call priority and the fallback investment |

Applying the taxonomy to the full integration surface. This is the master register; each
row is detailed in the subsection named.

| # | Integration | Direction | Transport | Cadence | Filing-critical? | Phase | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | **Tally** (accounting + migration) | Bi | File (XML/CSV) | Batch + one-time | Pay path (GL) | **P0** | §16.2 |
| B | **Banks — salary disbursement** | Out | File + host-to-host + API | Batch | Pay path | **P0** | §16.3 |
| C | **Biometric / attendance devices** | In | Device push (ADMS) + SDK pull | Real-time + batch | Pay path (LOP) | **P0** push / P1 pull | §16.4 |
| D | **EPFO** (ECR, UAN, KYC) | Out | File upload + RPA | Batch (monthly) | **Filing path** | **P0** | §16.5 |
| E | **ESIC** (contribution, IP) | Out | File upload + RPA | Batch (monthly) | **Filing path** | **P0** | §16.5 |
| F | **TRACES / income-tax e-filing** (Form 138 ex-24Q, Form 130 ex-16) | Out | File (FVU) + RPA | Batch (quarterly/annual) | **Filing path** | **P0** | §16.5 |
| G | **State PT portals** (per-state) | Out | File + RPA + manual | Batch (monthly/annual) | **Filing path** | P0 (top states) / P1 (rest) | §16.5 |
| H | **State LWF portals** | Out | File + manual | Batch (semi-annual/annual) | Filing path | P1 | §16.5 |
| I | **Accounting systems** (Zoho Books, QuickBooks, Busy, ERP GL) | Out | API + file | Batch | Pay path (GL) | P1 | §16.6 |
| J | **HRIS migration importers** (Zoho/Kredily/Frappe/greytHR/Excel) | In | File + API | One-time | Onboarding | **P0** | §16.7 |
| K | **Recruiting / job boards** (Naukri, LinkedIn, foundit, apna, Indeed) | Bi | API + posting | Event | Convenience | P1 | §16.8 |
| L | **Communication** (WhatsApp, email, SMS-DLT, e-sign) | Out | API | Real-time/event | Pay path (payslip delivery) | P0 (email/SMS) / P1 (WA) | §16.9 |
| M | **Identity / SSO / SCIM** | Bi | OIDC/SAML/SCIM | Real-time | Convenience | P1 | §16.10 |
| N | **Public API + webhooks + MCP** | Bi | REST + MCP | All | Platform | P1 (API) / P2 (MCP GA) | §16.11 |

Two posture decisions apply across the whole register:

**[Verified]** — **The government portals have no stable API; design for that as the base
case, not the exception.** EPFO's Unified Portal, ESIC portal, TRACES, and the state PT
sites are file-upload and screen-driven. There is no published, versioned, authenticated
REST contract a vendor can build a supported integration against (Source: EPFO Unified
Portal employer interface; TRACES portal — file-validation-utility workflow; observed
across all four as of 2026). Consequently the "integration" for the filing path is
**(1) generate a schema-perfect file** + **(2) assist the human through the upload** +
**(3) capture and reconcile the acknowledgement**. Any roadmap that promises "one-click
government filing via API" is selling something that does not exist and will churn on the
first rejection.

**[Verified]** — **Schema-driven, never hard-coded.** Every file format below — ECR text,
ESI contribution CSV, the FVU input for Form 138 (which is mid-breaking-change, §06),
each bank's NEFT template, each state's PT return — is a **versioned schema object**, not
code. Field numbers, column orders and delimiters change by gazette and by bank release.
Form 138 alone remapped challan heads 301–312 → A–K (303 deleted) and Annexure I 313–327 →
C–N, with the Q4 regular format still unpublished (§06 [Verified], Source: CBDT Notification
+ Protean/NSDL FVU release notes, Q1–Q3 v1.2 shipped 22 Jul 2026). A hard-coded layout is
a guaranteed production incident on the next notification.

**The schema object, concretely.** Every file-schema integration is described by a
declarative record the runtime interprets — never by branching code:

| Schema-object field | Example (EPFO ECR 2.0) |
| --- | --- |
| `schema_id` / `version` | `epfo.ecr` / `2.0` |
| `effective_from` / `effective_to` | `2020-04-01` / `null` (open) |
| `source_ref` | EPFO Unified Portal ECR upload spec, retrieved 2026 (URL + date) |
| `delimiter` / `line_terminator` / `encoding` | `#~#` / `CRLF` / `UTF-8` (no BOM) |
| `columns[]` (ordinal, name, type, rule) | 11 columns, ordered (see §16.5.1) |
| `validators[]` | UAN Verhoeff checksum, EPS≤EPF-wages@₹15k, arithmetic ties |
| `blocked` (bool) + `blocked_reason` | `false` (contrast Q4 Form 138 = `true`) |

A gazette change edits the schema object's data and mints a new `version` with a new
`effective_from`; the prior version stays live for in-flight (arrear/retro) periods.
This is the same effective-dating discipline the wage engine uses for the 50% add-back
(§06, "or such other per cent as may be notified" — [Verified]).

---

### 16.2 Tally — accounting export and the migration wedge

Tally is not a peer integration; it is the incumbent (§04). It appears twice: as the
**one-time migration source** that wins the deal, and as the **ongoing GL export target**
that lets the customer keep Tally as their book of record.

**[Verified]** — **The Tally data-import path is P0 because the import is the wedge, not
because Tally has a good API** (Draft 1 §18). TallyPrime is statutorily complete and
₹0-incremental (Source: TallyPrime feature list — PF 3A/5/6A/10/12A + ECR, ESI, PT, Form 16,
24Q Annexures I–II, included in base licence); a feature-parity pitch loses. We win by
making leaving Tally-for-payroll costless while letting the customer keep Tally-for-accounts.

| Facet | Specification |
| --- | --- |
| **Contract** | No live API dependency. Tally exposes an XML request/response over HTTP on a LAN port (default 9000) and reads/writes XML and CSV. We treat it as a **file-and-XML boundary**, not a service. Two flows: (1) **import** — parse a customer's Tally export (masters + vouchers) during onboarding; (2) **export** — emit a payroll journal voucher Tally can import. |
| **Data exchange — import** | Ingest: ledger masters (employee ledgers, salary/PF/ESI/PT/TDS payable ledgers), cost centres/categories (often used as departments), opening balances, and — where the Tally Payroll module is enabled — pay heads, attendance/production types, and employee masters with PF/ESI/UAN numbers. Format: Tally XML export or CSV per ledger. |
| **Data exchange — export** | Emit a **payroll journal voucher** per pay run: debit salary/wages and employer-contribution expense heads, credit net-pay-payable, PF payable (EE+ER), ESI payable, PT payable, TDS payable, and any recovery ledgers. Delivered as Tally-importable XML with a stable ledger-mapping table the customer confirms once, then reuses. |
| **Failure modes** | (1) **Ledger-name mismatch** — customer's ledger names don't match our mapping → voucher import fails or posts to a suspense ledger. (2) **Duplicate voucher** on re-export → double-counted GL. (3) **Tally version drift** — TallyPrime vs Tally.ERP9 XML dialect differences (e.g. `<ENVELOPE>` header changes, GST-era tag additions). (4) **Character/encoding** — special characters (`&`, non-ASCII) in employee names corrupt XML unless entity-escaped. (5) **Split company data** — customer runs multiple Tally companies; wrong `SVCURRENTCOMPANY` target. (6) **Financial-year boundary** — voucher dated in a year Tally hasn't opened is silently rejected. |
| **Fallback** | Every export is also downloadable as a **CSV/Excel journal** the customer's accountant can post by hand — the same reconciled totals, human-readable. Import failures never block a pay run or a filing; the GL post is downstream of disbursement. A **dry-run diff** shows the voucher before it is emitted. Idempotency: each voucher carries a deterministic `payrun_id` external key (as `VOUCHERKEY`/narration tag) so re-export updates rather than duplicates. |

**Worked example — the payroll journal voucher (50-employee run).** For a monthly run
with gross ₹42,00,000, the emitted voucher must balance to the rupee and tie to §16.3:

| Dr / Cr | Ledger (mapped) | Amount (₹) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dr | Salaries & Wages (expense) | 42,00,000 |
| Dr | Employer PF Contribution (expense) | 2,29,500 |
| Dr | Employer ESI Contribution (expense) | 41,600 |
| Cr | Net Pay Payable (→ bank batch, §16.3) | 37,86,900 |
| Cr | EPF Payable (EE ₹4,32,000 + ER ₹2,29,500) | 6,61,500 |
| Cr | ESI Payable (EE ₹9,600 + ER ₹41,600) | 51,200 |
| Cr | Professional Tax Payable | 9,800 |
| Cr | TDS Payable (u/s 192) | 61,700 |
| **—** | **Σ Dr = Σ Cr** | **45,54,200** |

`Net Pay Payable ₹37,86,900` must equal the bank disbursement batch total (§16.3) and
Σ payslip net — the three-way tie is checked before the voucher is offered for download.

> **[Hypothesis]** — *Most Tally seats that matter enable the Payroll module.* Kill/validate
> criterion: §20 validation item 2 (15–25 Tally-partner interviews). If <~5% enable
> payroll, the "import from Tally Payroll" path is low-value and we import from Tally
> *accounts* + a spreadsheet instead; at ~40% the Tally Payroll importer is the single
> highest-leverage onboarding asset. Do not over-build the Payroll-module importer until
> this reports.

**Acceptance criteria (Tally).**

- **AC-TLY-1:** For a 50-employee run, the emitted journal voucher's debits = credits to
  the rupee, and Σ(net-pay-payable) = the bank disbursement total (§16.3) = Σ payslips.
- **AC-TLY-2:** Re-exporting the same `payrun_id` produces zero new vouchers in Tally
  (idempotent by external key), verified against a live TallyPrime instance.
- **AC-TLY-3:** Onboarding import of a real customer Tally export maps ≥95% of employee
  and statutory ledgers automatically; the residue is surfaced in a mapping UI, never
  silently dropped.
- **AC-TLY-4:** A ledger-name mismatch routes the line to a named suspense ledger and
  raises a reconciliation exception — it never posts to the wrong head silently.
- **AC-TLY-5:** A voucher dated outside Tally's open financial year is caught pre-emission
  with an actionable message, not left as a silent Tally-side rejection.

---

### 16.3 Banks — salary disbursement and reconciliation

Salary disbursement is on the **pay path**: if it fails, employees are not paid, which is
a same-day escalation. India offers four disbursement mechanisms with materially different
contracts. We support a tiered posture: file first (universal), API where available (fast
tenants), aggregator as a fallback and an SMB default.

| Rail | What it is | Latency | When we use it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **NEFT** | Batched net settlement, 24×7 since Dec 2019 (Source: RBI circular, 16 Dec 2019) | Minutes–hours (half-hourly batches) | Default for bulk salary; universal |
| **RTGS** | Real-time gross settlement, ₹2 lakh minimum, 24×7 since Dec 2020 | Near-real-time | High-value single transfers (e.g. FnF, directors) |
| **IMPS** | Instant, 24×7, per-txn limit ₹5 lakh (NPCI) | Seconds | Off-cycle / urgent single payouts |
| **Host-to-host / corporate API** | Bank-specific bulk API or SFTP file drop | Bank SLA | Larger tenants with a corporate banking relationship |

**[Verified]** — **The universal contract is a bank-specific bulk-upload file, not an
API.** Every corporate bank (SBI, HDFC, ICICI, Axis, Kotak, YES) accepts a bulk salary
file in its own fixed format via corporate net-banking; there is no cross-bank standard
(Source: HDFC ENet, ICICI Corporate Internet Banking / iCIB, Axis Corporate iConnect
bulk-payment upload specs, 2026). Therefore the **bank file generator is a per-bank
versioned schema** (§16.1), exactly like the ECR and FVU generators.

| Facet | Specification |
| --- | --- |
| **Contract — file** | Per-bank bulk NEFT/salary upload template: beneficiary account, IFSC, name, amount, narration, debit account, value date, and (for salary-account banks) employee code. We ship templates for the top ~8 corporate banks in P0 and a **configurable generic template builder** (column mapping, delimiter, fixed-width vs CSV, header/trailer, record-count and hash-total checksum) for the long tail so onboarding never blocks on "my bank isn't supported." |
| **Contract — host-to-host / API** | For tenants on ICICI CIB / Kotak / HDFC / RazorpayX Payroll rails: authenticated bulk-payment API or SFTP drop with an async status callback. Credentials stored per §16.12 (secrets vault, per-tenant). Aggregators (RazorpayX, Cashfree Payouts, Open) provide a single API across banks and are the **SMB default** where the tenant has no corporate-banking file facility. |
| **Data exchange** | Outbound: the disbursement batch (net-pay lines) generated *only* from a locked, approved pay run (§08 pay-run state machine). Inbound: settlement status per line (success / failed / returned) via API callback, downloadable bank statement (MT940/CSV), or manual entry, feeding auto-reconciliation. |
| **Failure modes** | (1) **Invalid IFSC / account** → line rejected or credited wrong (IFSC validated pre-emission against the RBI/NPCI IFSC directory). (2) **Name-mismatch return** (beneficiary name vs account) — bank returns the credit T+1/2 with reason code. (3) **Partial batch** — some lines settle, some fail; the batch is *not* atomic. (4) **Cut-off missed** — file uploaded after the bank's salary cut-off pays next working day. (5) **Duplicate upload** — same batch uploaded twice → double payment. (6) **Insufficient balance** in the disbursement account → whole batch held. (7) **Holiday/RTGS-NEFT window** and value-date edge cases. (8) **Beneficiary not pre-registered** — some corporate portals require a beneficiary-approval lag (cooling period) before first credit. |
| **Fallback** | Universal downloadable bank file is always available even if the API path fails — the customer uploads it in net-banking themselves. **Partial-batch handling is first-class:** each line has an independent status; failed lines are re-queued into a *new* batch without re-paying settled lines (idempotency key per line = `payrun_id + employee_id`). A **pre-flight validation** (IFSC exists, account format, amount > 0, name present, no zero/negative net, batch hash-total matches) blocks a bad batch before it reaches the bank. Reconciliation exceptions (returns, mismatches) open a worklist item, never silently close. |



**Figure 101. Bank Reconciliation Flow**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PR["Locked, approved pay run (S08)<br/>Net Pay Payable = Sigma payslip net"] --> BATCH["Build disbursement batch<br/>net-pay lines: acct, IFSC, name, amount"]

    BATCH --> PF{"Pre-flight validation<br/>IFSC in RBI/NPCI directory - account non-empty<br/>amount = payslip net - no zero/negative<br/>hash-total + record-count trailer match"}
    PF -->|"any line fails"| BLOCK["BLOCKED pre-emission<br/>blocking error, not silent drop<br/>(AC-BNK-1 / AC-BNK-5)"]
    BLOCK --> BATCH

    PF -->|"all lines pass"| CUTOFF{"Cut-off + rail check<br/>after bank salary cut-off? - holiday / Sunday RTGS window?<br/>RTGS line < Rs 2 lakh -> auto-route to NEFT"}
    CUTOFF -->|"warn, do not silently slip payday"| EMIT

    EMIT{"Emit batch"} -->|"universal fallback"| FILE["Per-bank bulk-upload file<br/>customer uploads in net-banking"]
    EMIT -->|"corporate rail"| API["Host-to-host API / SFTP<br/>ICICI CIB, Kotak, HDFC"]
    EMIT -->|"SMB default"| AGG["Aggregator payout<br/>RazorpayX / Cashfree / Open"]

    FILE --> RAIL["Bank rails: NEFT / RTGS / IMPS"]
    API --> RAIL
    AGG --> RAIL

    RAIL --> SETTLE["Settlement status per line<br/>via API callback, MT940/CSV, or manual<br/>(batch is NOT atomic)"]

    SETTLE --> RECON["Reconciliation engine<br/>match settlement lines to pay-run lines by UTR/reference"]
    RECON --> CLASS{"Per-line outcome"}
    CLASS -->|"credited"| OK["Settled - idempotency key<br/>payrun_id + employee_id"]
    CLASS -->|"returned (e.g. R03 acct closed)"| EXC["Exception worklist<br/>reason code + assignee"]
    CLASS -->|"failed pre-network (IFSC decommissioned)"| EXC

    EXC --> REQ["Re-queue ONLY failed lines into a NEW batch<br/>settled employees never paid twice (AC-BNK-2)"]
    REQ --> BATCH

    OK --> TIE{"Three-way tie<br/>Sigma credited = Sigma net-pay = Sigma payslips<br/>AND every exception cleared?"}
    EXC -.->|"holds run"| DWE["disbursed-with-exceptions<br/>run cannot reach complete (AC-BNK-3)"]
    DWE -.-> TIE
    TIE -->|"no"| DWE
    TIE -->|"yes"| DONE(["complete<br/>pay-path analogue of 'filing accepted'"])
```


**Worked example — partial-batch return.** A 50-line NEFT batch of ₹37,86,900 (from
§16.2) is uploaded. Settlement callback: 48 lines credited, 1 line returned R03
(beneficiary account closed), 1 line failed pre-network (IFSC decommissioned after a bank
merger). The run moves to `disbursed-with-exceptions`. The engine re-queues **exactly the
2 failed lines** (₹1,54,300 combined) into a new batch keyed on the same
`payrun_id + employee_id` pair — the 48 settled employees cannot be paid twice. The run
cannot reach `complete` until Σ credited (₹37,86,900) = Σ net; the two exceptions carry a
reason code and an assignee. This is the pay-path analogue of "filing accepted, not filing
submitted."

**Reconciliation — the load-bearing part.** Disbursement is not "done" when the file
uploads; it is done when **Σ credited = Σ net-pay = Σ payslips** and every exception is
cleared. The reconciliation engine matches bank settlement lines back to pay-run lines by
UTR/reference, flags returns for re-issue, and holds the pay run in a
`disbursed-with-exceptions` state until cleared.

**Cut-off awareness (edge cases that cause real incidents).** The engine surfaces the
deadline clock rather than hiding it: a batch scheduled after the tenant bank's salary
cut-off is flagged as "will credit next working day"; a value date falling on a bank
holiday or a Sunday RTGS-maintenance window is warned pre-emission; an RTGS line below
₹2 lakh is auto-routed to NEFT. None of these silently slip a payday.

**Acceptance criteria (banking).**

- **AC-BNK-1:** Every net-pay line is validated (IFSC in directory, account non-empty,
  amount = payslip net) before the batch is emitted; a single invalid line surfaces as a
  blocking pre-flight error, not a silent drop.
- **AC-BNK-2:** Re-emitting a batch for an already-settled `payrun_id` pays no employee
  twice (per-line idempotency), proven with a returned-line re-issue test.
- **AC-BNK-3:** A partial settlement (e.g. 48/50 lines succeed) leaves the run in
  `disbursed-with-exceptions`, re-queues exactly the 2 failed lines, and the run cannot be
  marked complete until Σ credited = Σ net.
- **AC-BNK-4:** For a supported bank, the generated file imports into that bank's corporate
  net-banking bulk-upload without manual edits (validated per bank release).
- **AC-BNK-5:** A batch whose emitted hash-total / record-count trailer does not match the
  line body is rejected in-product before upload (guards silent truncation).

---

### 16.4 Biometric and attendance devices

Attendance feeds loss-of-pay, overtime and statutory registers (§09), so it is on the pay
path. Draft 1 named the device-push receiver **the best-evidenced call in the corpus.**

**[Verified]** — **Build the ADMS/WDMS push receiver in v1** (Draft 1 §09). The dominant
device-to-cloud path in India is **outbound**: the terminal HTTP-POSTs punch packets to a
tenant-scoped URL. No on-premise middleware, no static IP, no port-forwarding. eSSL and
ZKTeco both support it; corroborated across four independent sources and unshaken by
hostile re-check (Source: eSSL/ZKTeco ADMS/PUSH-SDK documentation, 2026).



**Figure 102. Device Push Ingest**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant DEV as eSSL / ZKTeco terminal
    participant EP as Tenant-scoped ADMS ingest endpoint
    participant SEC as Tenant-key + serial allowlist
    participant ING as Idempotent ingest (serial, device-user-id, ts)
    participant MAP as device-user-id to employee map
    participant WL as Exceptions worklist
    participant ATT as Attendance / Section 09 rules (LOP, OT, shift)

    Note over DEV,EP: Setup: admin pastes endpoint URL + tenant key into device cloud-server config once
    DEV->>EP: Register /iclock/cdata?SN=CJKD2043xxxx (serial)
    EP->>SEC: Validate serial + tenant key
    alt Unregistered serial / no tenant-key match
        SEC-->>DEV: Reject + log security event (AC-DEV-5, Section 16.12)
    else Registered
        SEC-->>EP: OK, serial to tenant to location resolved
        EP->>DEV: Queue enrolment / user-sync commands (/iclock/getrequest)
    end

    Note over DEV: Device offline 6h across shift change, buffers 214 punches
    DEV->>EP: POST attendance-log (cdata body: 214 punches)
    Note right of DEV: No 200 in time, device retries POST twice
    DEV->>EP: POST attendance-log (retry, same packets)
    EP->>ING: Punch packets (serial, user id, timestamp, verify mode)
    ING->>ING: Dedup on (serial, device-user-id, timestamp) - write each once

    ING->>MAP: Resolve device-user-id to employee
    alt Mapped
        MAP->>ATT: Attribute punch, derive first-in/last-out, OT, LOP
    else Unmapped (00042, 00119 not in HRMS)
        MAP->>WL: Hold punch, exclude from LOP/OT until admin maps (AC-DEV-3)
    end
    EP-->>DEV: 200 OK
    Note over ING,ATT: Result: 212 attributed, 2 held, 0 duplicated, 0 dropped

    Note over DEV,ATT: Device down / unsupported -> fallback: web-mobile check-in (GPS), bulk CSV, manual muster - never blocks payroll
```


| Facet | Specification |
| --- | --- |
| **Contract — push (P0)** | We expose a **tenant-scoped ingest endpoint** implementing the ADMS/PUSH protocol handshake (device registration `/iclock/cdata?SN=…`, command queue `/iclock/getrequest`, attendance-log POST, heartbeat). The admin pastes the endpoint URL + tenant key into the device's cloud-server config once; punches then flow with no middleware. Device serial → tenant → location mapping is registered at setup. |
| **Contract — pull (P1)** | For devices without ADMS or on segregated plant networks, a **pull path** via the vendor SDK / port-4370 protocol through a lightweight on-prem agent, or a **third-party connector**. Draft 1 [Verified]: a paid connector market exists at ~**$345 one-time to $588/year** — cheap enough that we **partner/buy for the long tail** rather than build for every SDK-bound brand and firmware. |
| **Data exchange** | Inbound punch packet: device serial, user id (device-local), timestamp, punch direction/verify mode. We map device-user-id → employee, dedup, and derive first-in/last-out, shift, OT and LOP per §09 rules (8-hr day, 48-hr week, OT at 2×, 144-hr/quarter ceiling — [Verified], Source: notified Central Rules under the Codes, 8 May 2026). Outbound (push protocol): enrolment/user-sync commands queued to the device. |
| **Failure modes** | (1) **Clock drift** on the device → punches land in the wrong day/shift (CERT-In also requires NTP sync, §16.12). (2) **Device offline** — punches buffered locally, arrive in a burst on reconnect (must be idempotent). (3) **Duplicate punches** (double-tap, retry). (4) **Unmapped device-user-id** (new joiner enrolled on device but not in HRMS, or vice-versa). (5) **Firmware quirks** on legacy port-4370 (protocol is reverse-engineered, behaves inconsistently — [Verified]). (6) **Shared-device identity** — 9 in 10 non-users live in a phone-owning household; worker identity ≠ device identity (§09 [Verified]). (7) **Serial spoofing** — an unregistered serial POSTing to the endpoint (mitigated by tenant-key + serial allowlist). |
| **Fallback** | If a device is down or unsupported, attendance falls back to **web/mobile check-in (with GPS/geofence), bulk CSV upload, and manual muster** — none block payroll. Buffered bursts are handled by **idempotent ingest** keyed on (serial, device-user-id, timestamp). Unmapped punches go to an **exceptions worklist** and are held out of pay until mapped, never dropped. A punch that cannot be mapped by pay-run lock is treated per the tenant's configured policy (present-assumed vs LOP), surfaced explicitly. |

**Worked example — buffered burst after reconnect.** A plant terminal (serial
`CJKD2043xxxx`) loses WAN for 6 hours across a shift change and buffers 214 punches. On
reconnect it POSTs them in one `cdata` body. Idempotent ingest keyed on
(serial, device-user-id, timestamp) writes each punch exactly once even though the device
retries the POST twice (it did not receive our first 200 OK in time). Two punches carry a
device-user-id (`00042`, `00119`) with no HRMS mapping — they land in the exceptions
worklist and are excluded from that day's LOP/OT computation until an admin maps them,
rather than being counted as absent. Net result: 212 attributed, 2 held, 0 duplicated,
0 dropped.

**Highest-leverage cheap artefact (from Draft 1 §09, carried into this section):** ship a
**public, model-level device compatibility matrix and a self-serve verification tool**
before the first enterprise sales call. It neutralises deal-gating risk and **no incumbent
publishes one** (Source: incumbent product/support sites, none surfaces a self-serve
device matrix — observed 2026). This is an integration deliverable, not just marketing: it
is the self-serve front door to §16.4.

> **[Killed]** — Do not size device work from the retracted "85–98% success / 1-in-7
> devices won't integrate" figure — it was marketing from the vendor selling the fix
> (Draft 1 §09, §20 banned-numbers table). Device integration effort is **currently
> unsized**; it needs a hardware spike before any completion date is committed.

**Acceptance criteria (devices).**

- **AC-DEV-1:** A factory-config eSSL or ZKTeco terminal pointed at the tenant ingest URL
  streams punches with zero on-prem software, mapped to employees within one poll cycle.
- **AC-DEV-2:** A device reconnecting after 6 hours offline delivers its buffered punches
  and produces **no duplicate** attendance rows (idempotent ingest).
- **AC-DEV-3:** An unmapped device-user-id raises an exception and is excluded from LOP/OT
  computation until resolved — it is never silently counted as absent or present.
- **AC-DEV-4:** The public compatibility matrix returns a supported/partner/unsupported
  verdict for a given make+model+firmware, self-serve, before any sales contact.
- **AC-DEV-5:** A POST from an unregistered serial (no tenant-key match) is rejected and
  logged as a security event (§16.12), not silently ingested.

### 16.5 Government statutory portals — the filing path

These are the integrations that carry the unit of delivery (§04). They share one brutal
property: **there is no supported API.** The "integration" is *generate a schema-perfect
file → assist the upload → capture and reconcile the acknowledgement.* We are candid about
this rather than pretending an API exists.

**[Verified]** — **The corrigendum discipline applies to every file schema here.** Two
adversarial research rounds reached *opposite* conclusions on the Nov-2026 EPF cliff
because one read a notification without checking for a corrigendum (Draft 1 §02 standing
rule; the uncorrected S.O. 5319(E) enumeration is still reproduced on indiacode.nic.in —
verifying there alone reproduces the error). Every statutory file schema carries a
gazette/notification source (URL + date), and the statutory-change watcher (§16.12, and
Draft 1 §02) must **catch amendments, not just new instruments** — a watcher keyed only to
new notifications would have missed the corrigendum that inverted the entire Nov-2026
analysis.



**Figure 103. Filing Lifecycle State Machine**

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    direction LR
    [*] --> prepared: Filing minted from PayRun, input_snapshot_ref frozen, nil_return_flag if zero-liability
    prepared --> validated: local format checks pass, format_version bound
    validated --> prepared: validation error, fix inputs
    validated --> submitted: uploaded to portal
    submitted --> acknowledged: ack_no + submitted_at captured
    acknowledged --> accepted: portal accepts
    acknowledged --> rejected: structured rejection reasons e.g. AADHAAR_UAN_MISMATCH, IFSC invalid
    rejected --> validated: fix identifier state, re-validate against SAME input_snapshot_ref
    accepted --> revised: correction / arrears delta
    rejected --> revised: re-file as correction
    revised --> [*]: mints NEW Filing linked by supersedes_filing_id
    accepted --> [*]

    note right of accepted
        Terminal-but-reopenable.
        Evidence of on-time filing
        (ack_no) is preserved.
    end note
    note left of rejected
        Terminal-but-reopenable.
        Resubmit keeps original
        on_time where portal
        treats correction as on-time.
    end note
```


**The filing lifecycle (one state machine for every portal).** Every statutory filing
moves through the same states, and only the last is "done":

`draft` → `validated` (passes in-product pre-validator) → `file-generated` →
`upload-assisted` (human uploads / RPA drives, §16.5 hypothesis) →
`submitted` (portal accepted the file) → **`acknowledged`** (TRRN/challan/token/receipt
captured) → `paid` (challan paid, confirmation stored) → `filed` (proof-of-filing archived,
5-yr retention). A period stays `filing-pending` until it reaches `acknowledged`/`paid` as
the return requires; a stuck state raises the deadline clock, never hides it. Blocked
formats (below) short-circuit to an explicit `blocked-pending-format` state before `draft`.

#### 16.5.1 EPFO — ECR, UAN, KYC

| Facet | Specification |
| --- | --- |
| **Contract** | File upload to the EPFO Unified Employer Portal. Primary artefact: the monthly **ECR (Electronic Challan-cum-Return)** text file → challan generation → payment via net-banking/authorised bank. Supporting: UAN generation for new joiners, KYC seeding (Aadhaar/PAN/bank), and Form 3A/6A/5/10/12A-equivalent registers. **Build against the Employees' Provident Funds Scheme, 2026** (12% re-notified retro to 21.11.2025 by S.O. 3582(E) — Draft 1 §06 [Verified]), not the repealed 1952 scheme. |
| **Data exchange** | Outbound: ECR file (UAN, name, gross wages, EPF wages, EPS wages, EDLI wages, EE contribution, ER EPF+EPS split, NCP days, refund of advances) in the EPFO-specified delimited layout. Inbound: the generated **TRRN / challan** and, after payment, the **payment confirmation** — captured and stored as the proof-of-filing artefact. |
| **Failure modes** | (1) **Wage-base error** — the 50% add-back (§06/§08) mis-computed → wrong EPF wages → wrong challan. (2) **UAN not generated / KYC not verified** → member rejected in ECR. (3) **Delimiter/format drift** on an EPFO release → upload rejected. (4) **Portal downtime / maintenance windows** near due dates. (5) **Arrears vs current** mis-tagged in a retro run. (6) **The cliff:** post-21-Nov-2026 scheme-name/field changes if the transitional saving lapses. (7) **NCP-days error** — non-contributory (loss-of-pay) days wrong → contribution mismatch. |
| **Fallback** | The ECR file is always downloadable for **manual upload by the employer or their CA** — the product never becomes a single point of failure for a statutory deadline. A **pre-upload validator** replicates known EPFO field checks (UAN Verhoeff checksum, wage relationships EPS wages ≤ ₹15k base, contribution arithmetic) to catch rejections before they happen. Filing status is tracked to **acknowledgement** (TRRN), not submission; an un-acknowledged ECR keeps the period in `filing-pending`. |

**The ECR 2.0 line layout (the schema object, concretely).** ECR 2.0 is a `#~#`-delimited
text file, one line per member, 11 fields (Source: EPFO Unified Portal ECR file-format
help, 2026):

| # | Field | Rule / worked value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | UAN | 12-digit, Verhoeff-checksum valid |
| 2 | Member name | as per UAN (KYC), name-match else rejection |
| 3 | Gross wages | ₹30,000 |
| 4 | EPF wages | ₹15,000 (capped at statutory ₹15k ceiling) |
| 5 | EPS wages | ₹15,000 (EPS wage ceiling ₹15k) |
| 6 | EDLI wages | ₹15,000 |
| 7 | EPF contribution (EE) remitted | ₹1,800 (12% × 15,000) |
| 8 | EPS contribution remitted | ₹1,250 (8.33% × 15,000) |
| 9 | EPF+EPS diff (ER share to EPF) | ₹550 (1,800 − 1,250) |
| 10 | NCP days | 0 |
| 11 | Refund of advances | 0 |

**Worked example — the 50% add-back that drives EPF wages (§06 [Verified]).** This is the
hardest single calculation in the build (Draft 1 §06), and it is what makes field 4 above
correct. Consider an employee at ₹30,000/month structured as Basic ₹12,000, HRA ₹6,000,
Conveyance ₹1,600, Special Allowance ₹10,400.

- **Excluded components** (HRA + conveyance + special allowance treated as excluded under
  the s.2(y)/s.2(88) definition) = ₹6,000 + ₹1,600 + ₹10,400 = **₹18,000 = 60% of total**.
- The proviso caps exclusions at **50%** of total remuneration = ₹15,000. Excess =
  ₹18,000 − ₹15,000 = **₹3,000 is deemed wages and added back.**
- **Add-back wage base** = (₹30,000 − ₹18,000) + ₹3,000 = ₹12,000 + ₹3,000 = **₹15,000**.
- EPF wages = min(₹15,000 add-back base, ₹15,000 ceiling) = **₹15,000** → fields 4–6.

This produces **two concurrent wage bases on one payslip** (§06): the add-back base
(₹15,000, drives PF/EPS/EDLI/gratuity) and the equal-pay/payment-of-wages base (₹30,000,
includes HRA and conveyance). The rule version is effective-dated because "50%" is a
notified variable, not a constant — an arrear run recomputes against the version in force
for the corrected period, not today's.

**EPF challan totals for this member (the amounts that must tie to the Tally voucher, §16.2):**

| Account head | Rate | Amount (₹) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A/c 1 — EPF (EE 12% + ER 3.67%) | 12% + 3.67% | 1,800 + 550 = 2,350 |
| A/c 10 — EPS (ER 8.33%, capped ₹1,250) | 8.33% × 15,000 | 1,250 |
| A/c 2 — EPF admin charges | 0.5%, min ₹500/estt/month | per establishment |
| A/c 21 — EDLI (ER 0.5%) | 0.5% × 15,000 | 75 |
| A/c 22 — EDLI admin | nil (abolished) | 0 |

(Source: EPFO contribution rates under EPF Scheme 2026 / EPS 1995 / EDLI 1976; A/c 2
minimum ₹500 per EPFO circular. Rates re-verify against notification — the watcher owns
this.)

#### 16.5.2 ESIC — contribution and IP management

| Facet | Specification |
| --- | --- |
| **Contract** | File upload / online entry to the ESIC portal: monthly **contribution file** (IP number, days, wages, contribution) → challan → payment. IP (Insured Person) registration for new joiners; wage-ceiling gate at ₹21,000 (₹25,000 for a person with disability) (§06). |
| **Data exchange** | Outbound: contribution file per ESIC layout (IP number, name, days worked, total monthly wages, contribution). EE 0.75% + ER 3.25% (Source: ESI (Central) Rules rate w.e.f. 1 Jul 2019 — re-verify against post-cliff notification). Inbound: challan + payment confirmation as proof-of-filing. |
| **Failure modes** | (1) **Ceiling-crossing mid-cycle** — an employee crossing ₹21k mid-contribution-period must be handled per the "continue to period end" rule; a naive cutoff mis-files. (2) **IP not registered** → member rejected. (3) **Applicability by area** — ESI applies in notified areas only; a location not in a notified area shouldn't file. (4) **Portal timeout on large files.** (5) **[Verified, Draft 1 §06] The ESI side of the Nov-2026 cliff is unresolved** — the successor regime after ~21 Nov 2026 is not yet named; this is validation item 8 and a hard dependency. |
| **Fallback** | Downloadable file for manual upload; pre-validation of ceiling and IP status; area-applicability check per location; **blocked-pending-clarity** state for post-cliff ESI rather than emitting a guessed file (§08 G7 — blocked states are honest). |

**Worked example — the two contribution periods and mid-cycle ceiling crossing.** ESI runs
on fixed contribution periods **April–September** and **October–March**, with benefit
periods lagging (Source: ESIC contribution/benefit-period rules). An employee earning
₹20,000 in April gets a raise to ₹23,000 effective July (mid-period). The **"continue to
period end" rule** means: because they were covered at the start of the April–September
period, contribution continues on the *full ₹23,000* until 30 September — they do **not**
drop out on crossing ₹21,000. From the next period (October) they are out of ESI. A naive
"stop at ₹21k the month they cross" cutoff under-files three months and creates a
recoverable default. Contribution at ₹23,000 for July: EE 0.75% = ₹172.50 (rounded to
₹173), ER 3.25% = ₹747.50 (rounded ₹748) — ESIC rounds each to the next rupee.

#### 16.5.3 TRACES / Income-Tax e-filing — TDS (Form 138 ex-24Q, Form 130 ex-16)

This is the most volatile file schema in the product because the format is **mid-breaking-change** (§06).

| Facet | Specification |
| --- | --- |
| **Contract** | Quarterly TDS return **Form 138 (ex-24Q)** prepared as an FVU (File Validation Utility) input, validated, and filed via the e-filing portal / TRACES; then **Form 130 (ex-Form 16) Part A** downloaded from TRACES and **Part B** generated by us. Also: challan (ITNS-281-equivalent) payment tracking and challan-to-deductee mapping. |
| **Data exchange** | Outbound: FVU-format quarterly file — challan heads (now A–K, 303 deleted) and Annexure I (now C–N, with 313/321/322/325 removed), Interest Allocation and Others Allocation added, Surcharge/Cess/Penalty deleted (§06 [Verified], Source: CBDT + Protean FVU v1.2 release, 22 Jul 2026; correction-statement structures 4 Aug 2026). Annexure II (annual salary detail) feeds Form 130 Part B. Inbound: FVU validation result, provisional receipt/token, TRACES Part-A PDFs. |
| **Failure modes** | (1) **Q4 regular format does not exist yet** (§06 [Verified]) → the annual certificate Part B cannot be fully built until it lands. (2) **PAN not available/invalid** → higher-rate TDS (20% u/s 206AA) + return rejection. (3) **Challan mismatch** — challan not yet reflected in OLTAS → short-payment default. (4) **Regime mis-election** (old vs new; new regime is now the default u/s 115BAC) at employee level → wrong TDS. (5) **FVU version drift** — a new FVU rejects last quarter's file structure. |
| **Fallback** | FVU file downloadable for filing by the customer's CA (the ICAI schedule prices *TDS return filing* explicitly — §04 [Verified] — so the CA expects to do this). **Q4 Form 138 and Form 130 Part B render as `blocked-pending-format`**, never silently emitted with guessed field mapping (§08 G7). Challan-status polling against OLTAS/TRACES flags un-reflected challans before filing. |

**Worked example — the challan-head remap that breaks a hard-coded layout.** A deductor's
Q2 FY26 return that previously carried challan sub-head `304` (TDS) and `305` (surcharge)
must now emit `B`/`C`-series heads with **Surcharge deleted entirely** and its value folded
per the new mapping; Annexure I fields `321`/`322` (previously separate) are removed and
`Interest Allocation`/`Others Allocation` added (§06 [Verified]). A vendor who hard-coded
column ordinal 305 = surcharge silently mis-files every deductor's return the quarter the
FVU flips. Our schema object versions the layout with `effective_from = 2026-07-22` and the
watcher (§16.12) routes the CBDT notification to it before any Q2 file is generated.

#### 16.5.4 State Professional Tax (PT) and Labour Welfare Fund (LWF)

| Facet | Specification |
| --- | --- |
| **Contract** | Per-state PT return + payment (monthly/quarterly/annual by state) on each state's commercial-tax portal; per-state LWF contribution (semi-annual/annual) on each state's labour-welfare portal. These are the most fragmented interfaces in the product — **one schema and cadence per state.** |
| **Data exchange** | Outbound: state-specific PT return (employee count by slab, PT deducted) and LWF file (EE+ER contribution by headcount). Inbound: challan/receipt. Frappe HR already ships PT across 15+ states and LWF across 14 free (§04 [Killed] — this is *parity*, not a differentiator; Source: Frappe India Payroll v16 feature list). |
| **Failure modes** | (1) **Slab drift** — states revise PT slabs and gender variants at Budget; a stale slab mis-computes (only Telangana was gazette-verified across both rounds — Draft 1 §02). (2) **Registration-not-done** per state/location (PTEC vs PTRC in Maharashtra — two separate registrations). (3) **Cadence confusion** — filing monthly where the state wants annual, or vice-versa. (4) **Portal-per-state** availability and format variance. (5) **Gender/exemption variants** — several states exempt women below a threshold or exempt senior citizens/disabled. |
| **Fallback** | Downloadable per-state file/return; **effective-dated per-state slab tables** with gazette provenance (this is a *build dependency* per Draft 1 §20 — the verified PT/LWF dataset for every state is undone work). Where a state has no usable portal export, produce the **filled human-readable return** for manual entry. States are P0 for the top employment states (MH, KA, TN, TG, WB, GJ, AP) and P1 for the rest, phased by tenant footprint. |

**Worked example — same salary, four states, four answers.** An employee earning ₹30,000
gross/month triggers different PT depending on the state of the place of work, which is why
PT must be effective-dated *per state* and never a single national table:

| State | Monthly PT on ₹30,000 | Cadence | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Karnataka | ₹200 | Monthly | ₹200 flat above ₹25,000 slab |
| Maharashtra | ₹200 (₹300 in February) | Monthly | Feb is the ₹300 month; PTEC + PTRC both required |
| West Bengal | ₹200 | Monthly | Slab: ₹15,001–25,000 = ₹130; ₹25,001–40,000 = ₹150; above = ₹200 |
| Tamil Nadu | half-yearly slab | Half-yearly | Filed to the local municipal body, not a state portal |

**[Hypothesis]** — the specific slab figures above are drawn from aggregator tables and are
**not gazette-verified** (only Telangana survived both research rounds — Draft 1 §02).
Kill/validate criterion: each state's slab must be replaced with a gazette-sourced,
effective-dated entry before that state ships P0; until then the state renders its PT with a
"slab unverified — confirm before filing" banner rather than emitting a silent figure. This
is the §20 "also undone, and cheap" build dependency.

**Master acceptance criteria (statutory portals).**

- **AC-GOV-1:** Every generated statutory file passes an **in-product pre-validator** that
  replicates the portal's/FVU's known field checks, so the modal outcome of an upload is
  acceptance, not rejection.
- **AC-GOV-2:** Filing status is tracked to **acknowledgement** (TRRN/challan/token
  captured and stored), and a period stays `filing-pending` until the ack is on file — a
  submitted-but-unacknowledged filing is not "done" (§04, §08 G5).
- **AC-GOV-3:** Every file schema is a versioned object with a gazette/notification source
  (URL + date); a format change is a data update, not a code deploy (§16.1).
- **AC-GOV-4:** Formats that **do not yet exist** (Q4 Form 138, Form 130 Part B) and
  regimes that are **unresolved** (post-cliff ESI) render as explicit blocked states, never
  as silently-emitted guessed files.
- **AC-GOV-5:** The statutory-change watcher fires on **amendments/corrigenda**, not only
  new notifications, and routes each hit to the owning schema for review.
- **AC-GOV-6:** The 50% add-back produces two concurrent wage bases per employee-period,
  and an arrear/retro run recomputes against the rule version in force for the corrected
  period (§06 [Verified]), verified by a retro-recompute test.

> **[Hypothesis]** — *RPA-assisted upload (browser automation that drives the portal on the
> user's behalf, with the human in the loop for OTP/captcha) is worth building for the top
> three portals.* Kill/validate criterion: if portal anti-automation (captcha, session
> fingerprinting, ToS) makes RPA fragile or non-compliant, drop it and stay at
> generate-file-plus-guide-upload. RPA is never the *only* path — the downloadable file is
> always the fallback. Do not let RPA touch anything that requires impersonating the
> employer's authenticated session in a way that violates portal terms.

### 16.6 Accounting systems beyond Tally

For tenants whose book of record is not Tally, the payroll journal must post to their GL.

| Facet | Specification |
| --- | --- |
| **Contract** | Zoho Books, QuickBooks (India), Busy, and generic ERP (SAP/Oracle/MS Dynamics/NetSuite) GL. Zoho Books and QuickBooks have real REST APIs; Busy and most ERPs are file/DI (data-interchange) based. |
| **Data exchange** | Same payroll journal voucher as §16.2 (debits/credits by expense and payable head), mapped once to the target chart of accounts. Zoho Books/QuickBooks: create-journal API call per pay run. ERP/Busy: emit the DI file (CSV/XML/IDoc-style) to the customer's mapping. |
| **Failure modes** | (1) **Chart-of-accounts mismatch** — target account codes don't match our mapping. (2) **API auth expiry** (OAuth token refresh). (3) **Period locked** in the accounting system (closed month) → post rejected. (4) **Rounding** — GL posts must tie to the payslip and bank totals to the rupee. (5) **Duplicate journal** on retry. (6) **GST/TDS interplay** — a payroll journal must not accidentally touch GST input ledgers. |
| **Fallback** | Universal downloadable journal (CSV/Excel) for any accounting system; idempotent posts keyed on `payrun_id`; a closed-period rejection opens an exception rather than failing silently. GL posting is downstream of disbursement and filing, so an accounting-integration failure never blocks pay or filing. |

**Acceptance criteria.**

- **AC-ACC-1:** A journal posted to Zoho Books/QuickBooks balances and ties to the bank
  disbursement and payslip totals to the rupee.
- **AC-ACC-2:** Token expiry triggers a silent refresh; a hard auth failure raises an
  actionable reconnect prompt, never a lost journal.
- **AC-ACC-3:** A post to a locked accounting period opens an exception with the target
  period surfaced, never a silent drop or a mis-dated re-post.

### 16.7 HRIS migration and importers

**[Verified/Hypothesis, Draft 1 §18]** — **Migration is a first-class product surface, not
a services task.** Implementation friction is the most-cited churn trigger in the market,
and mid-year cutover is where it concentrates. Importers from Zoho Payroll, Kredily and
Frappe are **acquisition infrastructure, not integrations** — budget them as such.
(This carries Draft 1's [Hypothesis] status — the churn-driver claim is not yet validated;
kill/validate criterion: §20 buyer interviews. If implementation friction is not a
top-three churn trigger in field interviews, migration is still worth building but is not
the primary GTM wedge.)

**The mid-year cutover problem** is the hard part, because a company switching in (say)
August must carry forward: opening balances, YTD earnings and TDS already deducted,
previous-employer income, investment declarations mid-cycle, **certificate continuity
across two systems** (one Form 130/16 spanning two payroll systems), EPF UAN and ESI IP
continuity, leave balances, and gratuity accrual (Draft 1 §07).

| Facet | Specification |
| --- | --- |
| **Contract** | One-time import from: **Excel/CSV** (universal), **Zoho Payroll / Kredily / Frappe HR / greytHR** exports (acquisition importers), and Tally (§16.2). Format: guided template + validation. |
| **Data exchange** | Ingest: employee master (with UAN/ESI-IP/PAN/bank), compensation structure and pay heads, **YTD earnings + YTD TDS + YTD statutory** (for mid-year), investment declarations and proof status, leave balances and accrual rules, gratuity/PF opening balances, and org structure. |
| **Failure modes** | (1) **YTD not carried** → wrong TDS projection for the rest of the year and a broken annual Form 130. (2) **UAN/IP discontinuity** → duplicate member accounts at EPFO/ESIC. (3) **Pay-head semantics differ** across source systems (what counts as "basic" for add-back). (4) **Declaration state lost** → employees re-declare mid-year. (5) **Silent data loss** on unmapped columns. (6) **Regime carry-forward** — the employee's old/new regime election must carry, or projected TDS inverts. |
| **Fallback** | A **staged migration** with a mandatory **parallel-run / reconciliation month** for mid-year cutovers: the first live run is diffed against the source system's last run and must reconcile before go-live. Unmapped columns are surfaced, never dropped (§08 G9 migration parity). A **YTD import validator** checks that carried-forward TDS + projected TDS is internally consistent, so the first in-product Form 130 is continuous. |

**Worked example — the mid-year TDS continuity check.** An employee joins the new system
in August (month 5 of FY). Source system YTD (Apr–Jul): taxable ₹4,00,000, TDS deducted
₹18,000. On import, the YTD validator recomputes annualised liability on the *full-year*
projection (₹4,00,000 actual + ₹5,00,000 projected Aug–Mar = ₹9,00,000) under the carried
regime election, subtracts the ₹18,000 already deducted, and spreads the balance over the
remaining 8 months. If the import dropped the ₹18,000-already-deducted figure, the engine
would re-deduct it, over-withholding ~₹2,250/month and producing a Form 130 that does not
reconcile to the two systems' combined challans. The validator blocks go-live until
`YTD-carried + YTD-projected` is internally consistent.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- **AC-MIG-1:** A mid-year import produces a first in-product payslip whose YTD figures
  continue the source system's YTD (verified by diff), and a year-end Form 130 that spans
  both systems correctly.
- **AC-MIG-2:** The Zoho/Kredily/Frappe/greytHR importers map ≥90% of fields automatically
  from a real export; the parallel-run reconciles to the rupee before go-live.
- **AC-MIG-3:** No import silently drops a column; every unmapped field is reported.
- **AC-MIG-4:** UAN/ESI-IP carried from the source are validated for continuity so the
  first ECR/ESI file does not create a duplicate member account.
