### 16.8 Recruiting and job-board integrations

**[Verified, Draft 1 §10]** — **A new entrant can build recruiting in India, but inbound
only.** Info Edge owns the passive-candidate graph (Resdex, "over 50 million profiles" per
Naukri's own FAQ) and does not licence database search to third-party ATSs; Resdex-in-ATS
is available only through Info Edge's own ATS (Zwayam markets this as exclusive). Naukri
publishes no developer API, no self-serve key, no partner docs (Source: Naukri/Info Edge —
absence of published developer documentation, corroborated across four vendors, 2026).
**Forbid scraping explicitly** — the only working Resdex extraction piggybacks a live
authenticated session and is legal exposure for us and the customer.

| Facet | Specification |
| --- | --- |
| **Contract** | **Inbound (posting + application sync) only.** Multi-post a requisition to Naukri, LinkedIn, foundit, apna and Indeed against **the customer's own job-board contract** ("bring your own contract"), with application ingest and dedup. **LinkedIn is the one large passive graph with a documented, certifiable partner path** — do it properly and early. |
| **Data exchange** | Outbound: job posting (title, description, location, comp band) to each board on the customer's account. Inbound: applications (candidate profile, resume, source) → dedup → ATS pipeline. No candidate-database *search* against any board (not licensed). |
| **Failure modes** | (1) **No customer contract** on a board → cannot post there. (2) **API/posting-quota limits** per board. (3) **Duplicate candidates** across boards → must dedup on email/phone. (4) **LinkedIn partner-review** gating the integration. (5) **Temptation to scrape** — explicitly architected out and forbidden in sales collateral. |
| **Fallback** | Where a board has no API for a tenant, provide **assisted manual posting** + an email/careers-page application capture (a public application form and an inbound-email parser) so the ATS pipeline is never empty even with zero board integrations. |

> **[Verified] Right-size the moat.** Naukri's "118M" is total resumes (an investor
> metric); Resdex — what recruiters actually buy — is "over 50 million profiles" per
> Naukri's own FAQ (Draft 1 §10). Do not overstate the graph we cannot reach; compete on
> inbound funnel quality, multi-post ergonomics, and the LinkedIn certified path.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- **AC-REC-1:** One requisition multi-posts to every board where the tenant has a contract,
  and ingests + dedups applications back into one pipeline.
- **AC-REC-2:** No code path performs candidate-database search or scraping against any job
  board; this is enforced architecturally and asserted in sales collateral.

### 16.9 Communication channels

Payslip delivery and workflow notifications ride these; e-sign carries the
prescribed-format appointment letter (§06, new since 21 Nov 2025).

| Channel | Contract & use | Failure modes | Fallback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Email (SMTP/API)** | Transactional email (payslips, filing confirmations, approvals) via a provider (SES/SendGrid-class) with per-tenant sender domain (SPF/DKIM/DMARC). | Bounce, spam-foldering, domain not verified. | In-app inbox + downloadable payslip; delivery status tracked. |
| **SMS (DLT-registered)** | OTP and critical alerts via a **TRAI DLT-registered** sender header + pre-approved template (Source: TRAI TCCCPR 2018 — DLT registration of header + content template mandatory). | Template not DLT-approved → blocked/scrubbed; carrier delay; header mismatch. | Email/WhatsApp/in-app fallback for the same alert. |
| **WhatsApp Business (P1)** | Frontline/deskless reach (§09). **[Verified]** A new WhatsApp business portfolio reaches only **250 unique users / rolling 24h** (Source: Meta WhatsApp Business Platform messaging-limit tiers), so a 5,000-worker site cannot be push-onboarded day one; design **worker-initiated**, not employer-push. | Tier limits; template rejection; **[Killed]** the "Meta charges for service messages in India from 1 Oct 2026" claim is false (applies to 9 other markets — §09 [Killed]); **Meta's India rate card is unresolved** (BSP quotes disagree 6.3–7.5×: marketing ₹0.8631 vs ₹0.95, utility ₹0.1150 vs ₹0.15) — download the rate card before committing any per-worker price. | Ramp within the 250/24h tier; fall back to SMS/IVR/email; never gate a payslip on WhatsApp. |
| **E-sign (P1)** | Appointment letters, policy acknowledgements via **Aadhaar eSign (ESP under the IT Act s.3A / CCA)** or a DSC/DocuSign-class provider. | Aadhaar OTP failure; ESP downtime; consent capture; name-in-Aadhaar mismatch. | Downloadable PDF for wet-signature; signature status tracked as an exception until complete. |

**Acceptance criteria.**

- **AC-COM-1:** Payslip delivery is tracked to a per-employee delivery status; a bounce
  opens the in-app copy, never a silent non-delivery.
- **AC-COM-2:** SMS uses only DLT-approved headers + templates; WhatsApp onboarding respects
  the 250/24h new-portfolio cap and degrades to SMS/email.
- **AC-COM-3:** No per-worker WhatsApp price is hard-committed until the Meta India rate
  card is downloaded (§09 [Killed]).

### 16.10 Identity, SSO and provisioning

| Facet | Specification |
| --- | --- |
| **Contract** | Employee/admin login via **Google Workspace and Microsoft Entra ID** (OIDC), enterprise **SAML 2.0** for larger tenants, and **SCIM 2.0** for automated user provisioning/deprovisioning. |
| **Data exchange** | Inbound identity assertions (OIDC/SAML) and user lifecycle events (SCIM create/update/deactivate → HRMS user, but **HRMS remains the system of record for employee master**; SCIM governs *login accounts*, not employment records). |
| **Failure modes** | (1) **IdP mis-mapping** — SSO identity ≠ employee record. (2) **Orphaned accounts** on deprovision failure. (3) **SAML clock-skew / cert-rotation** breaking login. (4) **SCIM loop** if HRMS also pushes to the IdP. |
| **Fallback** | Local password login (with MFA) remains available as a break-glass for admins so an IdP outage never locks out payroll on a due date. Clear precedence: employee master is authoritative; SSO/SCIM never mutates statutory fields (UAN, PAN, bank). |

**Acceptance criteria.** SSO login maps deterministically to an employee/admin record; a
deprovision event disables the login without deleting the employment record (retention, DPDP
§16.12); an IdP outage does not lock out the payroll admin; SCIM never overwrites UAN/PAN/bank.

### 16.11 Public API posture, webhooks and MCP

The platform interface. The strategic frame (Draft 1 §12): **own the data and the
tools the assistant calls, not the assistant itself.**

**REST API.**

| Facet | Specification |
| --- | --- |
| **Contract** | Versioned REST API (`/v1`), OAuth2 client-credentials + scoped API keys per tenant, **ACL-inheriting** (an API caller can never exceed the granting user's permissions). Documented, self-serve keys — consistent with Draft 1's "publish the price card / be evaluable without a demo" posture. |
| **Surface** | Read: employees, attendance, leave, pay-run summaries, filing status, documents. Write: **idempotent, audited, approval-gated** (create employee, submit declaration, initiate approvals). No write endpoint ever emits a statutory figure the engine didn't compute. |
| **Failure modes** | Auth/scoping errors, rate-limit breaches, schema-version drift for consumers, partial writes. |
| **Fallback / guarantees** | Idempotency keys on all writes; `Retry-After` on 429; deprecation policy (N-version support, sunset headers); no breaking change without a version bump. |

**Webhooks.** Event delivery (pay-run locked, filing accepted, disbursement settled,
device offline, filing-due-approaching) with signed payloads (HMAC), at-least-once
delivery, consumer-side idempotency (event id), exponential-backoff retry, and a
dead-letter + replay console.

**Rate limits (P0 even before the public API, per Draft 1 §13 [Verified]).** Per-tenant
**and** per-user limits are P0 because the product is priced per employee but consumed per
user — one heavy user can exceed the ARPU for that seat; even Microsoft hard-disables agents
at 125% of prepaid capacity (Source: Draft 1 §13 [Verified]). Budget, meter, and **degrade
gracefully** (throttle, don't error-storm).

**MCP server (P1 build, P2 GA).** Split three ways per Draft 1 §12:

1. **ACL-inheriting read tools** — the assistant sees only what the calling user may see.
2. **Idempotent, audited, approval-gated write tools** — a write proposes an action into
   the same approval workflow a human uses; it never bypasses segregation of duties (§08 G8).
3. **Per-tenant admin controls** to disable specific tools per assistant — a tenant can
   turn off, say, "initiate disbursement" for any external assistant.

> **[Killed, Draft 1 §12]** — **No revenue forecast may depend on the MCP server.** There is
> no evidence shipping an MCP server has changed a buying decision, and the round-one MCP
> adoption stats are banned (§20). We build it because if enterprise assistants converge on
> Copilot/Glean, we want to be the **governed data-and-tools source**, not because it sells.
> Design it to own the data and the tools; assume we do **not** own the chat surface.

**Acceptance criteria (API/MCP).**

- **AC-API-1:** Every write is idempotent (same key ⇒ one effect) and audited (who/what/when).
- **AC-API-2:** API and MCP callers can never exceed the granting user's ACL; a scope test
  proves an under-privileged token cannot read another user's payslip.
- **AC-API-3:** Per-tenant and per-user rate limits are enforced from v1 and degrade
  gracefully (429 + Retry-After), not with data loss.
- **AC-API-4:** A tenant admin can disable a named MCP write tool for an external assistant,
  and the disablement takes effect without a deploy.
- **AC-API-5:** A webhook consumer that is down receives buffered events on recovery
  (dead-letter replay) with no duplicate side-effects (consumer idempotency on event id).

### 16.12 Cross-cutting: reliability, idempotency, DPDP/CERT-In, residency

The properties every integration above must share. Stated once, enforced everywhere.



**Figure 104. Failure Taxonomy**

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    F["Integration failure<br/>(any of N integrations)"]

    F --> T["TRANSIENT<br/>timeout / 5xx /<br/>portal maintenance"]
    F --> P["PERMANENT<br/>bad data / rejected file /<br/>invalid IFSC / PAN / UAN"]
    F --> PT["PARTIAL<br/>batch settles some lines /<br/>ECR accepts some members"]
    F --> SD["SCHEMA DRIFT<br/>bank release / FVU version /<br/>EPFO layout / PT slab"]
    F --> EU["EXTERNAL UNAVAILABLE<br/>device offline / IdP down /<br/>portal down near due date"]

    T --> Tr["Exponential backoff + jitter,<br/>bounded retries, then queue.<br/>Deadline clock surfaced, not hidden"]
    P --> Pr["Pre-flight validation catches<br/>before emission; if it slips,<br/>opens exception worklist item"]
    PT --> PTr["Line-level status; re-queue only<br/>failures via per-line idempotency key;<br/>parent held in *-with-exceptions"]
    SD --> SDr["Versioned schema object updated<br/>as data; watcher flags change;<br/>old + new versions coexist"]
    EU --> EUr["Fallback path: manual upload /<br/>web check-in / break-glass login.<br/>Primary is never a single point of failure"]

    Tr --> G["Shared guarantee:<br/>no silent failure;<br/>idempotent (a duplicate is worse than a miss);<br/>pay + filing always land"]
    Pr --> G
    PTr --> G
    SDr --> G
    EUr --> G

    classDef fail fill:#fde2e2,stroke:#c0392b,color:#000;
    classDef resp fill:#e2f0fd,stroke:#2471a3,color:#000;
    classDef goal fill:#e2fde8,stroke:#1e8449,color:#000;
    class T,P,PT,SD,EU fail;
    class Tr,Pr,PTr,SDr,EUr resp;
    class G goal;
```


**Failure taxonomy and response (applies to all N integrations).**

| Failure class | Response |
| --- | --- |
| **Transient** (timeout, 5xx, portal maintenance) | Exponential backoff with jitter, bounded retries, then queue for later — the deadline clock is surfaced, not hidden. |
| **Permanent** (bad data, rejected file, invalid IFSC/PAN/UAN) | Pre-flight validation catches it before emission; if it slips through, it opens an **exception worklist** item — never a silent failure. |
| **Partial** (batch settles some lines, ECR accepts some members) | Line-level status; re-queue only the failures with a per-line idempotency key; the parent object stays in a `*-with-exceptions` state until cleared. |
| **Schema drift** (bank release, FVU version, EPFO layout, PT slab) | Versioned schema object updated as data; the watcher (below) flags the change; old and new versions coexist for in-flight periods. |
| **External unavailable** (device offline, IdP down, portal down near due date) | Fallback path (manual upload / web check-in / break-glass login); the primary is never a single point of failure for pay or filing. |

**Idempotency is universal.** Every outbound artefact — bank batch line, GL journal, ECR
member row, webhook event — carries a **deterministic external key** so re-sends update
rather than duplicate. This is the single most important reliability property: in a
statutory/money system, a duplicate is worse than a miss.

| Artefact | Idempotency key |
| --- | --- |
| Bank NEFT line | `payrun_id + employee_id` |
| Tally / GL journal | `payrun_id` (voucher external key) |
| ECR member row | `payrun_period + UAN` |
| Device punch | `serial + device_user_id + timestamp` |
| Webhook event | `event_id` (consumer-side dedup) |
| API write | client-supplied `Idempotency-Key` header |

**DPDP 2023 on integrations.**

- **[Verified, Draft 1 §17]** DPDP s.7(i): employers need no employee consent to process
  employee data *for employment purposes* — this removes the consent-UX friction a
  GDPR-bound product carries. But **onward transfer to a sub-processor** (a BSP for
  WhatsApp, a payout aggregator, an e-sign ESP, an AI provider) still requires a **data
  processing agreement and a maintained sub-processor register** with purpose limitation
  (Source: DPDP Act 2023, and standard data-fiduciary obligations).
- **Data minimisation at the boundary:** each integration sends only the fields it needs
  (a job board does not need bank/UAN; a device ingest does not need PAN). Enforced as a
  per-integration allowed-field allowlist, not a convention.
- **Retention & deletion** propagate to integrations: a deprovisioned/erased employee's
  data must be removable from downstream caches subject to the **five-year statutory
  retention** on registers and filings (retention wins where the law requires it — §14).

**CERT-In on integrations (binds from day one, not at enterprise scale — Draft 1 §17
[Verified]).**

- **6-hour incident reporting** for every body corporate — an integration breach (e.g. a
  leaked bank-API credential) is reportable within 6 hours; name a **CERT-In point of
  contact before the first paying customer** (Source: CERT-In Directions, 28 Apr 2022).
- **180 days of ICT logs retained within Indian jurisdiction** — integration call logs,
  file-transfer logs, and webhook delivery logs are in scope.
- **Clock sync to NIC/NPL NTP** — the same NTP requirement that fixes device clock-drift
  (§16.4) is a CERT-In obligation; one control, two problems.
- **Attacks on AI/ML systems are an explicitly reportable class** (item (xx) of twenty) —
  the MCP/AI integration surface *enlarges* the reportable perimeter; log and monitor it
  accordingly.

**Residency and provider abstraction (segment-specific gate — Draft 1 §17 [Verified]).**

- For **regulated buyers**, RBI Outsourcing-of-IT Directions impose data localisation,
  RBI's right-to-audit, sub-contracting consent and exit obligations on any SaaS vendor —
  **no turnover threshold.** SBI's RFP requires all data functions within India; IRDAI
  mandates records in Indian data centres (Source: Draft 1 §17 [Verified]). Every
  integration touching a regulated tenant must keep data-at-rest and processing in India
  and be exit-able.
- **At least three interchangeable backends with residency selectable per tenant** — this
  is the same abstraction the AI model-router needs for cost (§13), so it is one piece
  of work serving two constraints. Residency is a **per-provider matrix**, and data-at-rest
  residency ≠ in-country inference — track both per provider (Draft 1 §13: OpenAI offers
  India data-at-rest + Bedrock in-country inference; Anthropic offers neither; Vertex has an
  India region — re-verify per provider, do not rely on Sarvam hosting until verified).

**The statutory-change watcher (integration-facing).** Every file-schema integration
(§16.5, bank formats, PT/LWF slabs) subscribes to the watcher. **[Verified, Draft 1 §02]**
It must **catch amendments and corrigenda, not only new instruments** — the Nov-2026
inversion was a corrigendum, and a new-notifications-only watcher would have missed it.
Each hit routes to the owning schema object with its gazette source (URL + date) for a
review-and-version step before any period is filed against it. The watcher is not just a
product feature; per Draft 1 §05 it is the operating-model consequence — the company is a
**compliance-maintenance operation with a permanent statutory team**, and the watcher is its
tooling.

Mapped to the module sequencing (§05.5). Only what a beachhead tenant (20–200, §05) needs
to run its first correct filing is P0; the platform surface follows. This phasing honours
the scope discipline of Draft 1: all three segments are the *vision*, but v1 ships the
beachhead — the register above is deliberately not all P0.



**Figure 105. Integration Phasing Timeline**

```mermaid
timeline
    title Integration phasing (SS16.13) mapped to module sequencing (SS05.5)
    section P0 - first correct filing + first correct payslip
        Filing path (unit of delivery) : EPFO ECR : ESIC contribution : TRACES Form 138 + Form 130 : PT top states MH KA TN TG WB GJ AP
        Pay path : Bank salary file top ~8 banks + generic template + reconciliation : ADMS device-push receiver
        Onboarding + infra : Tally import wedge + GL export : Migration importers Excel Zoho Kredily Frappe greytHR : Email + DLT-SMS : Per-tenant + per-user rate limits
    section P1 - reach, breadth, platform
        Device + state breadth : Device pull-path SDK + third-party connectors : Remaining-state PT + LWF
        Accounting + comms : Accounting APIs Zoho Books QuickBooks ERP GL : WhatsApp Business : e-sign Aadhaar
        Platform open : Public REST API + webhooks : SSO SAML SCIM : Payout aggregator RazorpayX Cashfree : Host-to-host bank APIs : Recruiting job-board posting LinkedIn certified first
    section P2 - assistant-era surface (after SS20 validation reports)
        Assistant + deferred : MCP server GA read-write-admin split : RPA-assisted portal upload conditional on SS16.5 kill criterion : Deeper ERP connectors : Benefits insurer endorsement APIs data model in v1
```


| Phase | Integrations | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **P0 — first correct filing + first correct payslip** | Tally import (migration wedge) + GL export; bank salary file (top ~8 banks + generic template) with reconciliation; **ADMS device-push receiver**; EPFO ECR; ESIC contribution; TRACES/Form 138 + Form 130; PT for top employment states; migration importers (Excel + Zoho/Kredily/Frappe/greytHR); email + DLT-SMS; per-tenant/per-user rate limits. | These carry the unit of delivery and the pay path. Nothing ships without them. |
| **P1 — reach, breadth, platform** | Device pull-path/SDK + third-party connectors; remaining-state PT + LWF; accounting APIs (Zoho Books/QuickBooks/ERP GL); recruiting job-board posting (LinkedIn certified path first); WhatsApp Business; e-sign; SSO/SAML/SCIM; public REST API + webhooks; payout aggregator (RazorpayX/Cashfree) path; host-to-host bank APIs. | Widen device coverage, state coverage, and open the platform. |
| **P2 — assistant-era surface** | MCP server GA (read/write/admin split); RPA-assisted portal upload (subject to the §16.5 kill criterion); deeper ERP connectors; benefits/insurer endorsement APIs (data model built in v1 per Draft 1 §11, monetisation deferred). | Only after the core filing engine and platform API are proven and the validation programme (§20) has reported. |

**What P0 explicitly excludes (and why that is a decision, not an omission).** LWF (P1 —
low value, semi-annual/annual, small amounts); the public REST API (P1 — internal-first,
rate limits ship P0 as infra); the MCP server (P2 — no revenue may depend on it, §16.11
[Killed]); RPA (P2 and conditional on its kill criterion); benefits endorsement APIs (P2 —
data model only in v1 per Draft 1 §11). Committing these to P0 would dilute the one thing
that must be perfect at launch: the filing lands and the salary credits.

### 16.14 Section acceptance summary — the integration guarantees

Ten guarantees that any integration in this section must satisfy to be called "done."
These are the §16 analogue of the payroll engine's G1–G10 (§08).

| # | Guarantee | Enforced by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **IG1** | **Filing/pay is never single-point-dependent** on an external system — every filing-path and pay-path integration has a working manual/file fallback | §16.2–16.5 fallbacks; §16.12 |
| **IG2** | **Idempotency everywhere** — every outbound artefact (bank line, ECR row, GL journal, webhook, MCP write) has a deterministic external key; re-send never duplicates | §16.3, 16.6, 16.11, 16.12 (key table) |
| **IG3** | **Pre-flight validation** — files are validated against the portal's/bank's known checks before emission; the modal upload outcome is acceptance | AC-BNK-1, AC-GOV-1 |
| **IG4** | **Acknowledgement, not submission, is the completion state** — a filing/disbursement stays pending until the ack/settlement is captured | AC-GOV-2, AC-BNK-3, §04/§08 G5 |
| **IG5** | **Schema-driven, versioned, gazette-sourced** — every file format is data with a source (URL + date), not code; amendments are data updates | §16.1, AC-GOV-3, §16.12 watcher |
| **IG6** | **Blocked states are honest** — formats that don't exist (Q4 Form 138, Form 130 Part B) and regimes unresolved (post-cliff ESI) render blocked, never guessed | AC-GOV-4, §08 G7 |
| **IG7** | **No model-generated figure crosses a boundary** — the engine computes; the assistant explains, drafts, routes | §07 [Verified], §16.0 |
| **IG8** | **ACL-inheriting, audited, approval-gated writes** — no external caller (API/MCP) exceeds the granting user or bypasses segregation of duties | AC-API-1/2, §16.11 |
| **IG9** | **DPDP/CERT-In at the boundary** — sub-processor register + DPA, data minimisation per integration, 6-hour incident path, 180-day logs in India, NTP sync | §16.12 |
| **IG10** | **Residency selectable per tenant across ≥3 backends** — regulated tenants keep data-at-rest and processing in India, and the vendor is exit-able | §16.12, Draft 1 §17 |

**Bottom line for the integration layer.** In this market the integrations *are* the
product moat that Tally, Kredily and Frappe cannot match — not because our APIs are
cleverer, but because **the government gives no API and we invest in the fallback anyway.**
The device-push receiver (§16.4), the reconciled bank file (§16.3), the schema-perfect
statutory files with captured acknowledgements (§16.5), and the honest blocked states where
a format doesn't yet exist are the concrete expression of Draft 1's thesis: **the filing,
not the payslip, is the unit of delivery — and the integration is judged by whether that
filing lands, not by whether an API returned 200.**


---

## 17. Non-Functional Requirements — Security, DPDP, Scale

This section specifies **how well the system must behave**, not what it does. Every
functional requirement in §07–§16 assumes the guarantees below; several would be
incorrect or non-compliant without them. Two facts from Draft 1 make this section
unusually load-bearing for an India-first HRMS, and they are not restated per-NFR:

- **CERT-In binds from day one, not at enterprise scale (§12, [Verified]).** 6-hour
  incident reporting, 180 days of ICT logs retained *within Indian jurisdiction*, and
  clock sync to NIC/NPL NTP servers are obligations on *every* body corporate — they
  apply to the 20-employee first customer, not only to the 2,000-seat prospect. Days
  of work now; a painful, un-fundable migration later if deferred.
- **ISO 27001:2022 has a seasoning clock (§01, [Verified]).** Indian Bank's June 2026
  RFP requires the certificate to have been *held for at least one year prior to RFP
  publication*. Acquisition takes 3–6 months; the seasoning adds twelve. The
  security NFRs below are therefore written to the ISO 27001 Annex A control set from
  month zero, so the audit at month ~6 certifies a system already built to it — not a
  system retrofitted to pass.

**Numbering.** NFRs are numbered `NFR-<AREA>-###`. Each carries a **phase tag**
(P0 = beachhead launch, 20–200 seg; P1 = expansion 200–2,000; P2 = enterprise /
regulated), a one-line requirement, detail, and a **measurable target** with a
**verification method** (how we prove it in a test, an audit, or a dashboard). A
target with no way to measure it is a wish, not a requirement, and is rejected in review.

**The measurability rule.** Every NFR in this section states a number and the method
that reads that number. "Highly available" is banned; "≥ 99.9% monthly successful-request
ratio measured at the load balancer, excluding declared maintenance windows" is required.

### 17.1 The residency-first architecture premise

One architectural decision sits upstream of nearly every NFR below and cannot be
deferred, per §13 [Verified]: **residency is a per-provider matrix, and data-at-rest
residency is a different guarantee from in-country inference.** Regulated buyers ask
about both, separately. The system is therefore built on a **provider-abstraction
layer** from v1 that lets residency be selected *per tenant*, not per deployment.

| Layer | What must be swappable per tenant | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Data at rest** (Postgres, object store, search index) | Region of the primary and its replicas | RBI Outsourcing Directions, IRDAI records-in-India, SBI RFP "all processing within India" — no turnover threshold (§13 [Verified]) |
| **LLM inference** | Which of ≥3 backends serves each task class, and in which region it runs | Anthropic offers no India data-at-rest and a US-only immutable workspace geo; OpenAI offers India data-at-rest plus Bedrock in-country inference; Vertex has an India region (§13 [Verified]) |
| **Egress / sub-processors** | The list of third parties any tenant's data touches (email, SMS, WhatsApp BSP, e-sign, payment rails) | DPDP sub-processor disclosure; RBI sub-contracting consent |

This is the **same abstraction the model router needs for cost** (§13 [Verified]) — one
piece of engineering serving two constraints (residency and margin). It is P0 because
retrofitting per-tenant region selection into a single-region monolith is a re-platform,
not a feature. **[Verified]**

> **Design note — the residency default.** The India-first thesis makes `region=ap-south`
> (Mumbai) and `region=ap-south-2` (Hyderabad) the defaults; the abstraction exists so a
> regulated tenant can *pin* both data-at-rest and inference to India and receive a
> written attestation, while an SMB tenant inherits the default without a decision.

**Worked example — onboarding a regulated tenant (an NBFC of 900 employees).** The NBFC
is subject to RBI's Outsourcing of IT Services Directions (§13 [Verified]), which impose
localisation, RBI's own right-to-audit, sub-contracting consent and exit obligations *with
no turnover threshold* (Source: RBI Master Direction on Outsourcing of IT Services, Nov
2023). The tenant record is created with `data_residency=india_pinned` and
`inference_residency=india_only`. Consequences that must be automatic, not manual:

1. Primary Postgres, replicas, object store, search index and **all backups** provision in
   `ap-south-1` with DR in `ap-south-2` — never a foreign region (§17.14).
2. The model router marks every task class for this tenant `india_inference_required`, so
   a task whose only capable backend is US-only (e.g., the Anthropic geo, §13 [Verified])
   is **refused with a typed error**, not silently sent abroad (NFR-RES-701).
3. The sub-processor manifest for the tenant is generated and frozen; adding a new
   sub-processor requires a re-consent step and updates the attestation document.
4. The tenant's residency attestation PDF is produced from live config, not hand-authored,
   so it can never drift from what the system actually does — an RBI auditor reconciling
   the attestation against a network-policy dump finds them identical.

The point of the walkthrough: residency is a **property set at tenant creation that
propagates deterministically to every subsystem**, because a regulated buyer's auditor
tests the seams, not the brochure. Retrofitting this after a single-region launch is the
re-platform §17.1 exists to avoid. **[Verified]** (residency obligations); the automation
of the attestation is a design commitment, not a claim about the regulator.



**Figure 107. Residency Provider Matrix**


### 17.2 Security — authentication

**NFR-SEC-101 · Authentication strength** · **P0**
All human logins require a verified factor beyond a password. Admin, payroll-approver
and CA-console roles require phishing-resistant MFA.

| Target | Value | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MFA coverage on privileged roles | 100% of admin / payroll-approver / CA seats; enforced, not opt-in | Access review, quarterly; login without a second factor is impossible by config |
| Supported second factors | TOTP (RFC 6238), WebAuthn/FIDO2 passkeys; SMS OTP **fallback only**, never sole factor | Config audit; SMS-only accounts = 0 for privileged roles |
| Password storage | Argon2id, per-user salt, memory cost ≥ 19 MiB, ≥ 2 iterations (Source: OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet, 2024) | Code review + hash-format inspection in DB |
| Password policy | ≥ 12 chars, screened against a breached-password corpus (HIBP-style k-anonymity), no forced periodic rotation (NIST 800-63B) | Registration test suite |
| Brute-force / credential-stuffing defence | ≥ 5 failed attempts → exponential backoff + CAPTCHA; account lock alert to user | Automated abuse-simulation test |

**NFR-SEC-102 · Employee self-service login for low-literacy / shared-device users** · **P0**
The frontline reality from §09 [Verified] — nine in ten non-users share a household
phone; worker identity ≠ device identity — forces an auth path that does not assume a
personal smartphone with a password manager.

- **Target:** OTP-to-phone login (with the SMS-fallback caveat above treated as
  acceptable for *non-privileged* employee self-service, since the blast radius is one
  employee's own payslip), plus optional employer-issued short PIN bound to a device.
- **Measurable:** median employee login completes in ≤ 20 seconds on a 3G connection
  (measured in synthetic RUM from a throttled device profile); ≤ 2 taps after OTP entry
  to reach the payslip.

**NFR-SEC-103 · Session management** · **P0**

| Target | Value | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Session token | Opaque, server-side revocable; not a long-lived stateless JWT for privileged sessions | Design review |
| Idle timeout | Admin/payroll 30 min; employee self-service 24 h; CA console 30 min | Automated session test |
| Absolute session lifetime | 12 h admin; re-auth for approval of any pay run or filing regardless of session age (step-up) | Test: approving a filed return always prompts re-auth |
| Concurrent-session control | Admin can view and revoke all active sessions of any user in their tenant | Manual + API test |

**NFR-SEC-104 · SSO for expansion and enterprise** · **P1/P2**
SAML 2.0 and OIDC SSO with SCIM 2.0 provisioning. SCIM de-provisioning propagates a
disabled/terminated employee to *loss of all access* within **≤ 5 minutes** (measured
end-to-end in a provisioning test). This is a hard enterprise-procurement gate, not a
nicety, and the seasoning-clock logic applies: build the interface early even before a
customer asks.

---

### 17.3 Security — authorization

**NFR-SEC-201 · Tenant isolation** · **P0**
The single most important security property of a multi-tenant payroll system: **no
tenant can ever read or write another tenant's data**, and this must be enforced at the
data layer, not only in application code.

| Target | Value | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Isolation mechanism | Row-level security (Postgres RLS) keyed on `tenant_id`, enforced in the database; application `tenant_id` scoping is defence-in-depth, not the sole control | Code review + a mandatory automated "cross-tenant read" test in CI that must fail closed |
| Cross-tenant leakage incidents | 0, with a CI gate: every table holding tenant data has an RLS policy or an explicit annotated exemption | CI check counts unguarded tenant tables; build fails if > 0 |
| CA-console cross-client access | A CA sees only clients that have granted access; switching clients re-scopes the session token | Multi-client switch test (§16 CA console) |

**NFR-SEC-202 · Role-based + attribute-based access control** · **P0**
RBAC with a small, auditable set of built-in roles (Employee, Manager, HR-Admin,
Payroll-Admin, Payroll-Approver, Auditor/CA-read-only, Owner) plus ABAC constraints
(department, location, cost-centre). **Separation of duties is enforced:** the user who
*prepares* a pay run or a return cannot be the user who *approves and files* it.

- **Measurable:** maker ≠ checker on every filing and every pay-run approval — a
  self-approval attempt is rejected 100% of the time (automated SoD test).
- **Least privilege:** default new admin role grants **read-only**; write and
  approve are explicit grants. Verified by a periodic "excess privilege" report that
  lists every seat with approve rights.

**NFR-SEC-203 · CA read-only audit access** · **P0**
Per §16, the CA console offers *read-only audit access*. This is a distinct permission
class that can view registers, payslips and filings but can never mutate a monetary
field. Verified: a CA-role write to any payroll figure returns 403 in 100% of attempts.

**NFR-SEC-204 · Sensitive-field access logging** · **P0**
Read access to defined sensitive fields (Aadhaar/masked, bank account, PAN, salary,
health/disability) is itself an audited event, not only writes. See §17.5.

---

### 17.4 Security — encryption

Encryption strength is driven by a **data-classification scheme**, because AES-256 on
everything and application-layer envelope encryption on everything are not the same cost,
and the scheme decides where the expensive control applies. Four classes, each with a
default handling rule:

| Class | Examples | Handling rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Restricted** | Aadhaar, bank account, PAN, health/disability, biometric attendance template | App-layer envelope encryption (per-tenant DEK, KMS master); masked by default; read is an audited event (§17.5); never in logs, never in a URL, never model-input without redaction |
| **Confidential** | Salary, CTC, PF/ESI/TDS figures, appraisal, disciplinary | RLS-scoped, storage-encrypted; write is audited; not exposed to the AI assistant except through approval-gated, ACL-inheriting tools (§12) |
| **Internal** | Org chart, leave balances, attendance summary | RLS-scoped, storage-encrypted |
| **Public** | Statutory form templates, holiday calendar | No special handling |

The classification is a **field-level tag in the data model**, the same tag that drives the
DPDP processing-purpose mapping (§17.6) and the sensitive-field access log (NFR-SEC-204) —
one annotation serving encryption, audit and privacy at once. A field with no classification
tag fails the build (a CI lint counts untagged columns; must be 0).

**NFR-SEC-301 · Encryption in transit** · **P0**

| Target | Value | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TLS floor | TLS 1.2 minimum, TLS 1.3 preferred; TLS 1.0/1.1 disabled | SSL Labs-style scan ≥ grade A; automated in CI |
| HSTS | `max-age ≥ 31536000; includeSubDomains; preload` | Header scan |
| Internal service-to-service | mTLS within the cluster for services carrying tenant data | Service-mesh config audit |
| Device ingest (ADMS/WDMS) | The attendance push receiver (§09 [Verified]) accepts device POSTs over TLS to a tenant-scoped URL; plaintext HTTP ingest is refused | Ingest endpoint test |

> **Device-ingest caveat, [Hypothesis].** Some legacy eSSL/ZKTeco firmware on the
> reverse-engineered port-4370 path (§09 [Verified]) does not do modern TLS. **Kill/validate:**
> during the hardware spike (§09, device integration currently unsized), measure the share
> of the target install base that cannot POST over TLS 1.2+. If it is material, the answer is
> a tenant-side lightweight relay, never downgrading the cloud endpoint. No plaintext ingest
> ships to the internet regardless.

**NFR-SEC-302 · Encryption at rest** · **P0**

| Target | Value | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Storage-level | AES-256 on all volumes, DB, object store, backups | Provider config attestation |
| Application-level field encryption | Aadhaar, bank account, PAN, and health data encrypted at the application layer with envelope encryption (per-tenant data key wrapped by a KMS master key) so a raw DB dump does not expose them | Code review + DB dump inspection |
| Key management | Managed KMS (India-region), automatic key rotation ≤ 365 days, per-tenant data keys | KMS policy audit |
| Backup encryption | Backups encrypted with keys distinct from primary; restore requires KMS access | Restore drill (§17.14) |

**NFR-SEC-303 · Aadhaar handling** · **P0**
Aadhaar is a special case in Indian data law and in the UIDAI regulations. The system
**does not store the raw 12-digit Aadhaar number** except where a specific statutory flow
requires it (e.g., UAN seeding); where stored it is application-encrypted and displayed
masked (`XXXX XXXX 1234`) by default. Aadhaar is never used as a login identifier or a
primary key. **[Verified]** (UIDAI Aadhaar (Data Security) Regulations 2016; masking is a
published UIDAI requirement.)

- **Measurable:** 0 endpoints return an unmasked Aadhaar to any role below a named,
  audited privilege; unmasking is itself a logged, reason-coded event.

**NFR-SEC-304 · Secrets and key material** · **P0**
No secret (DB credential, KMS key, provider API key, BSP token) in source, in an image
layer, or in an environment file committed to a repo. Secrets live in a managed secrets
store with rotation. Verified by a secret-scanning gate in CI (build fails on a detected
secret) plus a quarterly rotation attestation.

**NFR-SEC-305 · Secure SDLC, dependency & supply-chain security** · **P0**
The ISO 27001 Annex A control set and the VAPT expectation of regulated procurement (§17.15)
are not runtime toggles — they are earned in the pipeline. This NFR makes the pipeline itself
a control surface, because a payroll system that ships a known-vulnerable dependency into a
statutory filing path is one CVE away from a CERT-In-reportable incident.

| Target | Value | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dependency vulnerability gate | No `Critical`/`High` CVE in a shipped dependency without a logged, time-boxed exception | SCA scan (e.g., dependency audit) in CI; build fails on ungated High+ |
| SBOM | A software bill of materials generated per release | SBOM artefact exists per build tag |
| Static analysis | SAST on every PR; security-relevant findings block merge | CI gate |
| Change control on statutory paths | Any change to the payroll-compute or filing-generation code requires maker≠checker review (mirrors the runtime SoD, NFR-SEC-202) | Branch-protection config; 0 self-merged statutory-path PRs |
| VAPT cadence | Third-party penetration test before first customer, then annually and on major release (§17.15) | VAPT report on file; findings tracked to closure |
| AI-specific review | Prompt-injection and tool-abuse test cases in the release suite for any change to an approval-gated MCP write tool (§12) | Test suite present; ties to NFR-OBS-1105 |

> **Why change-control on statutory paths is a hard gate, not process theatre.** The payroll
> engine's determinism invariant (§08 I4) and the audit trail's completeness (NFR-SEC-401)
> are only trustworthy if the code that computes a statutory figure cannot change without a
> second reviewer. A single unreviewed commit that alters a PT slab lookup can silently
> mis-file for every multi-state tenant in that state — the maker≠checker rule that governs
> runtime approvals therefore governs the source that produces them.



**Figure 108. Encryption Key Hierarchy**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    KMS["Managed KMS — India region (ap-south)<br/>Master Key / KEK<br/>auto-rotation &le; 365 days · KMS policy audit"]

    KMS -->|"wraps (envelope encryption)"| DEK_A["Per-tenant DEK<br/>tenant t_00912"]
    KMS -->|"wraps"| DEK_B["Per-tenant DEK<br/>tenant t_00875"]
    KMS -.->|"distinct key, never primary's"| BKP["Backup / DR Key<br/>restore requires KMS access<br/>(NFR-SEC-302, §17.14)"]
```

### 17.5 Security — audit trail

**NFR-SEC-401 · Immutable audit log** · **P0**
Per the payroll engine invariant I5 (§08) and the four statutory registers'
five-year retention (§06 [Verified]), every mutation of a monetary or
statutory field, every access to a sensitive field, every login/logout, every
permission change, and every filing action is recorded as an **append-only,
tamper-evident** event.

| Target | Value | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fields per event | actor, tenant, timestamp (UTC + IST), source IP, action, entity, before-value, after-value, rule-version applied, authority/approval reference | Schema review |
| Immutability | Append-only store; no application path can UPDATE or DELETE an audit row; tamper-evidence via hash-chaining (each event carries a hash of the prior event) | Attempt-to-mutate test returns error; chain-verification job |
| Retention | ≥ 5 years for statutory-register-linked events (matches register retention); ≥ 180 days for ICT/system logs (CERT-In floor, §17.6) — whichever is longer per event class | Retention-policy audit |
| Clock accuracy | Timestamps sourced from NIC/NPL-synced NTP (§17.6); skew ≤ 100 ms | NTP monitoring |
| Completeness | 0 monetary mutations without a corresponding audit event — enforced by writing the audit event in the same DB transaction as the mutation | Transactional test; orphan-mutation detector = 0 |

> **Worked example — a PF recompute under the 50% add-back (§06 [Verified]).** A tenant
> corrects an employee's HRA mid-year; the excluded-components share now exceeds one-half of
> remuneration, so the Code on Wages s.2(y) / Code on Social Security s.2(88) add-back
> re-bases PF for prior periods (§06 [Verified]). The arrears recompute (§08 I3) writes, in
> the *same transaction* as the monetary change, an audit event:
>
> ```
> event_id      : 0x9f3c… (sha256 of this event's canonical form + prev_hash)
> prev_hash     : 0x71ab…            actor: payroll_admin:emp_4471
> tenant        : t_00912             ts: 2026-07-14T09:22:07Z / 14:52:07 IST
> action        : PAYROLL.RECOMPUTE   entity: pf_contribution:emp_88/2026-04
> before_value  : { pf_wages: 18000, ee_pf: 2160 }
> after_value   : { pf_wages: 24500, ee_pf: 2940 }
> rule_version  : wagedef@2026-05-08  approval_ref: run_approval:ra_5521
> ```
>
> Three properties the schema forces and QA verifies: (1) `rule_version` names the
> effective-dated wage-definition rule *in force for the period being corrected*, not
> today's (§06), so the recompute is reproducible; (2) `prev_hash` chains the event, so a
> tampered or deleted row breaks the chain and the nightly verification job flags it; (3) the
> event cannot exist without the mutation and the mutation cannot commit without the event
> (single transaction) — which is how "0 un-audited monetary mutations" is guaranteed rather
> than hoped for.

**NFR-SEC-402 · Audit log usability** · **P0**
An audit trail nobody can query is a liability, not a control. Admins and CA-auditors
can filter the log by employee, period, actor, and action, and export a signed
statement for a dispute or an inspection. **Target:** any single employee's full
change history for a financial year returns in ≤ 3 seconds (P95).

**NFR-SEC-403 · Access review** · **P1**
Quarterly access-recertification workflow: owners attest to each privileged grant;
un-attested grants past 90 days are flagged. Verified by a recertification-coverage
report ≥ 95% each quarter.

---

### 17.6 DPDP Act 2023 and CERT-In obligations

This is where an India-first HRMS diverges sharply from a GDPR-shaped product, in both
directions: DPDP is *easier* on employee-data consent and *harder* on breach-clock and
localisation-of-logs.

**Why the controls in this section are sized the way they are — the penalty schedule.**
DPDP is not a soft-touch regime. The Schedule to the DPDP Act 2023 sets financial penalties
per breach, imposed by the Data Protection Board, that dwarf a beachhead tenant's annual
contract:

| Failure | Penalty ceiling (per DPDP Act 2023 Schedule) |
| --- | --- |
| Failure to take reasonable security safeguards to prevent a breach | up to **₹250 crore** |
| Failure to notify the Board / affected principals of a breach | up to **₹200 crore** |
| Breach of Significant Data Fiduciary obligations (DPO/DPIA/audit) | up to **₹150 crore** |
| Breach of general obligations / children's-data duties | up to **₹200 crore** |

(Source: DPDP Act 2023, the Schedule referenced by s.33.) Two consequences for this PRD:
the **security-safeguards** penalty is the largest, which is why NFR-SEC-201/301/302/305 are
all P0 and gated in CI rather than aspirational; and because the fiduciary carrying the
penalty is the *employer* (data fiduciary), not the processor by default, the product is a
**risk-transfer instrument for the buyer** — a concrete part of the filing-first value
thesis (§04), not a compliance checkbox. The exact quantum and the Board's enforcement
posture depend on notified DPDP Rules; treat the ceilings as the order of magnitude the
architecture must respect, not as a settled tariff. **[Verified]** (Act text) / the Rules'
operational detail is **[Hypothesis]** — see NFR-DPDP-503/505.

**NFR-DPDP-501 · Employee-data processing basis** · **P0**
Per §12 [Verified]: **DPDP s.7(i) lets an employer process employee personal data for
employment purposes without the employee's consent.** The product uses the "legitimate
use / employment" basis for core HR and payroll, which removes the consent-UX friction a
GDPR-bound product carries — a genuine structural advantage for building AI-first in India.

- **Measurable:** core payroll/HR flows require **0** consent gates for employment-purpose
  processing; consent is captured only where processing exceeds the employment purpose
  (e.g., voluntary wellness programme, optional benefits marketing, or a family-member's
  data collected for insurance dependants).
- **[Verified]** — but with a bounded scope: s.7(i) covers *employment* purposes.
  Dependant data (§11 benefits), ex-employee retention beyond statutory minimums, and
  any secondary use fall **outside** s.7(i) and need a lawful basis of their own. The data
  model tags each field with its processing purpose so the system can prove which basis
  applies.

**NFR-DPDP-502 · Data-principal rights** · **P0/P1**
DPDP grants access, correction, erasure, and grievance-redressal rights. For an
employee (the data principal), the system provides:

| Right | Target | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Access / portability | Employee downloads their own record (profile, payslips, filings, declarations) as a machine-readable export | Self-service export test; completes ≤ 60 s |
| Correction | Employee raises a correction request routed to HR-Admin; tracked to closure | Workflow test |
| Erasure, bounded by statute | Erasure honoured **except** where retention is legally required — payroll/PF/ESI/TDS records carry statutory retention (e.g., 5-year register retention; TDS record retention). The system erases what it may and documents the statutory hold on the rest | Erasure test shows retained classes with a cited hold reason |
| Grievance officer | A named DPDP grievance contact is configured per deployment; SLA to first response published | Config check |

> **Erasure vs. retention is a real tension, not a checkbox.** A terminated employee's
> right to erasure collides with the employer's duty to retain PF/ESI/TDS records and to be
> able to reproduce a filed return under inspection. The design rule: **erase discretionary
> data, retain statutorily-mandated data with a documented hold, and never let an erasure
> request silently break a filing's reproducibility.** The hold periods are enumerated in
> NFR-DPDP-506.

**NFR-DPDP-503 · Consent Manager & notice** · **P1**
Where consent *is* required (see 501), capture it with a clear notice, itemised purpose,
withdrawal path, and an audit record of consent version and timestamp. DPDP contemplates
Consent Managers; the architecture leaves an integration seam but does not depend on the
ecosystem being mature at launch. **[Hypothesis]** — the operational shape of DPDP
Consent Managers is not yet settled by notified rules as of the research date; **kill/validate:**
re-check the DPDP Rules for the Consent Manager registration regime before building the
integration, and do not ship a dependency on it until the rule is notified.

**NFR-DPDP-504 · Data Protection Officer / Significant Data Fiduciary** · **P2**
If classified a Significant Data Fiduciary (turnover/volume thresholds to be set by
notified rules), additional obligations attach (DPO, DPIA, audit). **[Hypothesis]** —
the SDF thresholds are not yet notified; the design keeps a DPIA template and a DPO-role
seam ready so classification, if it comes, is a process step, not a re-architecture.
**Kill/validate:** watch the DPDP Rules for the SDF designation criteria (volume of data,
turnover, risk to sovereignty/electoral integrity); do not incur DPO/DPIA operating cost
until either the platform crosses a notified threshold or a specific tenant's contract
requires it — but never let the *seam* be closed, since re-opening it is the expensive part.
(Source: DPDP Act 2023 s.10 on SDFs; thresholds pending notified Rules.)

**NFR-DPDP-505 · Breach notification** · **P0**
DPDP requires notifying the Data Protection Board and affected data principals of a
personal-data breach. This runs *in parallel* with the CERT-In clock below, on a
different timeline and to a different authority. The incident runbook (§17.14) fires
both. **[Hypothesis]** — the precise DPDP breach-notification timeline is set by notified
rules; **validate** against the DPDP Rules and treat the stricter of DPDP-vs-CERT-In as
the binding clock until confirmed.

**NFR-DPDP-506 · Statutory data-retention schedule (the erasure exceptions, enumerated)** · **P0**
An erasure engine that cannot cite *why* it retained a record is a liability under both DPDP
(which requires the retention to be lawful) and inspection (which requires the record to
exist). The system carries a machine-readable retention schedule keyed per data class, so an
erasure request produces an itemised "erased / retained-with-reason" statement automatically.

| Data class | Minimum retention | Statutory basis (source cue) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PF records, contribution cards (Form 3A/6A), returns | 3 years after settlement, per EPFO scheme rules; align to longer register duty | EPF Scheme 1952 / **Employees' Provident Funds Scheme 2026** (§06 [Verified], S.O. 3582(E)) |
| ESI records / contribution registers | ≥ 5 years | ESI (General) Regulations 1950 (**[Hypothesis]** — confirm exact clause; ESI regime unresolved to 22 Nov 2026, §06) |
| TDS records, challans, quarterly returns (**Form 138**, ex-24Q) | ≥ 7 years typical for income-tax records | Income-tax record-keeping practice; **Form 138 replaces 24Q** (§06 [Verified]) |
| Form 130 (ex-Form 16) issued certificates | ≥ 7 years | Follows TDS record practice (§06 [Verified]) |
| Four consolidated statutory registers (electronic) | **5 years** | Notified Rules under the four Labour Codes (§06 [Verified]) |
| Gratuity records / nomination (Form F) | Through employment + limitation period on claims | Payment of Gratuity Act 1972 (**[Hypothesis]** — confirm limitation window) |
| Wage/muster/OT registers | 5 years (register duty) | Notified Rules under the Codes (§06 [Verified]) |
| Appointment letter, wage slip (prescribed format, new since 21 Nov 2025) | Through employment + register-linked period | Code on Wages Rules (§06 [Verified]) |
| Discretionary data (wellness, optional-benefit marketing, non-mandated survey) | **No statutory hold — erase on request** | DPDP s.7/erasure right (§12 [Verified]) |

- **Measurable:** an erasure request on a terminated employee returns a statement listing
  every retained class with its cited hold and expiry date, and erases everything with no
  hold, within the DPDP response window; a retained-with-reason class that has *no* cited
  basis is a build-fail (the schedule must be complete).
- **Reproducibility guard:** erasing discretionary data must never break the ability to
  regenerate a filed return for a retained period (ties to NFR-SEC-401 rule-versioning).
- The three **[Hypothesis]** rows carry a shared **kill/validate:** confirm each retention
  period against the current scheme rule/regulation text (checking for a corrigendum, per
  the Draft-1 standing rule) before the erasure engine treats it as authoritative; until
  confirmed, retain the longer of the candidate periods.



**Figure 109. Erasure Vs Retention Decision**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    REQ["DPDP s.7 erasure request<br/>(terminated employee)"] --> LOOP{"For each field, keyed by its<br/>data-class + processing-purpose tag"}

    LOOP --> UNTAGGED{"Field carries a<br/>retention-class tag?"}
    UNTAGGED -->|No| BF1["BUILD-FAIL<br/>untagged column<br/>(CI lint must be 0)"]
    UNTAGGED -->|Yes| HOLD{"Statutory retention<br/>hold applies?"}

    HOLD -->|"No hold<br/>(discretionary)"| DISC["Discretionary data:<br/>wellness, opt-benefit marketing,<br/>non-mandated survey"]
    DISC --> GUARD{"Reproducibility guard:<br/>does erasing this break<br/>regen of a filed return?<br/>(ties to NFR-SEC-401 rule-versioning)"}
    GUARD -->|No| ERASE["ERASE within DPDP window"]
    GUARD -->|Yes| BLOCK["Do not silently break filing:<br/>retain the reproducibility-linked<br/>fields, erase the rest"]

    HOLD -->|"Hold exists"| CITE{"Cited statutory<br/>basis present?"}
    CITE -->|No| BF2["BUILD-FAIL<br/>retained-with-reason but<br/>no cited basis"]
    CITE -->|"Yes, [Verified]"| RETAIN["RETAIN with documented hold:<br/>class + cited basis + expiry date"]
    CITE -->|"Yes, [Hypothesis]"| HYP["Retain LONGER of candidate<br/>periods until scheme text confirmed<br/>(kill/validate: re-check for corrigendum)"]
    HYP --> RETAIN

    RETAIN --> CLASSES["Held classes & minimums:<br/>PF / Form 3A-6A - 3 yrs post-settlement (EPFS 2026)<br/>ESI registers - >=5 yrs [Hypothesis]<br/>TDS / Form 138 challans-returns - >=7 yrs<br/>Form 130 certificates - >=7 yrs<br/>4 consolidated registers - 5 yrs<br/>Wage / muster / OT registers - 5 yrs<br/>Gratuity / Form F - employment + limitation [Hypothesis]<br/>Appointment letter / wage slip - employment + register period"]

    ERASE --> STMT["Itemised statement:<br/>erased list + retained-with-cited-reason list<br/>+ expiry dates, produced automatically"]
    BLOCK --> STMT
    CLASSES --> STMT
```


#### CERT-In directions (2022) — binding from the first customer

**NFR-CERT-601 · 6-hour incident reporting** · **P0**
Per §12 [Verified]: CERT-In requires reporting of specified cyber incidents **within 6
hours** of noticing them, for every body corporate. The AI/ML-attack class is explicitly
reportable (item (xx) of twenty) — and an AI-first product *enlarges* the reportable
surface, so this is not a formality. (Source: CERT-In Directions under s.70B(6), IT Act,
28 April 2022.)

| Target | Value | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Detection-to-report capability | The runbook and on-call can produce a CERT-In-format report within the 6-hour window | Tabletop drill measures elapsed time; must be ≤ 6 h |
| CERT-In point of contact | Named **before the first paying customer** (§12 [Verified]) | Onboarding checklist gate |
| Reportable-class coverage | Runbook enumerates all 20 classes incl. AI/ML-system attacks; each maps to a detection signal | Runbook review |

The reportable classes most likely to fire for an AI-first payroll SaaS, and the detection
each maps to (a subset of the twenty in the CERT-In Annexure; Source: CERT-In Directions
under s.70B(6), IT Act, 28 April 2022):

- **Unauthorised access to data / data breach / data leak** → tenant-isolation alerts
  (NFR-SEC-201), surprise-egress detector (NFR-RES-703), sensitive-field access anomalies.
- **Identity theft, phishing, credential compromise** → brute-force/stuffing signals
  (NFR-SEC-101), impossible-travel and anomalous privileged-login detection.
- **Attacks on servers, databases, applications (incl. SQLi)** → WAF + SAST/DAST signals.
- **Attacks on IoT devices** → anomalies on the ADMS/WDMS attendance-ingest endpoint (§09),
  which is the one internet-facing device surface in the product.
- **Attacks or malicious activity affecting *systems related to AI and Machine Learning*
  (item xx of twenty)** → prompt-injection, tool-abuse and anomalous assistant tool-call
  detection (NFR-OBS-1105). An AI-first product *enlarges* this surface, so it is a first-
  class detection, not a formality.

> **Worked dual-clock timeline — a prompt-injection escalation.** T+0: NFR-OBS-1105 raises a
> tool-abuse alert (an assistant tool-call attempts a payroll mutation outside its ACL). T+8
> min: on-call acknowledges (MTTA ≤ 5 min target, NFR-OBS-1104), triages, confirms the
> approval-gate held and no monetary field changed (§08 — model never calculates). T+45 min:
> scope assessed — was any Restricted-class data (§17.4) exposed? Two clocks now run from the
> *moment of awareness*: **(a) CERT-In 6-hour** report to the empanelled channel regardless
> of whether data leaked (an attack on the AI system is itself reportable); **(b) DPDP** Board
> + affected-principal notice *only if* personal data was breached, on the DPDP timeline
> (NFR-DPDP-505). The runbook fires whichever clocks apply and, per NFR-DPDP-505, treats the
> **stricter** as binding until the DPDP Rules settle the exact window. Tabletop drills
> (NFR-CERT-601, NFR-DR-1405) measure elapsed time against 6 hours.

**NFR-CERT-602 · 180-day log retention within Indian jurisdiction** · **P0**
Per §12 [Verified]: ICT system logs retained for a **rolling 180 days** and stored
**within Indian jurisdiction**. This is a residency requirement on *logs*, not only on
primary data — a common miss. (Source: CERT-In Directions, 28 April 2022.)

- **Measurable:** log store region = India, verified in provider config; retention window
  ≥ 180 days verified by querying the oldest available log; a log-shipping path that
  egresses to a non-India region is a build-fail.

**NFR-CERT-603 · Time synchronisation to NIC/NPL** · **P0**
Per §12 [Verified]: all systems sync clocks to **NIC or NPL NTP servers** (or servers
traceable to them). Skew tolerance ≤ 100 ms; monitored, alerts on drift. This underpins
the audit-trail timestamp integrity in §17.5. (Source: CERT-In Directions, 28 April 2022.)

**NFR-CERT-604 · KYC & logs for the assistant** · **P1**
CERT-In's log and KYC expectations extend to any user-facing service. The AI assistant's
tool-calls (§12, MCP write tools are approval-gated and audited) are logged with the same
fidelity as human actions, so an AI-initiated change is as reportable and as reconstructable
as a human one.



**Figure 110. Incident Dual Clock**

```mermaid

    ACK["T+8 min · On-call ACK<br/>MTTA target &le; 5 min (NFR-OBS-1104)<br/>Triage: approval-gate held, no monetary field changed (&sect;08)"]
    SCOPE{"T+45 min · Scope assessed<br/>Was any Restricted-class data<br/>(&sect;17.4: Aadhaar, bank, PAN, salary)<br/>exposed?"}
```

### 17.7 Data residency & provider abstraction

Extends §17.1 into measurable NFRs. Per §13 [Verified], residency is a *segment-specific
procurement gate*, not a general differentiator — so the requirement is **selectable
guarantees**, sized to who is buying.

**NFR-RES-701 · Per-tenant residency pinning** · **P0 (capability) / P1 (regulated attestation)**

| Target | Value | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Data-at-rest region control | A tenant can be pinned to India (Mumbai + Hyderabad DR); the default is India | Deploy a tenant with `region=india`; confirm no data object lands outside India |
| In-country inference control | A regulated tenant's task classes route only to backends with India-region inference; a task with no India-region backend is *refused*, not silently sent abroad | Router test: a pinned tenant + a US-only model = task blocked with a clear error |
| Sub-processor transparency | Per-tenant list of every third party its data touches, with region and purpose | Generated report; matches actual egress (verified against network policy) |
| Written attestation | Regulated tenants receive a residency attestation document (data-at-rest India + inference region stated per task class) | Document exists and is accurate for a pinned tenant |

**NFR-RES-702 · Three interchangeable inference backends** · **P0**
Per §13 [Verified]: **at least three interchangeable LLM backends**, re-pointable
per task class *without a deploy*. This single requirement serves cost (router), residency
(pin), and resilience (failover) — three constraints, one build.

- **Measurable:** re-pointing a task class from backend A to backend B is a config change
  applied in ≤ 60 seconds with no service restart; a synthetic "provider down" test fails
  over to a second backend within the task's latency budget.
- **Correctness guardrail (§13 [Verified]):** no statutory or monetary figure is ever
  model-generated regardless of backend, so a backend swap can never change a payroll
  number — only the phrasing of an explanation. Verified by the deterministic-replay test
  (§08 I4): the same pay run produces byte-identical monetary output irrespective of which
  model explained it.

**NFR-RES-703 · Data-egress control** · **P0**
Default-deny egress: tenant data leaves the India perimeter only through an
allow-listed, per-tenant-configured sub-processor. Verified by a network-policy audit and
a "surprise egress" detector (any outbound destination not on the allow-list raises an
alert). This is also a CERT-In and RBI-audit artefact.



**Figure 111. Provider Abstraction Layer**

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph TENANT["Per-tenant residency policy (set at tenant creation, NFR-RES-701)"]
        POL["data_residency=india_pinned<br/>inference_residency=india_only<br/>(SMB default: region=ap-south, no decision)"]
    end

    POL --> PAL

    subgraph PAL["Provider-Abstraction Layer (P0, v1) - one build, three constraints"]
        direction TB
        NOTE["Selectable per tenant, not per deployment<br/>Residency pin + cost router + failover"]
        DATA["Layer 1 - Data at rest<br/>Postgres / object store / search index + all backups"]
        INFER["Layer 2 - LLM inference<br/>Router re-points task class per backend, no deploy, &le; 60s"]
        EGRESS["Layer 3 - Egress / sub-processors<br/>email, SMS, WhatsApp BSP, e-sign, payment rails"]
    end

    DATA --> D1["Primary + replicas pinned to ap-south-1 (Mumbai)<br/>DR in ap-south-2 (Hyderabad) - never foreign (§17.14)"]

    INFER --> ROUTE{"Task class needs<br/>India-region inference?"}
    ROUTE -->|"india_inference_required"| BOK["Route to India-capable backend"]
    ROUTE -->|"only capable backend is US-only"| REFUSE["REFUSED with typed error<br/>never silently sent abroad (NFR-RES-701)"]

    BOK --> B2["OpenAI - India data-at-rest + Bedrock in-country"]
    BOK --> B3["Vertex - India region"]
    REFUSE -.blocked.-> B1["Anthropic - US-only geo,<br/>no India data-at-rest"]

    B1 --> DET["Correctness guardrail (NFR-RES-702):<br/>no statutory/monetary figure is model-generated;<br/>backend swap changes only phrasing -<br/>byte-identical pay-run output (§08 I4)"]
    B2 --> DET
    B3 --> DET

    EGRESS --> DENY{"Destination on<br/>per-tenant allow-list?"}
    DENY -->|yes| ALLOW["Allowed sub-processor<br/>region + purpose logged"]
    DENY -->|no| ALERT["Default-deny + surprise-egress detector<br/>raises alert (NFR-RES-703)<br/>CERT-In / RBI-audit artefact"]

    D1 --> ATTEST["Residency attestation PDF<br/>generated from live config, never hand-authored -<br/>reconciles to network-policy dump (§17.1)"]
    DET --> ATTEST
    ALLOW --> ATTEST
```

### 17.8 Availability & SLAs

Availability targets are **phased**, because a 20-employee beachhead customer and a
regulated 2,000-seat account do not buy the same guarantee, and over-promising uptime at
launch burns money the ARPU (§18, ~₹52–126 PEPM realised) cannot fund.

**NFR-AVAIL-801 · Uptime targets by phase** · **P0/P1/P2**

| Phase / segment | Monthly uptime SLA | Error budget (monthly) | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P0 — 20–200 beachhead | **99.9%** ("three nines") | ~43 min | Successful-request ratio at the load balancer, excluding declared maintenance |
| P1 — 200–2,000 expansion | **99.9%** with published status page + RCA on every SLA breach | ~43 min | Same, plus external synthetic monitoring from ≥ 2 Indian regions |
| P2 — regulated / enterprise | **99.95%** contractual, with financial service credits | ~22 min | Contractual, third-party-verifiable monitoring; SBI/IRDAI-style right-to-audit |

> **Why not 99.99% at launch, [Hypothesis].** Four-nines (~4.3 min/month) needs multi-AZ
> active-active plus a mature on-call, which the beachhead ARPU cannot fund and the
> beachhead buyer does not contractually require. **Kill/validate:** if beachhead churn
> interviews (§20) show uptime is a top-3 loss reason at 99.9%, raise the target; until then
> spend the reliability budget on *correctness of filings*, which is the actual unit of
> value (§04).

**NFR-AVAIL-802 · Filing-window availability is the hard SLA** · **P0**
Generic uptime matters less than availability *during statutory deadlines*. The system
treats the days around the **7th (TDS), 15th (PF ECR / ESI), and state-PT due dates** as
**peak-critical windows** with a stricter internal target of **99.95%** and a freeze on
non-emergency deploys. A missed filing because the platform was down is an existential
failure, not an SLA line item.

- **Measurable:** during declared statutory windows, availability ≥ 99.95% and
  change-freeze compliance = 100% (no non-emergency deploy in the window).

**NFR-AVAIL-803 · Graceful degradation** · **P0**
Per §13 [Verified] (rate limits P0; degrade gracefully): under load or partial outage,
the system **sheds the AI assistant and non-critical features first, and protects the
deterministic payroll/filing path last.** A tenant hitting a rate limit gets a queued,
explained response — never a wrong number and never a dropped filing.

- **Measurable:** in a load test at 3× peak, the payroll-compute and filing-submit paths
  maintain their latency SLA while the assistant is throttled; 0 payroll transactions lost.

**NFR-AVAIL-804 · Maintenance windows** · **P0**
Planned maintenance is scheduled in low-usage IST windows (published ≥ 48 h ahead),
never inside a statutory filing window, and excluded from the SLA denominator only if
declared. Verified against the deploy calendar vs. the statutory calendar (§06).

---

### 17.9 Scale targets

Scale is anchored on the government denominator, not an analyst projection. Per §04
[Verified]: **96.2 mean contributing employees per establishment**; the beachhead is
20–200; greytHR's 34,000 customers ≈ 4.4% of 7.66 lakh contributing establishments is the
realistic ceiling on share. So the scale targets below are *deliberately* modest at P0 and
headroom-tested at P2, rather than vanity numbers.

**NFR-SCALE-901 · Tenant & headcount targets by phase** · **P0/P1/P2**

| Dimension | P0 target | P1 target | P2 headroom (must not architect out) | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Active tenants | 1,000 | 10,000 | 50,000 | Load test at target tenant count |
| Employees / tenant (typical) | up to 200 | up to 2,000 | up to 30,000 (SBI RFP floor, §01) | Single-tenant scale test |
| Total employees on platform | ~100,000 | ~1,000,000 | ~10,000,000 | Aggregate load test |
| Concurrent users at month-end peak | 5,000 | 50,000 | 200,000 | Peak-simulation test |
| Devices (attendance ingest) | 10,000 terminals | 100,000 | 500,000 | Ingest-throughput test |

**NFR-SCALE-902 · The month-end concurrency spike is the real scaling problem** · **P0**
Payroll load is not uniform — it spikes hard around pay-run day and filing deadlines
(the 7th/15th). The architecture is sized for the **peak-to-average ratio**, not the
average. **[Hypothesis]** — assume a peak of **≈ 10×** average daily load in the
25th–7th window; **validate** with production telemetry after the first three month-ends
and re-size. A system sized for the mean will fall over exactly when the customer needs
it most.

**NFR-SCALE-903 · Multi-state, effective-dated data at scale** · **P0**
Per the risk register (§20 [Verified]) — uneven state-rule notification under the four
Codes — the data model assumes **per-state, effective-dated rules** as the norm, not the
exception. A single tenant may span 15+ states' PT and 14+ states' LWF (§05 Frappe
parity). Scale target: a pay run for a 200-employee tenant spanning 10 states completes
within the batch SLA (§17.10) with correct per-state slabs applied.

**NFR-SCALE-904 · Recruiting cost meters separately from headcount** · **P1**
Per §13 [Verified]: recruiting cost does not track headcount (a 15%/month-hiring tenant is
15× the cost of a 3% one on identical PEPM). The scale model meters recruiting load
(requisitions, candidate volume, AI screening calls) on its own axis so a hiring-heavy
tenant does not degrade a hiring-light tenant's service. Verified by per-tenant, per-axis
resource metering (§17.11).



**Figure 112. Month End Load Profile**

```mermaid
graph LR
  classDef base fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#2e7d32,color:#1b5e20;
  classDef ramp fill:#fff8e1,stroke:#f9a825,color:#e65100;
  classDef peak fill:#ffebee,stroke:#c62828,color:#b71c1c;
```

### 17.10 Performance

**NFR-PERF-1001 · Interactive latency** · **P0**

| Interaction | Target (P95) | Target (P99) | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Page/API interactive response | ≤ 500 ms | ≤ 1.5 s | RUM + synthetic, measured from Indian networks |
| Employee payslip view | ≤ 800 ms on 3G-throttled profile | ≤ 2 s | Throttled synthetic (frontline reality, §09) |
| Audit-history query (1 employee, 1 FY) | ≤ 3 s | ≤ 5 s | Query benchmark |
| Assistant first-token | ≤ 2 s | ≤ 4 s | AI-path telemetry; independent of payroll SLA |

**NFR-PERF-1002 · Batch / pay-run throughput** · **P0**

| Batch job | Target | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pay run, 200 employees, multi-state | ≤ 60 s end-to-end (compute → payslips → register update) | Batch benchmark |
| Pay run, 2,000 employees | ≤ 5 min | Batch benchmark (P1) |
| ECR / ESI / PT / Form 138 file generation | ≤ 30 s per return for a 200-employee tenant | File-gen benchmark |
| Retro / arrears recompute (§08 I3) | Recompute against period-version rules ≤ 2× the cost of a fresh run | Recompute benchmark |

**NFR-PERF-1003 · Front-end weight for low-bandwidth India** · **P0**
The self-service surface must work on entry-level Android over 3G. **Target:** initial
JS/CSS payload ≤ 200 KB gzipped for the employee app; Largest Contentful Paint ≤ 2.5 s on
a Moto-G-class device on 3G (measured in Lighthouse CI, gated in the build). This is a
first-class requirement, not polish, because the deskless worker (§09) is the user.

**NFR-PERF-1004 · AI cost-per-interaction budget** · **P0**
Per §13 [Verified]: model choice *is* the margin. Each task class carries a **per-task
cost ceiling**; a call that would exceed it is routed to a cheaper backend or degraded.
The 52.7× cheapest-to-dearest spread (§13 [Verified]) is the lever. **Target:** median
inference cost per assistant interaction stays inside the per-task ceiling set by the
router; breaches are logged and alert. Absolute PEPM figures are placeholders pending
prototype instrumentation (§13, §20) — the *ratio* discipline is the requirement, the
absolute number is not yet evidence. **[Hypothesis]** — **kill/validate:** instrument real
tokens-per-query against a real HR policy corpus (§20); if measured inference cost per
employee-month lands ≥ 5× the ₹0.15–3.27 estimate (§13), the "AI free / bundled" premise
compresses at the low end and PERF-1004's per-task ceilings tighten or a task class is
dropped to a cheaper model tier.

### 17.11 Observability

**NFR-OBS-1101 · Cost & usage attribution from v1** · **P0**
Per §13 [Verified]: build full **token, cache and cost attribution per tenant, user,
agent and model from v1, while the price of AI is still zero** — retrofitting attribution
after pricing exists is far harder. This is the single most strategically important
observability requirement, because it is what lets AI be run as cost-of-goods (§13) and
what lets recruiting be metered separately (§17.9).

| Target | Value | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Attribution granularity | Every inference call tagged with tenant, user, agent, model, task-class, input/output tokens, cache state, INR cost at booked FX | Query the ledger for any dimension; totals reconcile to the provider invoice ± 2% |
| FX in the ledger | Costs booked at ₹94.43/USD baseline with FX sensitivity at ₹90/95/100 (§13 [Verified]); the ₹83.3 figure is banned (§02) | Ledger config audit |
| Per-tenant / per-user rate limits | Enforced (§13 [Verified], P0); one heavy user cannot exceed the tenant's budget; hard-degrade at a defined % of prepaid capacity | Abuse test: a runaway user is throttled, not billed through the roof |

**NFR-OBS-1102 · The three pillars** · **P0**

| Pillar | Target | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Metrics | RED (rate/errors/duration) per service + business metrics (filings-on-time, pay-runs-completed) | Dashboard exists; alerts wired |
| Logs | Structured, correlation-ID-linked, 180-day India-resident retention (§17.6) | Log-store audit |
| Traces | Distributed tracing across the request path incl. assistant tool-calls | Trace sampling verified |

**NFR-OBS-1103 · The headline business SLI is "filings on time"** · **P0**
Per §04 [Verified]: the filing, not the payslip, is the unit of delivery. So the
top-line operational dashboard is not CPU — it is **% of due filings generated and
accepted on time, per tenant, per statute.** **Target:** ≥ 99% of due filings completed
before the statutory deadline across the tenant base; any tenant trending toward a miss
raises an alert to CS **before** the deadline, not after.

**NFR-OBS-1104 · Alerting & on-call** · **P0**
SLO-based alerting (error-budget burn-rate), not threshold spam. On-call rota with a
runbook per alert. Statutory-window alerts (§17.8) page immediately. **Target:** ≥ 95% of
pages are actionable (post-incident review tracks false-page rate); mean time to
acknowledge ≤ 5 min for P0 alerts.

**NFR-OBS-1105 · AI-attack detection feeds the CERT-In clock** · **P0**
Because AI/ML-system attacks are a reportable class (§17.6, §12 [Verified]), the
observability stack has explicit detections for prompt-injection, tool-abuse, and
anomalous assistant tool-call patterns, wired to the incident runbook. **Target:** a
simulated tool-abuse event is detected and raised to the incident channel within the
window that keeps the 6-hour CERT-In report achievable.
